findings.title: A plain MEMBER can shrink a filed declaration by deleting a line after it is frozen READY — record_declaration_filed sums what is left and never compares it to the declaration's own frozen completeness_report
findings.boundary: MEMBER (lowest role that can edit shipment lines) -> the immutable filed_snapshot, i.e. the org's own compliance record and the regulator that receives its total. No privilege escalation and no product bypass: this is `removeLine` used exactly as designed.
findings.precondition: Membership in an org holding IMPORTER_DECLARANT, role MEMBER (not ADMIN, not OWNER). A declaration already marked READY over a member shipment that has more than one calculated line. The window is between 'mark ready' and 'record filed' — in practice days or weeks, since the declarant leaves to file at the official registry in between (master plan section 22: Snowkap does not file).
findings.affected_actor: Own tenant, and through it the regulator. The org's own filed CBAM total is understated by whatever the deleted lines carried. It is not cross-tenant.
findings.exploit:
1. ADMIN marks the ANNUAL 2026 declaration READY. markDeclarationReady recomputes and freezes member_shipment_ids=[shipment A] and completeness_report={complete:true, line_count:2}. Shipment A holds line 1 (100 t -> 139 tCO2e) and line 2 (10000 t -> 13900 tCO2e). True total 14039.
2. A plain MEMBER opens shipment A — still READY, therefore still editable by design — and deletes line 2. Application path: removeLine (src/application/shipments/manage-lines.ts:616), which gates ONLY on hasCapability(context,'IMPORTER_DECLARANT') and has no hasAdminAccess check. Database path: shipment_lines_delete_parent_not_terminal, whose USING excludes only LOCKED and VOID parents. calculation_results_line_id_fkey ON DELETE CASCADE takes the 13900 calculation with it.
3. The ADMIN returns and clicks 'record filed'.
4. record_declaration_filed returns OK. v_line_count=1, v_uncalculated_count=0, v_empty_member_count=0 (the shipment still has one line, so the per-shipment emptiness check does not fire). The snapshot freezes 139.
findings.evidence:
Sandbox: postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/p14_review_sandbox, all inside begin/rollback.

  -- ADMIN freezes READY exactly as markDeclarationReady would
  set local role authenticated;
  set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","role":"authenticated"}';
  update declarations set status='READY',
    member_shipment_ids=array['aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000010'::uuid],
    completeness_report='{"complete":true,"blockers":[],"line_count":2,"shipment_count":1,...}'::jsonb
  where id='aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000040';
  -- UPDATE 1

           t             | frozen_line_count
  -------------------------+-------------------
   READY: frozen report says |                 2

           t         |  sum
  -------------------+-------
   TRUE period total | 14039

  -- PLAIN MEMBER (role MEMBER, distinct user) deletes the large line
  set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","role":"authenticated"}';
  delete from shipment_lines where id='aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000023';
  -- DELETE 1
   MEMBER deleted line; lines left | 1

  -- ADMIN files
  set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000002",...}';
  select * from record_declaration_filed('aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000040','REF-T12');
    t   | result_status |        result_declaration_id
  ------+---------------+--------------------------------------
   FILE | OK            | aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000040

                  t                |                                  totals                                   | report_said
  ---------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------
   FILED SNAPSHOT vs FROZEN REPORT | {"line_count": 1, "shipment_count": 1, "embedded_emissions_tco2e": "139"} | 2

14039 -> 139, a 99.0% understatement. Note the last row: the declaration's own frozen completeness_report says 2 lines and its own filed_snapshot says 1, in the same row, and nothing compares them.

File evidence: src/application/shipments/manage-lines.ts:616-627 (removeLine, capability check only, no admin gate); supabase/migrations/20260903110000_..., function body — the aggregation CTE derives member_lines from live shipment_lines and never reads v_decl.completeness_report (the identifier appears nowhere in the function).
findings.why_controls_fail:
Four controls should have caught this and each misses by a definable margin.
(1) buildCompletenessReport ran at READY, before the delete. It is a point-in-time gate, correctly.
(2) The filing-time re-check in record_declaration_filed is the control designed for exactly this window — its own comment says 'a line can be added, re-determined, or DELETED entirely AFTER the completeness gate passed and BEFORE anyone clicks record filed'. But it only asks, of the lines that EXIST NOW, whether each has a current calculation. A deleted line has no row to fail the check. Absence is invisible to a per-row test.
(3) v_empty_member_count was added (20260829350000) for a delete case, and its comment claims the per-shipment shape fixes deletes generally. It does not: it fires only when a member shipment reaches ZERO lines. Delete one of two and every counter is happy. This is the specific place where the migration comment overstates what the code does.
(4) completeness_report is persisted on the row and frozen for exactly this purpose, and the RPC never looks at it. `v_line_count` is computed and compared only against 0.
findings.impact: An immutably archived, legally meaningful CBAM filed_snapshot understated by up to ~100%, with a fully consistent audit trail behind it (a legitimate shipment_line.deleted event, then a legitimate declaration.filed event) and a self-contradicting row that no code path reads. Reachable by the lowest-privileged role in the product with no bypass, no forged payload, and no unusual action. Once filed, the only remedy is an amendment, which nothing prompts because nothing detects the drift.
findings.recommendation: In record_declaration_filed, before building the snapshot, refuse unless the aggregation agrees with the facts frozen at READY. Concretely: compare v_line_count against (v_decl.completeness_report->>'line_count')::bigint and cardinality(v_member_ids) against (v_decl.completeness_report->>'shipment_count')::bigint, and return a new result_status (e.g. 'MEMBERSHIP_DRIFTED') on any mismatch, folded into the same refuse-and-stop path INCOMPLETE uses. This costs one comparison on a path that already runs, needs no second implementation of any regulatory semantics, and is exactly the shape of the determination and quantity clauses already there. Surface the new status in src/application/declarations/record-declaration-filed.ts's discriminated union with a message telling the declarant to re-run the draft. Longer term, give the declaration a real REOPEN action so a drifted READY declaration has a recovery path other than filing it wrong and amending.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: A shipment added to the reporting period after the declaration reaches READY is permanently and silently excluded from the filed total, with no product path to recover before filing
findings.boundary: Ordinary operations -> the immutable filed_snapshot. Not an attack at all: this is a time-of-check/time-of-use gap between markDeclarationReady and record_declaration_filed that ordinary data entry triggers.
findings.precondition: None beyond normal use. Any member of the org can create a shipment (shipments_insert_own_org requires only org membership). The declaration must be READY and not yet filed. Late-arriving customs data landing after the declarant marks the period ready is the ordinary case, not a contrived one.
findings.affected_actor: Own tenant and the regulator. The org files a total that omits real, fully calculated, in-period shipments it holds and can see.
findings.exploit:
1. ADMIN marks the ANNUAL 2026 declaration READY. member_shipment_ids is frozen to the shipments that existed at that instant.
2. Anyone in the org enters shipment C for the same period (5000 t -> 6950 tCO2e), lines are determined and calculated through the trusted RPC, C is marked READY. Entirely normal product use.
3. ADMIN files. record_declaration_filed reads member_shipment_ids verbatim, never re-derives period membership, and freezes a snapshot covering only the old members.
4. Shipment C is not LOCKed (only members are), so it stays READY, and nothing anywhere compares the period's shipments against the filed declaration's membership.
findings.evidence:
Sandbox, begin/rollback. Steps 1-3 exactly as above:

          t         | real_total
  ------------------+------------
   PERIOD TRUTH NOW |       7089

  select * from record_declaration_filed('aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000040','REF-NORMAL-FLOW');
   result_status |        result_declaration_id
  ---------------+--------------------------------------
   OK            | aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000040

         t        |                                  totals
  ----------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   FILED SNAPSHOT | {"line_count": 1, "shipment_count": 1, "embedded_emissions_tco2e": "139"}

              t             | status
  --------------------------+--------
   ORPHANED SHIPMENT STATUS | READY

7089 -> 139, a 98.0% understatement, no forgery anywhere in the transaction.

No recovery path exists. src/application/declarations/generate-or-refresh-declaration-draft.ts:145-152 returns PERIOD_HAS_READY_DECLARATION for a READY declaration, so the draft cannot be refreshed. A repo-wide grep for a reopen action returns exactly one hit and it is a comment conceding the gap: generate-or-refresh-declaration-draft.ts:40 — 'reopen it to DRAFT (out of this function's scope)'. No such function exists in src/ or app/.

A grep for member_shipment_ids across app/ and src/ (excluding tests) shows it is written by generateOrRefreshDeclarationDraft and markDeclarationReady and, after freezing, read in exactly one place — get-declaration-detail.ts:181 — which fetches only those ids' current status. Nothing reconciles it against the period.
findings.why_controls_fail: markDeclarationReady's doc comment is explicit that it re-runs computeDeclarationDraftFacts rather than trusting a cached report, because 'trusting a stale report here would let this function mark READY a period that has since regressed'. That reasoning is exactly right and stops one instant too early: the report becomes stale again the moment markDeclarationReady returns, and the filing-time re-check the comment defers to (record_declaration_filed) re-derives lines but not membership. The RPC's own comment names 'added' as a case it handles; it handles an added LINE inside an existing member (which becomes INCOMPLETE if uncalculated) and does not handle an added SHIPMENT at all, because member_shipment_ids is the input, not something it recomputes.
findings.impact: A filed CBAM declaration that omits entire in-period shipments, permanently archived, with no signal to the declarant at any point. Because no reopen exists, a declarant who notices before filing has no way to fix it except to file the wrong number and amend. Because nothing detects it, the realistic case is that nobody notices. This is a regulatory-reporting integrity failure reachable through the product's happy path.
findings.recommendation: Re-derive membership inside record_declaration_filed and refuse on drift: select the org's non-VOID shipments matching v_decl.reporting_period_kind/year/quarter, and if that set is not equal to v_member_ids, return a distinct result_status rather than filing. That check lives in SQL, needs no regulatory logic, and is the same shape as the existing gates. Pair it with the completeness_report comparison from Finding 1 and with a REOPEN (READY -> DRAFT) action so the drift has a remedy — the RLS policy already permits that transition (declarations_update_own_org_pre_filing's USING allows READY, its WITH CHECK allows DRAFT), so only the application action is missing.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: member_shipment_ids and completeness_report are client-writable on a DRAFT declaration and the filing RPC binds them to nothing — enabling a forged member set, a cross-period member, the same shipment filed twice, and an amendment that silently lowers the corrected total
findings.boundary: ADMIN/OWNER of an importer org, posting raw PostgREST instead of using the product -> the immutable filed_snapshot. Same threat shape the repository itself classified as a RELEASE BLOCKER in 20260903190000_p141 ('a member of the importing organisation, posting raw PostgREST rather than using the product').
findings.precondition: ADMIN or OWNER of an org holding IMPORTER_DECLARANT, with a valid session, issuing a PATCH to /rest/v1/declarations while the declaration is DRAFT. No forged determination, no forged calculation, no cross-tenant access.
findings.affected_actor: Own tenant and the regulator. Also the integrity of the filing record itself: two of these vectors produce snapshots that are internally false rather than merely incomplete (a member from another reporting period; the same calculation counted in two filings).
findings.exploit:
The one enabling write, common to all four vectors:

  update declarations set status='READY',
    member_shipment_ids = array[<chosen subset>],
    completeness_report = '{"complete":true, ...}'::jsonb
  where id=<draft id>;

declarations_update_own_org_pre_filing permits it (USING: admin_or_owner AND status IN (DRAFT,READY)), and app.prevent_declaration_fact_change() only freezes those two columns when old.status <> 'DRAFT', so from DRAFT they are wide open. Then call record_declaration_filed. Four filings, all returning OK:
(a) OMIT: name one of the period's two shipments -> 278 filed as 139.
(b) CROSS-PERIOD: name a shipment whose reporting_period_year is 2025 in a declaration for ANNUAL 2026 -> filed. The RPC checks org and status only.
(c) DOUBLE-FREEZE: file ANNUAL 2026 with shipment A, then file QUARTERLY 2026 Q1 with the same A. The second passes because record_declaration_filed accepts LOCKED members (intended for amendments) and there is no cross-declaration exclusivity. Both snapshots name the same calculation_result_id.
(d) AMENDMENT SHRINK: file the original with both shipments (278), create the amendment, name only one member -> amendment files 139 and becomes 'the current version of this period'. The dropped shipment stays LOCKED, so it never resurfaces as undeclared.
findings.evidence:
All in sandbox, all inside begin/rollback.

(a) OMIT — org's ANNUAL 2026 truly holds P14REV-A (139) + P14REV-B (139):
   result_status | OK
   totals        | {"line_count": 1, "shipment_count": 1, "embedded_emissions_tco2e": "139"}

(b) CROSS-PERIOD:
                t               |                    decl_period                    |          member_period           |  totals
   -----------------------------+---------------------------------------------------+----------------------------------+----------
    T1 cross-period member file | {"kind": "ANNUAL", "year": 2026, "quarter": null} | [{"y": 2025, "ref": "P14REV-B"}] | ..."139"
   result_status = OK. The snapshot asserts ANNUAL 2026; the shipment it froze is a 2025 shipment.

(c) DOUBLE-FREEZE:
            t          |                  id                  | kind      | qtr | total |                 calc_ids
   --------------------+--------------------------------------+-----------+-----+-------+------------------------------------------
    T10 both snapshots | ...0041                              | QUARTERLY |   1 | 139   | ["aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000030"]
    T10 both snapshots | ...0040                              | ANNUAL    |     | 139   | ["aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000030"]
   Both OK. Identical calculation_result_id in two filed declarations for overlapping periods.

(d) AMENDMENT SHRINK:
    T11 file original (both shipments)        | OK      ->  original total  278
    T11 file amendment (one shipment dropped) | OK      ->  amendment total 139
    T11 shipment B status after amendment     | LOCKED

Policy/trigger evidence:
  pg_policy on public.declarations, declarations_update_own_org_pre_filing:
    USING       (app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of(org_id) AND (status = ANY (ARRAY['DRAFT','READY'])))
    WITH CHECK  (app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of(org_id) AND (status = ANY (ARRAY['DRAFT','READY','VOID'])))
  app.prevent_declaration_fact_change(): `if old.status <> 'DRAFT' and (new.member_shipment_ids is distinct from old.member_shipment_ids ...)` — no guard while DRAFT.
findings.why_controls_fail: markDeclarationReady is the only thing that ever computes a correct member set, and it is application-layer. The database accepts any member set from an ADMIN on a DRAFT row. The filing RPC then applies three checks to that set — org match, READY-or-LOCKED status, and per-line calculation currency — none of which is a binding to the period or to the completeness gate. app.prevent_declaration_fact_change() protects these columns only AFTER DRAFT, which is precisely one state too late, because DRAFT -> READY is the transition that is supposed to make them trustworthy. On (c), the acceptance of LOCKED members is deliberate and documented ('an amendment covers shipments the superseded version already locked') but is not restricted to amendments, so any declaration can freeze an already-filed shipment. On (d), the amendment machinery enforces chain SHAPE (declarations_supersedes_uq, ORIGINAL_NOT_FILED, ALREADY_AMENDED) and nothing about chain CONTENT — nothing requires an amendment to cover at least its predecessor's members.
findings.impact: A filed, immutable CBAM record understated by an arbitrary factor, or internally false (a 2026 filing whose frozen member is a 2025 shipment; one calculation counted in two filings). The amendment variant is the worst of the set: the correction mechanism itself becomes the understatement mechanism, the superseded original still shows the true 278, the current version shows 139, and the dropped shipment stays LOCKED so it reads as 'declared'. I rate this BLOCKER for consistency with the project's own precedent rather than on cross-tenant reach — 20260903190000 and 20260903110000 both treat own-org, raw-PostgREST, self-inflicted understatement as release-blocking, and this is the same class one layer up.
findings.recommendation: Stop trusting member_shipment_ids at filing time. The clean fix subsumes Findings 1 and 2: have record_declaration_filed re-derive the member set from the declaration's own reporting period (org's non-VOID shipments matching kind/year/quarter) and refuse unless it equals v_member_ids. That single check closes (a), (b) and the drift findings at once. Separately: (i) restrict the LOCKED-member allowance to declarations with supersedes_declaration_id IS NOT NULL, and require an amendment's member set to be a superset of its predecessor's — that closes (c) and (d); (ii) extend app.prevent_declaration_fact_change() so member_shipment_ids/completeness_report can only be written by the trusted paths even while DRAFT, or move that write into a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that computes the set itself, which is the pattern 20260903190000 already established for calculation_results and the pattern this table now needs for the same reason.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: `pnpm test:e2e` runs the full mutating Playwright suite against the PRODUCTION Supabase project, with the production service-role key and rate limiting disabled, whenever .env.local is absent
findings.boundary: Developer workstation / test harness -> the live production database and Auth project. The boundary that is supposed to separate a test run from production data does not exist.
findings.precondition: A machine that has .env (filled in per the README) and does not have .env.local. That is precisely the state the README's documented setup produces: README:117 says `cp .env.example .env`, and the README never mentions .env.local at all. Anyone who set up this repo to run `pnpm regulatory:verify` (which CLAUDE.md documents as needing SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD from .env) and then runs the E2E suite is in it.
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant's production data, and the regulator-facing record. The suite creates accounts, organizations, shipments, emission data, declarations and cross-org sharing grants.
findings.exploit:
No attacker required; this is a foot-gun that fires on a documented command.
1. `pnpm test:e2e` -> playwright.config.ts.
2. playwright.config.ts:93-94 builds resolvedEnv by parsing .env.local first, then .env, with first-file-wins semantics.
3. With no .env.local, every key comes from .env — the production project.
4. resolvedEnv is spread into webServer.env (playwright.config.ts), so the spawned server receives production SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and the 219-character production SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.
5. The same env block sets NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS_BUILD="true" and DANGEROUSLY_DISABLE_RATE_LIMITS_FOR_E2E_TESTS="true", so the suite hits production auth and mutation endpoints with every limiter disabled.
6. webServer.command runs `pnpm build && node .next-e2e/standalone/server.js`, then the suite executes. importer-journey, producer-journey, cross-org-sharing-journey, team-invitation-journey and actual-data-determination are all mutating (32, 22, 44, 17 and 48 fill/click operations respectively).
findings.evidence:
playwright.config.ts:93-94
```
parseEnvFileInto(".env.local", resolvedEnv);
parseEnvFileInto(".env", resolvedEnv);
```
with parseEnvFileInto's documented `if (key in into) continue;` first-wins rule.

I re-executed that exact parser against the real files. Exact output:
```
with .env.local present  -> SUPABASE_URL host = 127.0.0.1:54321 | NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL host = 127.0.0.1:54321
with .env.local ABSENT   -> SUPABASE_URL host = tjwzlbujbsnoacbhzmax.supabase.co | NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL host = tjwzlbujbsnoacbhzmax.supabase.co
   service-role key would be passed to the E2E server: YES (len 219)
```

README:115-119 (the only documented env setup):
```
pnpm install
cp .env.example .env
# fill in .env — see the comments in .env.example for what each
# variable is for and where to find it in the Supabase dashboard
```
`grep -n "\.env\.local" README.md` -> no matches.

Mutating spec sizes: `grep -rcE "fill\(|click\(" tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` -> actual-data-determination 48, cross-org-sharing-journey 44, importer-journey 32, producer-journey 22, team-invitation-journey 17.
findings.why_controls_fail: The control that makes CI safe is a CI-only step: .github/workflows/ci.yml:388 ('Write .env.local for the E2E app build (local Supabase)') writes .env.local from `supabase status` before Playwright runs. Nothing in the repository provides that guarantee locally. playwright.config.ts's long doc comment on resolvedEnv is entirely about env-file PRECEDENCE (a P13 fix for the standalone server resolving the wrong file) and never asserts which project it landed on. There is no check that SUPABASE_URL is loopback, no refusal to run when it is not, and no warning printed. The E2E bypass hardening actively makes this worse rather than better: because the harness is designed to build with the rate-limit bypass on, the run hits production with every auth and mutation limiter disabled. The prior passes reasoned about .next-e2e never becoming the deploy artifact — the opposite direction, the test RUN reaching production, was not examined.
findings.impact: A single documented command can write test-fixture organizations, shipments, emission data and filed/amended declarations into the live regulatory database, and create real accounts in the production Auth project — with rate limiting off, so at full speed and volume. In a CBAM context this is contamination of records that back a regulatory filing, and it is not obviously reversible: the suite's writes are indistinguishable in shape from real tenant data. The blast radius is the whole production dataset, and the trigger is a developer running the project's own test command on a correctly-set-up-per-README machine.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed in playwright.config.ts: after resolving env, refuse to start unless the resolved SUPABASE_URL/NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL host is loopback (127.0.0.1/localhost), and throw with an explicit message otherwise. Do not make this overridable by an env var that a shell profile could carry. Separately, stop reading .env as a fallback for the E2E harness at all — require .env.local explicitly and error when it is missing, which also removes the silent-wrong-project failure mode the P13 comment was chasing. Document .env.local in README's setup section alongside .env.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: An ADMIN can mint a never-expiring ADMIN invitation to an outside address, and offboarding that ADMIN does not revoke it — a persistent backdoor into the tenant
findings.boundary: Own-tenant privilege boundary and the organization membership boundary: an ADMIN (a role the product deliberately keeps below OWNER) plants an admission grant that outlives their own removal and admits an identity that was never a member of the organization.
findings.precondition: ADMIN or OWNER of one organization, plus the ability to issue a raw PostgREST/Data-API request as themselves. The anon key is public and inlined in the client bundle by design, and any user can obtain their own access token directly from GoTrue with their own password, so this is a capability every admin already has. No second account, no other tenant, no service-role key.
findings.affected_actor: The victim organization and everyone whose data it holds — including producers whose VERIFIED emissions data is shared into it, since an ADMIN sees everything the organization can see.
findings.exploit: 1. As ADMIN of the victim org, POST one row to organization_invitations with role='ADMIN', email=<attacker-controlled address>, and expires_at='infinity' (or '9999-12-31'). organization_invitations_insert_admin_or_owner constrains only org_id, invited_by and status='PENDING'; expires_at is unconstrained by the policy, has no CHECK constraint, and is INSERT-granted to `authenticated` at column level. 2. Be offboarded: the OWNER deactivates the membership and then hard-deletes it. 3. Any time later — there is no expiry job, and accept_organization_invitation's only time check is `expires_at < now()` — sign in as the invited address and call accept_organization_invitation(). It returns OK and inserts a memberships row at ADMIN.
findings.evidence:
Sandbox p14_review_sandbox, scratchpad/a7_p1.sql and a7_p2.sql.

P1b (as ADMIN a7-admin@victim.test under `set local role authenticated`):

  values ('a7111111-...-000000000001','a7-attacker@evil.test','ADMIN','a7000000-...-000000000003','9999-12-31T00:00:00Z') returning ...;
  -> 24333c3c-dc9b-4824-adf3-13f3253b6879 | a7-attacker@evil.test | ADMIN | PENDING | 9999-12-31 00:00:00+00   (INSERT 0 1)
P1c, same session, also accepted expires_at='infinity', created_at='1999-01-01' and a forged accepted_by:
  -> 006545a2-... | a7-other@victim.test | ADMIN | PENDING | infinity | 1999-01-01 00:00:00+00 | a7000000-...-000000000001

Full chain (a7_p2.sql, all committed):
  STEP1 minted        | a7222222-...-000000000001 | a7-attacker@evil.test | ADMIN | PENDING | infinity
  STEP2 deactivated   | 6f24ba69-... | ADMIN | 2026-09-03 12:40:54.517682+00      (UPDATE 1)
  STEP2 hard-deleted  | 6f24ba69-... | ADMIN                                      (DELETE 1)
  STEP2 invitation still? | a7222222-...-000000000001 | a7-attacker@evil.test | ADMIN | PENDING | infinity | inviter_still_member = 0
  STEP3 attacker can SEE it | a7222222-...-000000000001 | a7111111-...-000000000001 | ADMIN
  STEP3 accept result | OK | a7111111-...-000000000001
  STEP3 membership now | ADMIN | a7-attacker@evil.test | (deactivated_at null)

Schema evidence: supabase/migrations/20260828130000_organization_invitations.sql:142-150 (insert policy — no expires_at term); column default `(now() + '7 days')` with no CHECK (\d output: `expires_at | (now() + '7 days'::interval) | NO`, and pg_constraint lists only email-format, role, status, pkey and two FKs).
findings.why_controls_fail: Three controls look like they cover this and none does. (a) The 7-day expiry is a column DEFAULT, not a constraint — organization_invitations_insert_admin_or_owner never mentions expires_at, and `authenticated` holds a column-level INSERT grant on it (information_schema.column_privileges: INSERT | accepted_at,accepted_by,created_at,email,expires_at,id,invited_by,org_id,role,status). (b) organization_invitations_select_own_email and organizations_select_via_pending_invitation were hardened in 20260829380000 with `expires_at > now()` specifically to stop a lapsed invitation lingering — that clause is satisfied forever by a forged expires_at, so the hardening is inert against the party who chooses the value. (c) accept_organization_invitation re-validates the email, the confirmation status, PENDING and expiry, but never re-validates the INVITER: it does not check that invited_by still has a membership, still holds ADMIN/OWNER, or is not deactivated. Deactivation correctly severs everything else (verified: a deactivated ADMIN reads zero memberships, zero organizations, zero invitations and cannot insert one), which makes this the one authority that survives offboarding. The 20260903130000 `membership.invitation_created` audit event records the act but is a record, not a control.
findings.impact: A departing, disgruntled or compromised administrator leaves behind a permanent, self-service re-entry path at ADMIN role, keyed to an address they control, that survives every offboarding action the product offers. Nothing in the schema or the application ever expires it. Recovery requires an OWNER to notice the row on the Team screen and revoke it — and with expires_at='infinity' that row renders as `expires Invalid Date` (app/team/pending-invitations-list.tsx:125,130 formats it with a Date constructor), which is less conspicuous than a real date. For a CBAM filer this is unauthorised access to the declaration and to producers' shared VERIFIED emissions data, by an identity the organization believes it removed.
findings.recommendation: Stop accepting expires_at from the client. Either revoke the column-level INSERT/UPDATE grant on expires_at from `authenticated`, or add `and expires_at <= now() + interval '7 days'` to organization_invitations_insert_admin_or_owner's WITH CHECK (a CHECK constraint cannot reference now(), so it has to be the policy or a BEFORE-INSERT trigger that overwrites the value). Separately, make acceptance depend on the inviter's continuing standing: in accept_organization_invitation, refuse (a new status, e.g. INVITER_NO_LONGER_AUTHORIZED) when no active ADMIN/OWNER membership exists for invited_by in v_invite.org_id — and cascade-revoke PENDING invitations when a membership is deactivated or deleted.

findings.title: A member can file an engine-produced emissions figure computed under a different good's Annex II treatment: good_sector is not frozen on the row and not re-checked at filing (100x under-report, live-reproduced)
findings.boundary: Authenticated member of an importer/declarant org -> the authoritative persisted calculation result and the immutable filed declaration snapshot. The trusted-write boundary established by 20260903190000 is not crossed; the inputs it binds are simply incomplete.
findings.precondition: A plain MEMBER (not admin/owner) of an org holding IMPORTER_DECLARANT, with a DRAFT or READY shipment, and one ACTIVE+VERIFIED emission_data record whose cn_scope covers both an Annex-II code and a non-Annex-II code. cn_scope has no constraint of any kind on emission_data and app.code_prefix_covers treats entries as prefixes, so a single entry '7' covers all of chapter 72 and '2' all of chapter 25. No admin rights, no service-role key, no forged calculation row.
findings.affected_actor: The regulator and the filing. The importer's own declaration understates embedded emissions by the entire indirect component of every affected line; the filed_snapshot is immutable and internally consistent, and its provenance block names a calculation_results row that reproduces perfectly against its own frozen inputs.
findings.exploit: 1. The line carries an ACTUAL determination built from the shared record. Set cn_code to an IRON_STEEL good (72061000). 2. The trusted server path runs: calculateLine resolves good_sector=IRON_STEEL, the engine applies RULE-EE-004 direct-only, indirect 9.90 is excluded, and record_calculation_result persists embedded_emissions_tco2e='10' for a 100 t line (verified engine output). 3. As the member, UPDATE cn_code to a CEMENT good (25232100) together with a DIFFERENT determination -- only resolved_at changes, which nothing validates. This is needed because app.validate_emission_determination_write() nulls a determination that is unchanged while cn_code changes; supplying a distinct one routes to the validator instead, which passes because cn_scope covers the cement code. 4. As the member, UPDATE emission_determination back to the exact JSON the calculation froze, with cn_code unchanged this time so the auto-null branch does not fire. The validator re-runs under the CEMENT code and accepts it. 5. The line now declares a CEMENT good whose correct engine output is 1000, while the persisted, engine-produced, byte-matching calculation says 10. record_declaration_filed's freshness gate compares determination, quantity and quantity_unit -- never cn_code -- and reports the line as calculated and current.
findings.evidence:
Sandbox p14_review_sandbox, one BEGIN ... ROLLBACK, fixture seeded as superuser and every attack step run as `set local role authenticated` with request.jwt.claims sub=be92879e-73db-41c3-a0b0-5961ea57d1b4 (role MEMBER of org 8eb4367f). Full script at C:\Users\RAHIL~1.NAI\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--projects-snowkap-cbam\0738b301-3787-4c6c-83dd-c747580bc58c\scratchpad\attack.sql. Verbatim output:

  --- FIXTURE READY. sectors: 72061000=IRON_STEEL  25232100=CEMENT
  --- acting as: authenticated uid=be92879e-73db-41c3-a0b0-5961ea57d1b4 role_in_org=MEMBER
  UPDATE 1
  --- STEP A applied. line cn_code=72061000  determination_present=true  resolved_at=2026-09-03T10:00:00.000Z
  --- RPC(record_calculation_result) -> OK id=1f8b184f-c206-448f-af0e-97992431eb3c
  UPDATE 1
  --- STEP B applied. line cn_code=25232100  resolved_at=2026-09-03T10:00:01.000Z
  UPDATE 1
  --- STEP C applied. line cn_code=25232100  resolved_at=2026-09-03T10:00:00.000Z
  === FINAL STATE ===
  line.cn_code                = 25232100   (sector = CEMENT)
  frozen calc embedded_tco2e  = 10   steps say good_sector = IRON_STEEL
  determination byte-identical to the line's current one? true
  record_declaration_filed would count this line as UNCALCULATED? false
  ROLLBACK
  === after rollback: calc rows for line = 0, line cn_code = 72081000, ED2 rows = 0

The UNCALCULATED predicate is copied verbatim from the live prosrc of public.record_declaration_filed (member_line_counts): `c.determination is distinct from ml.emission_determination or c.quantity is distinct from coalesce(ml.net_mass_tonnes, ml.quantity_mwh) or c.quantity_unit is distinct from (case when ml.net_mass_tonnes is not null then 'TONNES' else 'MWH' end)`. cn_code appears nowhere in it.

The two engine outputs, produced by running the real src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts under tsx with direct_specific=0.10, indirect_specific=9.90, quantity=100:
  sector IRON_STEEL -> embedded_emissions_tco2e "10", steps[0].step="ANNEX_II_DIRECT_ONLY", inputs.good_sector="IRON_STEEL", indirect_specific_excluded="9.90"
  sector CEMENT     -> embedded_emissions_tco2e "1000", single LINE_EMBEDDED_EMISSIONS step, no good_sector recorded anywhere
findings.why_controls_fail: supabase/migrations/20260903190000 revokes INSERT and grants the RPC to service_role only, and its three added bindings are determination (byte-identical to the line's), quantity/quantity_unit (the line's own), and actor membership. good_sector is a fourth engine input and is bound by none of them -- it is not even a parameter of record_calculation_result, and calculation_results has no column for it (20260829180000). src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts:116-141 derives it at calculation time from the shipment's current release_date and the line's current cn_code. It is recorded on the row only inside `steps`, and only when the Annex II gate fired -- a row computed with sector CEMENT and one computed with sector null are byte-identical, so the row cannot even say what sector it saw. record_declaration_filed's P13/P14 freshness fixes closed 'redetermined without recalculating' and 'quantity edited' but compare no classification field. app.validate_emission_determination_write() nulls the determination on a cn_code change only while the determination is unchanged, which the two-step restore sidesteps; and the ACTUAL branch of app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record binds the snapshot to the cn_code only through cn_scope prefix coverage, which is unvalidated producer text. reproduceCalculationResult would catch this row (it re-derives sector from the current cn_code and would return MISMATCH), but it is invoked only from a user-triggered Server Action (app/(importer)/shipments/[id]/actions.ts:1247) -- nothing in the calculation, READY or filing path runs it.
findings.impact: An ordinary member can under-report a filed CBAM declaration by the entire indirect-emissions share of any affected line -- 100x in the reproduced case (10 tCO2e filed against a true 1000) -- using only writes RLS is designed to permit, with no forged calculation row, a number the engine genuinely produced, a determination that validates, and a filing gate that reports the line as current. Because 134 of the 170 goods in the ACTIVE dataset are IRON_STEEL or ALUMINIUM, the Annex II exclusion is the single largest lever on the figure. Detection requires a human to open one row's reproduction panel.
findings.recommendation: Freeze the sector decision on the row, and bind it the way determination and quantity are bound. Concretely: add the cn_code (and the cbam_goods dataset/record identity actually consulted) as columns on calculation_results and as parameters of record_calculation_result, with the RPC refusing unless p_cn_code equals the line's current cn_code -- a CN_CODE_MISMATCH alongside DETERMINATION_MISMATCH. Add the same `c.cn_code is distinct from ml.cn_code` clause to record_declaration_filed's uncalculated_count. Make reproduceCalculationResult read the frozen cn_code from the row instead of re-deriving it from the line, which also removes its dependence on release_date and on the live dataset. Record the ANNEX_II step unconditionally (including good_sector=null and non-Annex-II sectors) so every row states what treatment it applied. Also stop populating parameter_datasets with [] for the ACTUAL path: cbam_goods is a regulatory dataset the engine consumed and the row currently names none.

findings.title: The Annex II sector proxy is contradicted by the ACTIVE dataset's own CN-level signal: DEFAULT and ACTUAL file numbers 47-50% apart for the same good, and the code's justifying claim is false
findings.boundary: Regulatory determination boundary — the DEFAULT (RULE-EE-001) and ACTUAL (RULE-EE-009) paths must produce the same treatment for the same good; and the boundary between an authoritative versioned dataset and a hand-written set in application code.
findings.precondition: None beyond normal use. An importer-declarant with any shipment line for CN 26011200 (agglomerated iron ores, sector IRON_STEEL, a TRADE_GOOD in the ACTIVE dataset) who determines it from ACTUAL data rather than the default value.
findings.affected_actor: The regulator and the filing. The declared embedded emissions on an ACTUAL-determined iron-ore line are understated by the whole indirect component — up to 50% of the published total. Also the declarant, who cannot see that the two methods disagree.
findings.exploit: 1. Query the ACTIVE dataset for which declarable goods publish an indirect value at all — this is the dataset's own CN-code-level direct-only signal. 2. Compare it against ANNEX_II_SECTORS = {IRON_STEEL, ALUMINIUM} in src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts:46-52. 3. They disagree on exactly two goods: CN 26011200 (proxy says Annex II, dataset publishes indirect) and CN 28041000 hydrogen (proxy says not Annex II, dataset publishes no indirect). 4. Run the real engine on CN 26011200 with the dataset's own Uzbekistan figures both ways.
findings.evidence:

  CN 26011200 Uzbekistan ACTUAL  sector=IRON_STEEL     | COMPUTED | 390  | ANNEX_II_DIRECT_ONLY,LINE_EMBEDDED_EMISSIONS
  CN 26011200 Kazakhstan ACTUAL  sector=IRON_STEEL     | COMPUTED | 170  | ANNEX_II_DIRECT_ONLY,LINE_EMBEDDED_EMISSIONS

file:line — src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts:46-52 (the proxy), :95-98 (the false claim), :298-331 (the exclusion).
findings.why_controls_fail: The control is the comment at calculate-line-emissions.ts:95-98: 'It does not touch the DEFAULT path. RULE-EE-001 trusts the published dataset's own pre-summed total, which is already Annex-II-correct at source; recomputing there would be the exact violation RULE-EE-004 warns about.' Measured against the dataset, that is false for CN 26011200: total_value = direct_value + indirect_value there (0.740 = 0.390 + 0.350), so the DEFAULT path's number includes indirect for a good the ACTUAL path treats as direct-only. The second control, ANNEX_II_APPLICABILITY_DATASET_REQUIREMENTS.md, disclosed the proxy's imprecision as a hypothetical and asserted at §1 that cbam_goods 'carries no Annex II membership field at all, only this coarser sector' — but the membership signal is not in cbam_goods, it is in default_emission_values.indirect_status, which nobody looked at. So the risk was filed as theoretical when a concrete instance was already live in the ACTIVE dataset. Nothing else checks the two paths against each other: checkCalculationCurrency compares a calculation to its line's determination, never DEFAULT against ACTUAL for the same good.
findings.impact: For any ACTUAL-determined line of CN 26011200, embedded emissions are understated by the indirect share: 47.3% for Uzbekistan (390 vs 740 tCO2e per 1000 t), 50.0% for Kazakhstan and Serbia. The understated figure carries a complete, internally consistent ANNEX_II_DIRECT_ONLY trace step attesting that the exclusion was deliberate, and record_declaration_filed freezes it into an immutable filed snapshot. The hydrogen case runs the other way (14820 vs 10820 tCO2e per 1000 t, +37%). Both are wrong; only one direction is discoverable by the importer as a cost.
findings.recommendation: Do not ship D1 with the sector proxy. Two options, both owner escalations under ADR-0013: (a) revert D1 to the pre-2026-09-03 fail-closed gate, which refused rather than silently excluding — the imprecision then costs a refusal, not a wrong filed number; or (b) build the ANNEX_II_APPLICABILITY dataset the requirements doc already specifies, and treat default_emission_values.indirect_status as the corroborating cross-check rather than a substitute for the primary source. Either way, add a test that asserts DEFAULT and ACTUAL produce the same treatment for the same good — the invariant that would have caught this — and correct the false statement at calculate-line-emissions.ts:95-98 immediately, since it is currently the stated reason no one examined the DEFAULT path.

findings.title: A shipment's filing reporting period is unvalidated client input, so goods can be silently excluded from the declaration that must contain them
findings.boundary: Filing boundary — which shipments belong to a reporting period. Declaration membership is derived exclusively from shipments.reporting_period_kind/year/quarter, which nothing ties to release_date.
findings.precondition: Any authenticated member of the org, posting to PostgREST (or any future/alternate write path). No admin role, no capability, no service_role.
findings.affected_actor: The regulator and the filing. Goods actually released for free circulation in the reporting year are absent from the filed declaration, and the completeness report reports COMPLETE without them.
findings.exploit: 1. INSERT a shipment with release_date 2026-06-01 and reporting_period_year 2031 (or QUARTERLY 2024-Q3). RLS permits it; there is no CHECK and no trigger tying the two. 2. computeDeclarationDraftFacts filters shipments by org_id + reporting_period_kind/year/quarter only (src/application/declarations/compute-declaration-draft-facts.ts:97-134) — the 2026 declaration never sees it. 3. buildCompletenessReport is computed over that filtered set, so it reports no blocker. 4. record_declaration_filed trusts the frozen member_shipment_ids verbatim and never re-derives membership.
findings.why_controls_fail: The only enforcement of the release_date -> period derivation is reportingPeriodForReleaseDate() called in src/application/shipments/create-shipment.ts:92 — an application-layer convention with no database counterpart, on a table whose RLS INSERT policy checks tenancy alone. The database is the trust boundary here, not the Server Action. Separately, even without any forgery, membership is frozen at markDeclarationReady (mark-declaration-ready.ts:171-177) and the filing RPC never re-derives it, so a shipment created for the same period between READY and filing is silently omitted too — and create-shipment.ts has no guard against creating one. The P14.1/P13 hardening work correctly made the filing RPC re-check line-level freshness (a line added or re-determined after the gate) but never asked the same question one level up about shipments.
findings.impact: A CBAM declaration that omits real imports, filed as complete, with the omission archived in an immutable snapshot. Under-reported by whatever those shipments carried — unbounded. The forged-period variant is deliberate evasion; the READY-window variant happens by accident in normal use.
findings.recommendation: Add a database CHECK or BEFORE trigger deriving reporting_period_kind/year/quarter from release_date (or asserting consistency with it), so the derivation cannot be bypassed by any write path. Separately, have record_declaration_filed re-derive the org's non-VOID shipments for the declaration's period and refuse with a MEMBERSHIP_STALE outcome if the set differs from member_shipment_ids — the same 'never trust a DRAFT-time fact at filing time' rule the RPC already applies to line calculations.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: A member can insert a self-verified ACTIVE emission_data row citing a non-existent evidence file, and drive a line's filed emissions to 0.01 tCO2e against a true default of 139
findings.boundary: The ACTUAL-determination evidentiary chain: 'VERIFIED by a verifier, with evidence files' is the entire basis on which an actual figure may replace a published default. The emission_data INSERT policy is the boundary.
findings.precondition: An authenticated member of an importer-declarant org. No sharing grant is needed (the org enters the data for its own installation), no admin role, no service_role.
findings.affected_actor: The regulator and the filing; and the integrity of the actual-vs-default distinction for every org.
findings.exploit: In one transaction as a normal member: 1. INSERT an operator and an installation with provenance IMPORTER_ENTERED. 2. INSERT emission_data with status='ACTIVE', verification_status='VERIFIED', verifier_user_id = self, evidence_file_ids = ['11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111'] (a UUID with no row in evidence_files), cn_scope=['2'] and direct_specific='0.0001'. 3. UPDATE the shipment line's emission_determination to the matching ACTUAL snapshot. The v10 validator accepts it, because every field it checks matches the emission_data row it was told to check against. 4. Press Calculate in the app: record_calculation_result's DETERMINATION_MISMATCH guard passes, because the line genuinely carries that determination.
findings.why_controls_fail: The evidence-existence invariant is enforced in the UPDATE policy's WITH CHECK and nowhere in the INSERT policy's. It therefore polices the DRAFT -> ACTIVE lifecycle the application drives, and not the single INSERT that lands in the terminal state directly. Neither policy constrains status, verification_status, or verifier_user_id at all, so 'verified' is self-assertable in the same statement. The determination validator (app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record) is genuinely thorough — it checks status='ACTIVE', verification_status='VERIFIED', non-empty evidence_file_ids, provenance against the installation, version, unit, both values, and the verifier id — but every one of those is a comparison against the emission_data row, so a fabricated row satisfies all of them. record_calculation_result's DETERMINATION_MISMATCH guard is likewise satisfied, because the forgery happened upstream and the line honestly carries it. This is the same class the P14.1 comment in calculate-line.ts:246-265 describes closing ('reproduced live at 0.001 against a true 139'); revoking INSERT on calculation_results moved the forgery one table upstream rather than eliminating it.
findings.impact: Any importer can file an arbitrarily low CBAM figure for any good, with a fully valid audit trail: a VERIFIED actual-emissions record, an evidence file reference, a real engine calculation, a complete trace. 99.993% under-report in the reproduction. It also destroys the meaning of the actual/default distinction and of owner decision D2's record_provenance field, since the org controls both sides of the attestation.
findings.recommendation: Move the evidence-existence predicate from the UPDATE policy into the INSERT policy (or into a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger so both paths share one implementation). Separately, forbid an INSERT that lands directly in status='ACTIVE' or verification_status='VERIFIED' — those states should be reachable only through the sanctioned lifecycle transitions — and forbid verifier_user_id = the inserting user for an org's own record. Re-run the P14.1 reproduction afterwards to confirm the 0.0001-against-139 path is closed at every table, not just calculation_results.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: A declaration with 197 or more member shipments can never be filed: the filing RPC's own audit payload exceeds the audit payload CHECK and aborts the whole transaction
findings.boundary: Application/UI -> database SECURITY DEFINER RPC transaction (own-tenant; the regulatory filing action itself)
findings.precondition: An ADMIN or OWNER of an IMPORTER_DECLARANT org with a READY declaration whose member_shipment_ids has 197 or more entries. No attacker, no elevated privilege, no unusual input — just an importer with a normal-sized annual declaration clicking "record filed".
findings.affected_actor: The declarant organization, and the regulator/filing itself: the single regulatory action the product exists to record cannot be performed.
findings.exploit: 1. Create a READY declaration with 197+ member shipments (each READY, one line, one current calculation_result — the ordinary state after markDeclarationReady). 2. Call record_declaration_filed(declaration_id, filed_reference). 3. The RPC passes every gate, locks the shipments, writes the filed_snapshot — and then its final `insert into public.audit_events` builds a payload containing the whole member_shipment_ids array. octet_length exceeds 8192, audit_events_payload_size_ck fires, and the entire transaction aborts. Nothing is filed. The same abort is reachable at ANY member count with a long filed_reference (see the separate finding).
findings.evidence:
Boundary established live in p14_review_sandbox with two identical fixtures differing only in shipment count.

196 members — SUCCEEDS:
  psql "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/p14_review_sandbox" -tAc "set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims = '{\"sub\":\"11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111\",\"role\":\"authenticated\"}'; select * from public.record_declaration_filed('55555555-5555-5555-5555-555555555555','EU-CBAM-REF-2026-0001');"
  ->  OK|55555555-5555-5555-5555-555555555555

197 members — FAILS:
  ... select * from public.record_declaration_filed('bbbbbbbb-0000-0000-0000-00000000000b','EU-CBAM-REF-2026-0001');
  ->  ERROR:  new row for relation "audit_events" violates check constraint "audit_events_payload_size_ck"

210 members — FAILS, with the failing statement named:
  ... select * from public.record_declaration_filed('33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333','EU-CBAM-REF-2026-0001');
  ->  ERROR:  new row for relation "audit_events" violates check constraint "audit_events_payload_size_ck"
     DETAIL:  Failing row contains (..., USER, 11111111-..., declaration.filed, DECLARATION, 33333333-..., {"line_count": 210, "filed_reference": "EU-CBAM-REF-2026-0001", ..., null).
     CONTEXT:  SQL statement "with locked as (...) insert into public.audit_events (...) values (..., 'declaration.filed', ..., jsonb_build_object(..., 'member_shipment_ids', to_jsonb(v_member_ids), ...))"
     PL/pgSQL function record_declaration_filed(uuid,text) line 455 at SQL statement

State after the failed 210 attempt (clean abort, action simply impossible):
  select status, filed_at is null from declarations where id='33333333-...';  ->  READY|t
  select status, count(*) from shipments where org_id='22222222-...' group by 1;  ->  READY|210

Payload size as a function of member count (same jsonb_build_object shape, 21-char filed_reference):
  195|8125  196|8165  197|8205  ...  210|8725   (bound is 8192)

Source: supabase/migrations/20260829330000_p9_declarations_schema.sql, record_declaration_filed() final INSERT (prosrc line ~455); bound in supabase/migrations/20260831140000_p13_review_audit_events_payload_bounds.sql.

Sandbox writes that COMMITTED for this reproduction (p14_review_sandbox only): orgs 22222222-…, 44444444-…, 66666666-…, aaaaaaaa-…0a and their users/shipments/lines/calculation_results/declarations; declaration 55555555-… was actually filed. All are p14rev-prefixed fixtures in the disposable database.
findings.why_controls_fail: The two-wall pattern has a hole exactly where it matters. Wall 1 is the MAX_AUDIT_PAYLOAD_BYTES check in src/application/audit/record-audit-event.ts:53-72, which is deliberately kept numerically identical to Wall 2 so the database never surprises anyone — but record_declaration_filed() does not go through recordAuditEvent at all. It writes audit_events directly, in SQL, for the stated and correct reason that the audit row must share the filing transaction (see the migration's own comment at prosrc ~447-453). So the one audit write that is transactionally coupled to a mutation is the one write Wall 1 does not guard, and Wall 2 — a CHECK constraint — cannot degrade gracefully: it aborts. The payload is built from `to_jsonb(v_member_ids)`, whose size is unbounded by construction, and nothing anywhere bounds member_shipment_ids. Every test and every prior audit exercised small declarations, so the threshold was never crossed. `pnpm test` passing is not evidence here: no test files a declaration above single digits.
findings.impact: The product's terminal regulatory action is unavailable above ~196 shipments — precisely for the large declarants who most need it, and at the deadline moment when they discover it. The failure surfaces as `RPC_FAILED` (src/application/declarations/record-declaration-filed.ts:172), a generic reason with no cause attached, and because the application has no logging (separate finding) there is no server-side trace to diagnose it from. Support would see "filing is broken for our biggest customer" with nothing to go on.
findings.recommendation: Stop putting the unbounded array in the audit payload. Record `member_shipment_count` plus a stable digest (e.g. md5 of the sorted id array) in the `declaration.filed` event — the ids are already durably frozen in `declarations.member_shipment_ids` and in `filed_snapshot`, so the audit row does not need to carry a second copy. Apply the same change to `shipment.locked`'s sibling insert if it can grow. Then add a regression test that files a declaration with 1000 members. Do the same for `declaration.marked_ready` (separate finding). Longer term, any audit payload built inside a transaction that must not abort should be size-clamped in SQL before the insert rather than relying on a CHECK that can only abort.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The restore acceptance test reports POSTURE MATCHES on a database where the P14.1 calculation-result trusted-write boundary has been fully reopened and TRUNCATE is reachable by `authenticated`
findings.boundary: Disaster recovery / restore acceptance. `docs/runbooks/BACKUP_RESTORE.md` states 'The acceptance test is no longer a checklist a human reads. It is scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs', and names 'compare-database-posture.mjs returning POSTURE MATCHES' as the outstanding success criterion for the real restore drill.
findings.precondition: A restore or rebuild that returns table privileges to PUBLIC rather than to the named API roles. This is not exotic: `pg_dump` records the grants that exist and never their absence, the hosted Supabase bootstrap does `grant all on all tables in schema public`, and `seed.sql` does the same. Any of those paths, or a manual `grant all ... to public` during a recovery, produces exactly this state.
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant, and the regulator. `calculation_results` feeds the immutable `filed_snapshot` of a filed CBAM declaration; the P14.1 blocker commit a80e94c exists because a member could file an emissions figure the engine never produced.
findings.exploit: 1. Build the candidate schema from migrations + seed. 2. Simulate the restore defect with a single statement: `grant insert, update, delete, truncate on public.calculation_results to public;`. 3. Run the acceptance test. It passes.
findings.evidence:
Sabotage:
  psql p14rev_fresh -c "grant insert, update, delete, truncate on public.calculation_results to public;"
  -> GRANT
  select relacl from pg_class where relname='calculation_results';
  -> {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,anon=rxtm/postgres,authenticated=rxtm/postgres,service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres,=awdD/postgres}

Effective privilege (what actually matters):
  select p, has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.calculation_results',p) from unnest(array['INSERT','UPDATE','DELETE','TRUNCATE','SELECT']) p;
  -> INSERT|t  UPDATE|t  DELETE|t  TRUNCATE|t  SELECT|t

What the comparator's own query sees:
  select grantee||' '||privilege_type from information_schema.role_table_grants where table_schema='public' and table_name='calculation_results' and grantee in ('anon','authenticated');
  -> anon SELECT / anon REFERENCES / anon TRIGGER / authenticated SELECT / authenticated REFERENCES / authenticated TRIGGER
  (the PUBLIC grant is invisible in this view, and the check filters grantee to four named roles at scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:132)

Live exploitation, real transaction:
  begin; set local role authenticated; truncate table public.calculation_results cascade; select 'TRUNCATE SUCCEEDED as authenticated'; rollback;
  -> BEGIN / SET / TRUNCATE TABLE / TRUNCATE SUCCEEDED as authenticated / ROLLBACK

The acceptance test on that database:
  node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs <sandbox> <p14rev_fresh>
  -> [MATCH] effective_grants (566 rows both sides)
  -> [MATCH] function_grants (84 rows both sides)
  -> [OK] truncate_granted_to_api_roles
  -> [OK] tables_without_insert_policy
  (the only [DIFFER] was `schemas`, over two unrelated scratch schemas)
findings.why_controls_fail: `effective_grants` (scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:126-135) and `truncate_granted_to_api_roles` (:401-411) both read `information_schema.role_table_grants` and both filter `grantee in ('anon','authenticated',...)`. A grant to PUBLIC never appears under those grantee names, yet `anon` and `authenticated` inherit it in full — `has_table_privilege` proves it and a live TRUNCATE confirms it. The file's own header says the lesson is 'the exact grant set'; it compares a projection of the grant set that omits the one grantee that implicitly covers every role. `api_roles_hold_their_grants` does not help: it only asserts a non-zero count.
findings.impact: The single control the P14.1 release blocker was closed with — 'the number is made unforgeable rather than checked' — is reopened, and the tool designated to prove a recovery is safe declares that recovery safe. TRUNCATE additionally bypasses RLS entirely, on an append-only compliance record, which is precisely why 20260903170000 revoked it.
findings.recommendation: Compare the raw ACL, not a filtered projection: `select relname, coalesce(relacl::text,'DEFAULT') from pg_class ...` for every table in public/app, and assert absolutely (not just source-vs-target) that no PUBLIC entry grants a, w, d or D on any product table. Add a self-check asserting `not has_table_privilege('authenticated', t, 'INSERT')` for the trusted-write tables by name. Compare `pg_default_acl` too.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The same acceptance test reports MATCH on a database where five fact-immutability and append-only triggers have been DISABLED — proven load-bearing, and the check that claims to cover them cannot see the difference
findings.boundary: Disaster recovery / restore acceptance, and the schema's own integrity walls. The comparator's `triggers` check declares its purpose as 'the fact-immutability and append-only walls in this schema are triggers'.
findings.precondition: Any restore, replication cutover or bulk-load procedure that leaves triggers disabled — `ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER` is standard practice during a large data load and is exactly the kind of step that gets performed during recovery and forgotten. `pg_restore --disable-triggers` produces the same shape.
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant. The disabled set covers audit-event timestamp pinning, declaration fact immutability, emission-data verification gating, organization capability append-only, and shipment-line determination validation.
findings.exploit: 1. `alter table public.organizations disable trigger organizations_capabilities_append_only;` (and four siblings). 2. Remove a capability from an organization — the operation migration 20260903160000 exists to make impossible. 3. Run the acceptance test.
findings.why_controls_fail: The `triggers` check (scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:184-196) selects `pg_get_triggerdef(t.oid)` and never `t.tgenabled`. `pg_get_triggerdef` renders the CREATE TRIGGER statement and is byte-identical whether tgenabled is 'O' (enabled) or 'D' (disabled). So the one column that decides whether the wall is standing is the one column not compared. The check's `why` string names fact-immutability and append-only as its subject, which makes this a vacuous check against its own stated purpose.
findings.impact: A restored production database can have every trigger-based integrity wall in the schema switched off — capability append-only, declaration fact immutability, audit timestamp pinning, emission-data verification gating, determination validation — and the recovery gate says the posture matches. Every one of those walls was added by a named P7-P14 security fix.
findings.recommendation: Add `|| ' | enabled=' || t.tgenabled::text` to the triggers check, and add a self-check that fails outright on any row where `tgenabled <> 'O'` for a non-internal trigger in public/app. One line each; both would have caught this.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: Rolling the application back past the 11 pending migrations breaks two core write paths at the database — the rollback runbook's central assumption ('every migration applied since then was additive') is false for this pending set, and the runbook does not enumerate the exceptions
findings.boundary: Application-rollback / schema-forward boundary. `docs/runbooks/ROLLBACK.md` §2: 'the rollback is safe only when every migration applied since then was additive... This is the expected, common case.'
findings.precondition: The exact procedure the runbook prescribes: promote the 11 pending migrations, deploy, then redeploy the recorded known-good SHA when something goes wrong. No attacker required — this is the documented incident response.
findings.affected_actor: Every importer and producer organization on the platform, during an incident, at the moment recovery is being attempted.
findings.exploit: BREAK 1 — calculation persistence. `20260903190000` does `drop policy if exists calculation_results_insert_own_org_as_self` (line 144) and `revoke insert, update, delete on public.calculation_results from anon, authenticated` (line 147), replacing the write path with a service_role-only RPC introduced in the SAME commit (a80e94c, which also rewrites `src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts`). The rolled-back build still does a direct RLS-scoped insert. BREAK 2 — ACTUAL determinations. `20260903120000` line 298 makes `record_provenance` mandatory in the frozen snapshot; the rolled-back build's snapshot literal does not contain that key.
findings.evidence:
BREAK 1, old code (git show a80e94c^:src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts):
  :238  const { error: insertError } = await supabase.from("calculation_results").insert({...})
  :269  reason: insertError.code === "42501" ? "SHIPMENT_NOT_EDITABLE" : "PERSIST_FAILED"
Live, on the fully-migrated fresh database:
  begin; set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims='{"sub":"1111...","role":"authenticated"}';
  insert into public.calculation_results (org_id,line_id,shipment_id,engine_version,parameter_datasets,quantity,quantity_unit,determination,steps,embedded_emissions_tco2e,calculated_by_user_id) select ... from public.shipment_lines limit 1;
  -> ERROR: permission denied for table calculation_results
     HINT: Grant the required privileges to the current role with: GRANT INSERT ON public.calculation_results TO authenticated;
  (SQLSTATE 42501 -> the old code reports "SHIPMENT_NOT_EDITABLE")

BREAK 2, old snapshot builder (git show 23993d9^:src/application/emissions/determine-from-actual-data.ts:507-529) contains exactly: emission_data_id, emission_data_version, installation_id, resolved_at, values, emission_unit, methodology, verification, evidence_file_ids, sharing_grant_id. No record_provenance.
Live validator verdict, everything else held identical, single transaction, real JWT claims:
  begin;
  set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111","role":"authenticated","email":"u@test.example"}';
  select app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record(<snapshot>, <org>, '72081000', 'IN', null);
  -> PRE-D2  (no record_provenance)  -> false
  -> POST-D2 (record_provenance set) -> true
  rollback;
The trigger that consumes that boolean (app.validate_emission_determination_write, installed by 20260829580000:637) raises `shipment_lines: emission_determination failed validation for line %` with errcode 42501 on false.

Full non-additive inventory of the pending set:
  20260903190000 - DROP POLICY + REVOKE insert/update/delete on calculation_results  [capability removal]
  20260903120000 - snapshot must carry record_provenance; new BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE triggers on operators and installations tying provenance to capability and making it immutable  [tightening]
  20260903160000 - organizations.capabilities append-only trigger  [tightening]
  20260903140000/150000 - emission_data verification downgrade gate trigger  [tightening]
  20260903180000 - DROP CONSTRAINT then ADD a strictly stricter calculation_results_numeric_format_ck  [tightening, non-atomic]
  20260903170000 - REVOKE TRUNCATE + alter default privileges  [privilege removal]
  20260903130000 - DROP POLICY audit_events_insert_own_org_as_self, recreated with a wider catalogue  [drop/recreate]
  20260903100000 - accept_sharing_grant_invitation gains status 'CAPABILITY_NOT_HELD'; the pre-P14 caller's switch has no case for it and falls to `default: return { status: "NOT_FOUND" }` (cad99ad:src/application/sharing/manage-sharing-grants.ts:780) - a legitimate importer is told the invitation does not exist
  20260902150000 - enforce_sharing_grant_insert_shape trigger and sharing_counterparty_org_names replaced
findings.why_controls_fail: ROLLBACK.md does describe the destructive case correctly in prose, and instructs the reader to 'explicitly confirm the target commit's code is still compatible with the current schema'. But it provides no list, no tooling and no gate — and it simultaneously tells the reader this situation 'should be rare' because §42 requires escalation for destructive changes. Neither 20260903190000 nor 20260903120000 is recorded anywhere as a destructive/escalated change; both were shipped as security fixes. The P14 audit's own migration table (docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:534-560) lists all 11 with one-line descriptions and never classifies any as non-additive. An operator following the runbook during an incident has nothing that would stop them.
findings.impact: Roll back after promoting these migrations and the platform silently loses its two central write paths. Calculation persistence fails with a diagnosis that points at the wrong thing entirely ('shipment not editable'), sending the incident response down a false trail. Every ACTUAL-emissions determination is refused with a bare 42501. Both failures are invisible to `/api/health`, which ROLLBACK.md §1 names as the confirmation signal.
findings.recommendation: Do not promote 20260903190000 and 20260903120000 in the same window as a release whose rollback target predates their application-side commits. Either (a) ship the application changes first, in a build that tolerates both schemas, then promote the migrations; or (b) record in the release report that the rollback floor is now commit a80e94c and 23993d9, not the pre-release SHA. Add the non-additive inventory above to ROLLBACK.md as a standing per-release checklist item, and add the 42501-means-permission-denied case to the calculate-line error mapping so a future rollback fails loudly rather than misleadingly.

findings.title: A plain MEMBER can permanently and silently suppress the audit trail for any record they create, by padding an unbounded name/reference field past the 8 KB audit payload bound
findings.boundary: Authenticated org member -> the organization's own audit record; and the product -> the regulator, whose entire auditability guarantee rests on audit_events being complete
findings.precondition: An ordinary MEMBER seat in any organization. No admin role, no capability, no direct database access, no API key -- only the normal create-a-supplier (or installation, operator, organization, shipment) form.
findings.affected_actor: The organization itself and any auditor or regulator relying on its audit trail. The suppressor is the actor, so this is an own-tenant integrity failure that the tenant cannot detect or repair.
findings.exploit: 1. As MEMBER be92879e in org 8eb4367f, submit the create-supplier form with a name of 9000 characters. app/(importer)/suppliers/actions.ts:96 validates it with `z.string().trim().min(1)` -- there is no `.max()`. 2. src/application/suppliers/manage-suppliers.ts:137-151 inserts the row. suppliers has no length CHECK on `name`, so it commits. 3. manage-suppliers.ts:166 then calls `await recordAuditEvent(..., payload: { name: supplier.name })`. 4. record-audit-event.ts:62-71 measures the payload as UTF-8 bytes of its JSON, sees 9012 > 8192, and returns `{ok:false, reason:"payload exceeds the audit payload size bound"}` WITHOUT attempting the insert. 5. The call site discards the return value -- it is a bare `await`. 6. No log line is emitted, because the application layer imports no logger (see the separate observability finding). Result: a supplier record exists with zero corresponding audit events, and nothing anywhere says so. Repeat freely. The same shape applies to installation.created (app/(producer)/installations/actions.ts:355), operator.created (:165), organization.created (app/onboarding/actions.ts:67, app/organization/actions.ts:64) and shipment.created (app/(importer)/shipments/actions.ts:76) -- all `z.string().trim().min(1)` with no upper bound, all feeding the field straight into the audit payload.
findings.evidence:
Live, committed, in p14_review_sandbox.

$ psql "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/p14_review_sandbox" -tA <<'EOF'
begin;
set local role authenticated;
set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"be92879e-73db-41c3-a0b0-5961ea57d1b4","role":"authenticated"}';
insert into suppliers (org_id, name) values ('8eb4367f-9aee-4d72-8ade-08b41f165bd7', repeat('A',9000));
commit;
select 'A) suppliers row COMMITTED: n='||count(*)||' name_len='||max(length(name)) from suppliers where org_id='8eb4367f-9aee-4d72-8ade-08b41f165bd7' and length(name)>8000;
select 'B) supplier.created audit rows in that org: '||count(*) from audit_events where org_id='8eb4367f-9aee-4d72-8ade-08b41f165bd7' and event_type='supplier.created';
EOF
BEGIN
SET
SET
INSERT 0 1
COMMIT
A) suppliers row COMMITTED: n=1 name_len=9000
B) supplier.created audit rows in that org: 0

The audit half, same role and claims:
  PAYLOAD BYTES = 9012  (bound is 8192)
  insert into audit_events (... payload) values (..., jsonb_build_object('name', repeat('A',9000)));
  ERROR:  new row for relation "audit_events" violates check constraint "audit_events_payload_size_ck"

Missing bounds, confirmed:
  select ... where pg_get_constraintdef(oid) ilike '%length(name)%' ...
  suppliers.name has length CHECK: NO
  shipments.reference has length CHECK: NO

The discarded return value, confirmed by exhaustive grep:
  $ grep -rn "await recordAuditEvent(" --include=*.ts src/ | grep -v "\.test\." | wc -l
  34
  $ grep -rn "=\s*await recordAuditEvent" --include=*.ts src/ | grep -v "\.test\."
  (no output)

Code: src/application/audit/record-audit-event.ts:62-71 (Wall 1 early return), :95 (`reason` returned); src/application/suppliers/manage-suppliers.ts:166 (bare await).
findings.why_controls_fail: Both walls work exactly as designed -- that is not the defect. record-audit-event.ts's own comment calls this the "two-wall pattern" and is careful that Wall 1's byte measurement is numerically identical to Wall 2's CHECK. The failure is that the refusal has no consumer and no sink. The P14/WP-K change added a `reason` string to the return value with a comment explaining it exists so "a rejected audit write ... does not vanish completely" -- but zero of the 34 call sites read it, so the contract is dead on arrival. The same comment then rules out the only other channel: it explicitly declines to import the logger from the application layer, and defers threading the outcome to call sites as a post-release item, reasoning that a partial rollout "would be worse than none." The result is not none -- it is worse than none, because the two walls now guarantee the database stays clean while the audit record is destroyed, and the deliberate decision not to log means the destruction is inaudible. The input-validation layer that should have prevented an oversized payload from ever forming (a `.max()` on the zod schema, or a length CHECK on the column) does not exist on any of the five affected fields.
findings.impact: An unprivileged member can create business records that leave no audit trail, deterministically and repeatably, with no error shown to them and no signal emitted to anyone. audit_events is append-only with no reconciliation job, so the gap can never be filled in retrospectively and there is no query that would reveal it -- a missing row is invisible by construction. For a CBAM compliance platform whose auditability story is the product, this means the audit log cannot be relied on to be complete, which undermines every downstream use of it including regulatory defence.
findings.recommendation: Three changes, smallest first. (1) Put a `.max()` on every user-supplied string that reaches an audit payload -- supplier name, installation name, operator name, organization name, shipment reference -- sized so the resulting payload cannot approach 8192 bytes, and add matching length CHECKs so the bound is not only in the UI layer. (2) Make the audit-write outcome impossible to discard: change recordAuditEvent's return to something a caller must handle, or have it throw on a Wall 1 rejection (a payload the application itself constructed being over the bound is a programming error, not an expected outcome, and the CLAUDE.md rule reserves `throw` for exactly that). (3) Give the mutation paths a real signal: either thread the outcome up to the Server Actions, which can already reach the logger, or accept the layering cost and let this one helper log. Doing (1) alone closes this exploit but leaves the general class -- an RLS refusal or a catalog miss would still vanish silently.
