findings.title: The importer's shared-data screen asserts a green "Current" badge on determinations that are provably superseded, and the staleness warning inverts from STALE to "Current" the moment the producer revokes the grant
findings.boundary: Producer org -> importer org: a cross-tenant claim about whether the importer's frozen emissions figure still reflects the producer's published data. Also product-UI vs stored-data truth.
findings.precondition: Nothing adversarial is required. A normal importer holding an ACTUAL determination taken under a sharing grant, and a producer taking either of two entirely legitimate actions: revoking or letting the grant expire, or superseding/discarding the emission_data row.
findings.affected_actor: The importer, who files a CBAM declaration on a figure the screen tells them is current; and downstream the regulator, who receives understated embedded emissions. The producer is also harmed -- their correction never reaches the counterparty.
findings.exploit:
Reproduced end to end against line 27023f49-882a-4aa4-badd-b3c62e0f7f24 (importer org 8eb4367f, installation bbadeade, grant 0b8bb226), whose frozen snapshot holds emission_data_version 1 at direct_specific 0.10 tCO2e/t.

Step 1 baseline, grant ACTIVE, only v1 exists -> the two queries checkActualDeterminationStalenessByShipment issues return v1 and the installation, so version 1 > 1 is false -> CURRENT. Correct.

Step 2 the producer supersedes v1 with v2 at direct_specific 9.99 (a ~100x correction, the kind a real verification round produces). Grant still ACTIVE -> the emission_data query returns v2 and the grant query returns the installation, so version 2 > 1 -> STALE. The UI correctly shows "Stale -- newer data available". Correct.

Step 3 the producer revokes the grant. Now BOTH filters close: the emission_data SELECT policy (`installation_id in app.user_shared_installation_ids() and status='ACTIVE' and verification_status='VERIFIED'`) returns zero rows, AND activeGrantedInstallationIds returns an empty set. `currentByInstallation.get(installation_id)` is undefined -> checkActualSnapshotStaleness(snapshot, null) hits its first branch and returns "CURRENT" -> app/(importer)/emissions/page.tsx:288-291 renders `<Badge tone="success">Current</Badge>`. The warning that was correct one moment earlier is replaced by a positive green assurance. Lines 268-273 of the same file, on the same table row, simultaneously render "Access since revoked" -- the page contradicts itself.

Step 4 the second, independent path to the same false badge: restore the grant to ACTIVE and have the producer DISCARD v2 with nothing re-activated (a full retraction). The emission_data query returns zero rows again -> null -> "CURRENT". The producer has withdrawn the data entirely and the importer's screen says the determination is current.

A third path needs no producer action at all: checkActualDeterminationStalenessByShipment:181-183 returns `{}` on any query error, and list-actual-determined-lines.ts:455 defaults an absent entry to "CURRENT" -- so a transient database fault paints every line on the screen green.
findings.evidence:
Live, in p14_review_sandbox. Each step run as `set local role authenticated` with `request.jwt.claims` set to the importer member be92879e-73db-41c3-a0b0-5961ea57d1b4.

STEP1 emission_data visible to importer: v1/ACTIVE
STEP1 active grants for installation: 0b8bb226-b55f-4c26-95c1-c967309e6643/ACTIVE
   -> checkActualSnapshotStaleness(v1 snapshot, v1) = CURRENT

SETUP: v1=SUPERSEDED/0.10 v2=ACTIVE/9.99
STEP2 (grant ACTIVE, v2 exists) emission_data query rows: v2/ACTIVE/direct=9.99
STEP2 activeGrantedInstallationIds: bbadeade-4ec9-48e2-ab5d-6351f9116589
   -> 2 > 1 = STALE

GRANT now: REVOKED
STEP3 emission_data query rows: NONE (zero rows)
STEP3 activeGrantedInstallationIds: EMPTY SET
STEP3 grant row still readable for provenance label: 0b8bb226-... status=REVOKED
   -> checkActualSnapshotStaleness(v1 snapshot, null) = CURRENT   <-- inversion

STATE: grant=ACTIVE | ed=v1=SUPERSEDED v2=DISCARDED
STEP4 (grant ACTIVE, producer retracted all data) emission_data ACTIVE rows: NONE (zero rows) -> CURRENT

The frozen snapshot the importer keeps filing on, unchanged throughout:
  {"values": {"direct_specific": "0.10", "indirect_specific": "0.05"}, "emission_data_version": 1, "sharing_grant_id": "0b8bb226-...", ...}

Code: app/(importer)/emissions/page.tsx:283-291 (the `staleness === "STALE" ? warning : <Badge tone="success">Current</Badge>` ternary) and :268-273 ("Access since revoked" on the same row); src/domain/emissions/check-actual-snapshot-staleness.ts:52-54 (`if (currentEmissionData === null) return "CURRENT"`); src/application/emissions/check-actual-determination-staleness.ts:93 and :108 (activeGrantedInstallationIds returns an empty Set on no grants or on error), :181-183 (query error -> `{}`), :218 (`grantedInstallationIds.has(...)` filter); src/application/emissions/list-actual-determined-lines.ts:455 (`?? "CURRENT"`).
findings.why_controls_fail: The staleness control is the only mechanism that tells an importer their frozen ACTUAL figure has been superseded, and it is derived by joining against rows the caller can still see. Revocation removes exactly that visibility, and activeGrantedInstallationIds then filters the same installation out a second time -- so the two independent defences both funnel to the identical `null`, and the domain function reads `null` as CURRENT. The domain function's comment defends this as failing "toward the quieter result rather than raising a false alarm", which would be sound if the UI rendered the quiet case as nothing. It does not: /emissions renders it as an affirmative green "Current". Quiet and affirmatively-reassuring are opposite things, and the two halves of this design were written against different assumptions. The codebase already knows about this exact gap and worked around it elsewhere: list-actual-determined-lines.ts's own doc comment explains that it deliberately resolves the grantor's NAME through sharing_grants rather than emission_data precisely because the emission_data path "fails the moment the sharing grant that produced THIS historical determination is later revoked", and cites checkActualDeterminationStalenessByShipment as documenting "this exact gap for the staleness signal". The provenance label was fixed. The staleness column, which carries far more weight, was not. Finally, nothing downstream compensates: I grepped src/domain/declarations, src/application/declarations and src/application/reporting for ActualSnapshotStaleness and checkActualSnapshot and found zero hits -- declaration completeness checks calculation-vs-determination staleness (LINE_CALCULATION_STALE) but never determination-vs-producer-data staleness, so filing is not gated on it either.
findings.impact: An importer files a CBAM declaration on emissions the producer has superseded or withdrawn, while the screen affirmatively tells them the figure is current. In the reproduced case that is 0.10 against a true 9.99 tCO2e/t -- roughly a hundredfold understatement of embedded emissions and therefore of certificates due and liability, frozen into an immutable filed_snapshot. The regression on revocation is the sharpest part: the system displayed the correct warning, then withdrew it and replaced it with a green assurance in response to an action the importer never sees and cannot influence. An importer who checked the screen before and after a revocation would reasonably conclude the producer had resolved the discrepancy.
findings.recommendation: Give ActualSnapshotStaleness a third state -- UNKNOWN -- and return it whenever the evidence is absent rather than present-and-equal: no ACTIVE row visible, no live grant for a shared installation, or a failed query. Then render UNKNOWN as a neutral or warning badge ("Cannot confirm -- access revoked", "Cannot confirm -- producer data withdrawn"), never as "Current", and never fold it into the same branch as a genuinely-verified-current determination. The three call sites that currently collapse to CURRENT are check-actual-snapshot-staleness.ts:52-54, check-actual-determination-staleness.ts:181-183, and list-actual-determined-lines.ts:455. Separately, and independently worth doing: have declaration completeness consult determination staleness, so a line that is known STALE or UNKNOWN cannot be filed without an explicit acknowledgement. Note that resolving the staleness signal through sharing_grants the way the provenance label already does would fix the revoked case but not the retracted-data case, so the UNKNOWN state is needed regardless.

findings.title: A plain MEMBER destroys a VERIFIED record's evidence -- array, metadata row, sha256 and all -- by superseding or discarding it first; every guard keys on a state the member moves in statement one, and nothing is audited
findings.boundary: Intra-tenant privilege boundary (MEMBER vs the verification/evidence integrity lock), with the harm landing on a DIFFERENT organisation's filed declaration and on the regulator's audit trail.
findings.precondition: An ordinary, non-deactivated MEMBER row in public.memberships for the producer organisation. No ADMIN, no OWNER, no service_role. The public anon key plus the member's own JWT is sufficient; supersedeEmissionData in src/application/emissions/manage-emission-data.ts carries no admin gate either.
findings.affected_actor: The importer/declarant counterparty whose determination and filed declaration cite this record, and the regulator, whose audit trail loses the document that substantiated a verification. The producer org's own OWNER cannot detect it -- no audit event is written.
findings.exploit:
Four statements, as role authenticated with a MEMBER JWT:
1. `update public.emission_data set status='SUPERSEDED' where id=<rec>;` -- ordinary product operation, leaves verification_status='VERIFIED', drops old.status out of the shrink guard's `old.status='ACTIVE'` predicate.
2. `update public.emission_data set evidence_file_ids='{}' where id=<rec>;` -- record is now SUPERSEDED + VERIFIED with ZERO evidence.
3. `update public.emission_data set verification_status='UNVERIFIED' where id=<rec>;` -- unrestricted, because the ADMIN/OWNER gate only fires when the TARGET is 'VERIFIED' or 'REJECTED'.
4. `delete from public.evidence_files where id=<ev>;` -- the delete policy's `ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED'` now passes; sha256, original_filename, storage_path and uploaded_by_user_id are gone permanently.
The DISCARD variant is identical with `status='DISCARDED'` at step 1 and works equally.
findings.evidence:
psql "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/p14_review_sandbox"; begin; set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"aaaa0000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002","role":"authenticated"}';

BEFORE   | ACTIVE     | VERIFIED   | {ffff0000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001}
update ... set status='SUPERSEDED'                -> UPDATE 1
1 superseded | SUPERSEDED | VERIFIED   | {ffff0000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001}
update ... set evidence_file_ids='{}'             -> UPDATE 1
2 evidence detached (still VERIFIED) | SUPERSEDED | VERIFIED | {}
update ... set verification_status='UNVERIFIED'   -> UPDATE 1
delete from public.evidence_files where id='ffff0000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'  -> DELETE 1
3 evidence row destroyed  | 0
4 audit events written    | 0
rollback;   post-rollback re-verify: ACTIVE|VERIFIED|{ffff0000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001}, evidence_files count 1.

DISCARD variant, same session shape:
BEFORE ed | ACTIVE | VERIFIED | {ffff...0001}
delete from public.evidence_files where id='ffff...0001'   -> DELETE 0   (correctly blocked while ACTIVE+VERIFIED)
update ... set status='DISCARDED'                          -> UPDATE 1
update ... set verification_status='UNVERIFIED'            -> UPDATE 1
C: ed | DISCARDED | UNVERIFIED
delete from public.evidence_files where id='ffff...0001'   -> DELETE 1
D: rows left | 0

Also reproduced against a pre-existing SUPERSEDED+VERIFIED record (eeee0000-...0002 / ffff0000-...0002): `S1 strip array | SUPERSEDED | VERIFIED | {}` then `S3 ef rows left | 0`.
findings.why_controls_fail: Three controls exist and all three key on the SAME mutable pair. (a) app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate's evidence-shrink rule, added by 20260903150000, opens with `if old.status = 'ACTIVE' and old.verification_status = 'VERIFIED'` -- the migration's header explains at length why `new.status` was removed from the un-verify rule, then leaves `old.status='ACTIVE'` in the shrink rule, so SUPERSEDED and DISCARDED fall outside it. Its comment argues DISCARD/SUPERSEDE are safe because they 'do not change verification_status' -- true, and irrelevant: they change the column the NEXT statement's guard reads. (b) evidence_files_delete_own_org (20260829560000) requires `ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED'`, which step 3 supplies. (c) removeEvidenceFile's Wall 1 (src/application/evidence/upload-evidence.ts:554, `if (ownership.verificationStatus === "VERIFIED")`) reads the identical live column, so the two walls are one wall. The un-verify gate that would have stopped step 3 is itself scoped `if old.status = 'ACTIVE'`. And no trigger exists on evidence_files (`select count(*) from pg_trigger where tgrelid='public.evidence_files'::regclass and not tgisinternal` -> 0), so the deletion is invisible: audit_events stayed at 0.
findings.impact: The document set a verifier signed off on, and that an importer froze byte-for-byte into a determination backing a FILED CBAM declaration, is irrecoverably deleted by the lowest-privileged role in the owning org, with no audit record, no notification to the counterparty and no way for either party to discover it. At step 2 the record still reads verification_status='VERIFIED', so a superseded historical dataset sits in the database asserting it was verified while carrying no evidence at all. For a regulatory filing system this is precisely the failure the evidence subsystem exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Stop keying evidence guards on the current lifecycle pair. Introduce an immutable high-water mark -- e.g. `emission_data.ever_verified_at timestamptz`, set by the trigger on the transition into VERIFIED and never cleared -- and rewrite all three controls against it: the shrink rule to `if old.ever_verified_at is not null` (dropping the old.status conjunct entirely), evidence_files_delete_own_org's EXISTS to `ed.ever_verified_at is null`, and removeEvidenceFile's Wall 1 to the same field. Independently, forbid downgrading verification_status away from 'VERIFIED' for ANY old.status, not just ACTIVE -- the carve-out has no stated justification. Add an AFTER DELETE trigger on evidence_files writing an EVIDENCE_FILE audit event so a direct-API deletion can never be silent. Add a regression test per route (ACTIVE->SUPERSEDED->strip; ACTIVE->DISCARDED->downgrade->delete) asserting the exact 42501.

findings.title: A READY declaration's member set is never re-verified against its reporting period: a shipment added after mark-ready is silently omitted from the immutable filed snapshot, and the product offers no way to include it
findings.boundary: Declaration filing integrity -- the boundary between what the reporting period actually contains and what the filed_snapshot says it contains. No privilege boundary is crossed; this is a correctness boundary on the legally meaningful artifact.
findings.precondition: None beyond normal, sanctioned use of the product by its intended users. An IMPORTER_DECLARANT org whose admin marked a period's declaration READY at any point before the period stopped receiving shipments. No forgery, no raw PostgREST, no elevated privilege, no bypass of any gate.
findings.affected_actor: The declarant organisation itself and the regulator receiving its CBAM declaration. The filed_snapshot is the archived, immutable, legally meaningful record and it understates.
findings.exploit: 1. Period ANNUAL 2026 contains one shipment, SHIP-58d83151 (100 t, 139 tCO2e). The admin generates the draft and marks it READY. markDeclarationReady FREEZES member_shipment_ids at that instant (src/application/declarations/mark-declaration-ready.ts:172). 2. A second real import arrives. Any member creates SHIP-OMIT-B (900 t) in the same period, adds its line, marks it READY; the admin calculates it through the normal engine path. Every step is an ordinary product action and the calculation row is engine-produced through record_calculation_result. 3. The admin opens the declaration. Because status is READY, DeclarationActions renders ONLY RecordFiledForm (app/(importer)/declarations/[id]/declaration-actions.tsx:90-95) -- no refresh action, no reopen action. getDeclarationDetail does not recompute period facts; the screen shows the frozen member set and the frozen `complete: true`. There is no in-product signal that the period grew, and calling generateOrRefreshDeclarationDraft for the period returns PERIOD_HAS_READY_DECLARATION (generate-or-refresh-declaration-draft.ts:151), so the admin cannot refresh it. 4. The admin clicks Record filed. record_declaration_filed re-verifies freshness INSIDE the frozen member set (missing calculations, superseded determinations, mismatched quantities, emptied members) but never re-derives the set. It returns OK.
findings.why_controls_fail: supabase/migrations/20260829470000 and 20260903110000 both open by naming the exact staleness window they close: "a line can be added, re-determined, or DELETED entirely AFTER the completeness gate passed and BEFORE anyone clicks record filed". Every clause they added -- the determination comparison, the quantity/unit comparison, v_empty_member_count -- iterates `member_lines`, defined as `select ... from public.shipment_lines sl where sl.shipment_id = any(v_member_ids)`. The gate therefore re-verifies added LINES inside an already-member shipment and never an added SHIPMENT. v_lockable_count only checks the listed members are the org's and are READY/LOCKED. There is no comparison of s.reporting_period_* against v_decl.reporting_period_* anywhere in the function, and no count of the period against the list. The migration's claim that "totals.shipment_count = cardinality(v_member_ids) is therefore a real invariant" is true and beside the point: cardinality(v_member_ids) is whatever the frozen array holds. The application-layer wall (markDeclarationReady re-running computeDeclarationDraftFacts) is a DRAFT->READY gate; it never runs again, and the READY screen exposes no action that would re-run it.
findings.impact: An immutable, archived, legally meaningful CBAM filing record understating embedded emissions by an unbounded fraction, produced entirely through sanctioned product actions, carrying complete: true, a full internally-consistent provenance block naming real engine-produced calculation rows, and a complete audit trail. Because CBAM liability is priced off declared embedded emissions, this is direct under-declaration. The omitted shipment is left in READY -- not LOCKED -- so no state anywhere records that it was excluded, and no later reconciliation can distinguish "never imported" from "omitted from the filing". Worse, the omission is not merely possible but unavoidable: with the declaration in READY there is no product path to add the shipment, so the admin's only options are to file the understated declaration or leave the period unfiled.
findings.recommendation: record_declaration_filed must re-derive period membership rather than trust member_shipment_ids. Alongside the existing v_lockable_count check add (a) a per-member period check -- every member shipment's (reporting_period_kind, reporting_period_year, reporting_period_quarter) must equal the declaration's -- and (b) the reverse completeness check: `select count(*) from public.shipments s where s.org_id = v_decl.org_id and s.reporting_period_* = v_decl.reporting_period_* and s.status <> 'VOID' and not (s.id = any(v_member_ids))` must be zero, else return a new PERIOD_MEMBERSHIP_STALE status. Both are cheap and sit on a code path that already runs. In parallel, the READY declaration screen must expose a re-verify/reopen action (and generateOrRefreshDeclarationDraft must stop dead-ending a READY period) so the named refusal is actionable rather than a second dead end.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: member_shipment_ids is client-writable and unvalidated against the reporting period, so an admin can file a curated or wholly cross-period declaration
findings.boundary: Declaration filing integrity -- the RLS/trigger boundary that is supposed to make member_shipment_ids a derived, frozen fact.
findings.precondition: ADMIN or OWNER of an IMPORTER_DECLARANT org, posting to PostgREST directly instead of using the product -- exactly the threat model supabase/migrations/20260903110000 and 20260903190000 accepted as blocker-worthy for calculation_results ("a member ... posting raw PostgREST rather than using the product").
findings.affected_actor: The regulator receiving the filing, and any auditor relying on the filed_snapshot. Own-tenant only -- RLS correctly bounds every id involved.
findings.exploit: Variant A (omission from an honest READY state): `update declarations set status='DRAFT' where id=...` (permitted: declarations_update_own_org_pre_filing's USING admits READY, its WITH CHECK admits DRAFT), then `update declarations set member_shipment_ids='{only the small shipment}', status='READY' where id=...` in one statement (permitted: app.prevent_declaration_fact_change only freezes member_shipment_ids when old.status <> 'DRAFT'), then record_declaration_filed. The "frozen once it leaves DRAFT" guard is defeated by a single READY->DRAFT round trip that RLS itself permits. Variant B (cross-period): put a 2025 shipment id into a 2026 declaration's member set and file it. record_declaration_filed checks only org ownership and READY/LOCKED status.
findings.why_controls_fail: app.prevent_declaration_fact_change freezes member_shipment_ids only for `old.status <> 'DRAFT'`, and declarations_update_own_org_pre_filing explicitly permits READY->DRAFT (USING admits DRAFT and READY; WITH CHECK admits DRAFT, READY, VOID). So the freeze is one permitted UPDATE away from being lifted. markDeclarationReady's re-derivation is an application-layer wall the RLS policy does not require anyone to go through -- the policy's WITH CHECK validates only the actor's role and the target status, never the member set's provenance. record_declaration_filed's own membership check is `s.id = any(v_member_ids) and s.org_id = v_decl.org_id and s.status in ('READY','LOCKED')`: org and status, never period, never completeness. Nothing in the filed_snapshot records each shipment's period, so the archived artifact cannot be checked against this afterwards.
findings.impact: An admin can freeze any subset of their org's shipments, or shipments from an entirely different reporting period, into an immutable filed CBAM declaration, with a passing determination check, a passing quantity check, a passing reproducibility story and a complete audit trail. This is the same defect class the project already declared a release blocker twice (forged quantity, forged emissions figure) reappearing one level up: the earlier fixes pinned what a calculation says about a line; nothing pins what the declaration says about the period.
findings.recommendation: Same structural fix as finding 1 -- validate membership inside record_declaration_filed, the only place a filed fact is created. Additionally consider removing member_shipment_ids from the authenticated UPDATE surface entirely (a column-level revoke, or moving the DRAFT->READY transition into a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that derives the set itself) so the application-layer derivation in markDeclarationReady stops being optional.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: A plain MEMBER can irreversibly VOID a READY, fully-calculated shipment, and it then vanishes silently from every declaration for its period rather than blocking one
findings.boundary: Role boundary (MEMBER vs ADMIN/OWNER) combined with declaration completeness -- a non-privileged member unilaterally and permanently changes what a period's filed declaration will contain.
findings.precondition: MEMBER role in an IMPORTER_DECLARANT org. No admin rights and no raw PostgREST required -- VOID is a member-level product action by design (src/application/shipments/transition-shipment.ts:96 gates only LOCK on hasAdminAccess; its own comment says "MARK_READY/REOPEN/VOID stay" member-level).
findings.affected_actor: The declarant organisation (whose admins are never shown that the period shrank) and the regulator. Own-tenant.
findings.exploit: 1. A member opens a READY, fully-calculated shipment and voids it. 2. The shipment is now terminal: shipments_update_own_org_not_terminal's USING clause excludes VOID, so neither the member, nor an ADMIN, nor the OWNER can restore it -- there is no un-VOID path anywhere. 3. computeDeclarationDraftFacts excludes VOID shipments from period membership outright (src/application/declarations/compute-declaration-draft-facts.ts:129, `.neq("status", "VOID")`). The shipment does not become a blocker; it ceases to exist for declaration purposes. 4. The admin generates/refreshes the draft, sees complete: true with no mention of the voided shipment, marks READY and files. The filed_snapshot is understated by the whole voided shipment.
findings.why_controls_fail: shipments_update_own_org_not_terminal's WITH CHECK is `org_id in (app.user_org_ids()) and (status <> 'LOCKED' or app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of(org_id))` -- it gates only LOCKED behind admin. VOID is open to every member, and the USING clause `status <> all(array['LOCKED','VOID'])` makes VOID terminal for everyone, so there is no recovery. compute-declaration-draft-facts.ts:112-129 makes the exclusion silent on purpose; its own comment reasons that keeping VOID in the member set "permanently deadlocked the whole period's declaration" and chose exclusion. That reasoning is sound about the deadlock and wrong about the consequence: it converted a loud, un-clearable blocker into no signal at all. buildCompletenessReport is never told the shipment existed, so no blocker, warning or count reflects it, and the filed_snapshot has no field that would show it either.
findings.impact: Any single non-privileged member can permanently and silently remove real imported goods from their organisation's CBAM declaration for a reporting period, with the resulting filed_snapshot reporting complete: true and no trace of the removal anywhere in the declaration record. The only surviving evidence is a shipment.voided audit event on a different aggregate that no declaration surface reads. This is a privilege-escalation-shaped hole in the compliance record: the role that cannot file a declaration can nonetheless dictate what a declaration contains.
findings.recommendation: Two changes, both needed. (1) Gate the VOID transition behind hasAdminAccess and an admin-only RLS WITH CHECK clause, the way LOCK already is -- retiring goods from a compliance record is not a member-level act. (2) Stop making VOID invisible: keep voided in-period shipments out of member_shipment_ids but surface them in the completeness report as an explicit, acknowledgeable disclosure (count, references, who voided them and when), and record that same list in filed_snapshot, so an archived filing states what it excluded rather than merely omitting it. If irreversibility is retained, it must at minimum be admin-only.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: A plain member steers the authoritative emissions figure by editing shipments.release_date: the Annex II direct-only treatment is silently dropped, the trusted RPC persists the inflated number, filing freezes it, and the reproduction proof is blinded by construction
findings.boundary: Member (authenticated, non-admin) -> the authoritative calculation result and the immutable filed declaration snapshot. The P14.1 trust boundary claims to sit 'where the engine runs, which is the server'; this crosses it by moving an engine INPUT the server reads at calculation time, rather than by forging the output.
findings.precondition: A plain MEMBER (role = MEMBER, not ADMIN/OWNER) of an IMPORTER_DECLARANT org, with an ACTUAL-method line on a good in an Annex II sector (IRON_STEEL / ALUMINIUM) whose parent shipment is DRAFT or READY. No admin rights, no service_role key, no forged determination, no forged quantity. Verified live: `select role from public.memberships where user_id='be92879e-73db-41c3-a0b0-5961ea57d1b4'` -> MEMBER.
findings.affected_actor: Own tenant, and through it the regulator. The declarant's own filed CBAM figure is wrong, and the filed_snapshot that is meant to be the re-provable record of it carries no trace that the Annex II treatment was ever considered.
findings.exploit: 1. Member sets a valid ACTUAL determination on line 27023f49 (cn_code 72061000 = IRON_STEEL, net_mass_tonnes 100, direct_specific 0.10, indirect_specific 0.05). Correct engine output = 100 * 0.10 = 10 tCO2e, because the Annex II branch excludes indirect. 2. Member issues a single UPDATE on a DIFFERENT table: `update public.shipments set release_date='2025-01-15'`. This is not the line, so app.validate_emission_determination_write never fires and emission_determination is untouched (md5 unchanged). 3. resolveGoodSectorForActualLine (calculate-line.ts:116-141) re-reads that release_date and passes it to findCbamGoodsByCode as the as-of date. 72061000's cbam_goods row is active_from 2026-01-01, so at 2025-01-15 the lookup returns zero rows, `candidates[0]?.sector ?? null` yields null, and the Annex II gate at calculate-line-emissions.ts (`goodSector !== null && ANNEX_II_SECTORS.has(goodSector)`) evaluates false. 4. The engine now computes 100 * (0.10 + 0.05) = 15 and emits a trace with NO ANNEX_II_DIRECT_ONLY step at all — a reader of the frozen trace cannot tell the treatment was skipped. 5. record_calculation_result accepts it: determination matches byte-for-byte, quantity and unit match, actor is a live member, org holds IMPORTER_DECLARANT. 6. record_declaration_filed accepts it: it compares determination, quantity and quantity_unit against the line, and nothing else. 15 is frozen into filed_snapshot.totals. 7. reproduceCalculationResult re-derives good_sector from the SAME still-manipulated release_date, recomputes 15, deepEqual matches the stored steps, and returns REPRODUCIBLE.
findings.why_controls_fail: Every wall that exists is about the determination and the quantity, and good_sector is neither. (a) `record_calculation_result`'s Binding 1 compares p_determination to the line's emission_determination — the determination is genuinely unchanged, so it passes; the RPC has no parameter for good_sector and never looks one up. (b) Binding 2 compares quantity and unit — both unchanged. (c) `app.validate_emission_determination_write` only nulls the determination when cn_code / origin_country / net_mass_tonnes / quantity_mwh / production_route_indicator change on the LINE; release_date lives on `shipments`, a different table with no such trigger (pg_trigger on public.shipments shows only prevent_org_id_change). (d) `record_declaration_filed`'s P13/P14 freshness gate compares c.determination, c.quantity and c.quantity_unit against the line — it never compares anything about the shipment. (e) `checkCalculationCurrency` (src/domain/emissions/check-calculation-currency.ts) defines staleness as determination inequality only. (f) `reproduceCalculationResult` cannot detect it because it re-derives the identical manipulated input rather than reading a frozen one — its own doc comment at reproduce-calculation-result.ts:264 asserts 'shipment_id.release_date is a stable, immutable historical fact (no update path exists for it -- only create-shipment.ts ever writes it)'. That is true of the application layer and false of the database: `shipments_update_own_org_not_terminal` permits any member to UPDATE any non-LOCKED/VOID shipment row, and this project's own threat model (the P14.1 migration header) explicitly counts 'a member posting raw PostgREST' as in scope. The whole P14.1 remediation is premised on the row's frozen inputs being the complete input set; they are not.
findings.impact: A plain member can make the authoritative embedded-emissions figure differ from the figure the engine's own rules produce, by 50% in the measured case (15 vs 10), and get it into an immutable filed declaration snapshot that the platform will later certify as REPRODUCIBLE. The direction is dataset-dependent, not attacker-limited: on today's dataset the reachable direction is over-statement (Annex II treatment dropped, indirect emissions wrongly added), but the same lever produces UNDER-statement the moment cbam_goods carries date-versioned sector rows — which is precisely what a dataset refresh creates (active_to on the old row, a new row with a new active_from). It also destroys the meaning of the reproduction proof for every ACTUAL-method row: REPRODUCIBLE currently means 'the stored number follows from the stored inputs AND from whatever the mutable world says today', which is not the §17 contract.
findings.recommendation: Freeze the derived input on the row instead of re-deriving it. Add a `good_sector` column (or a `parameter_datasets` entry naming the cbam_goods row id, trade_code and as-of date actually used) to calculation_results, populate it in record_calculation_result from a lookup the FUNCTION performs — not from a caller parameter — and have reproduceCalculationResult read the frozen value rather than calling resolveGoodSectorForActualLine. Independently, pin `shipments.release_date` with a BEFORE UPDATE trigger the same way `app.prevent_declaration_fact_change` and `app.prevent_emission_data_fact_change` already pin their tables' declared facts; release_date is a declared customs fact and the reporting period is derived from it. Correct the false immutability claim at reproduce-calculation-result.ts:264 in the same change.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The engine's unit guard accepts magnitude-prefixed denominators: tCO2e/kilotonne, TCO2E_PER_MEGATONNE, tCO2e/kMWh and tCO2/MMWh are computed as if per-tonne / per-MWh, producing 1000x and 1,000,000x wrong figures instead of UNIT_UNSUPPORTED
findings.boundary: Producer/operator free-text input -> the importer's authoritative calculation. Also reachable as pure member-side manipulation, since emission_data.emission_unit is unconstrained and the determination validator only requires the snapshot's unit to equal the emission_data row's own.
findings.precondition: An ACTUAL-method determination whose emission_unit is a magnitude-prefixed intensity string. No privilege at all is needed for the honest-mistake case: the producer entry form's own placeholder is free text ('e.g. tCO2e/t'), and emission_data.emission_unit has no CHECK constraint. For the deliberate case, whoever can create an emission_data row can choose the string.
findings.affected_actor: Cross-tenant (a producer's unit string determines an importer's filed number) and the regulator. The DEFAULT path is unaffected — default_emission_values_emission_unit_check restricts that column to exactly {TCO2E_PER_TONNE, TCO2_PER_MWH}.
findings.exploit: emission_unit = 'tCO2e/kilotonne', direct_specific = 0.10, indirect_specific = 0.05, line net_mass_tonnes = 100 t. The true figure is 100 t * 0.10 tCO2e/kt = 100 t * 0.0001 tCO2e/t = 0.01 tCO2e. The engine computes 10 (Annex II direct-only) — 1000x too high. unitMatchesQuantityBasis normalizes to 'TCO2E/KILOTONNE'; the numerator regex /^TCO2E?(?:\/|_PER_|$)/ matches on 'TCO2E/'; the denominator test is `normalized.includes("TONNE")`, and 'KILOTONNE' contains 'TONNE', so the anchored /\/T(?![A-Z0-9])/ pattern that was added to catch /TJ and /TWh is never even consulted. The identical hole exists on the MWh branch, where the entire denominator test is `normalized.includes("MWH")`.
findings.evidence:
Real engine, via tsx against src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts, line net_mass_tonnes='100', direct 2 / indirect 1 (expected COMPUTED 300 only for genuine per-tonne units):
"tCO2e/t"                    COMPUTED 300     <- correct
"tCO2e/kilotonne"            COMPUTED 300     <- should be UNIT_UNSUPPORTED (true value 0.3)
"TCO2E_PER_KILOTONNE"        COMPUTED 300     <- should be UNIT_UNSUPPORTED
"TCO2E_PER_MEGATONNE"        COMPUTED 300     <- should be UNIT_UNSUPPORTED (true value 0.0003)
"tCO2e/ktonne"               COMPUTED 300     <- should be UNIT_UNSUPPORTED
"tCO2e/short tonne"          COMPUTED 300     <- should be UNIT_UNSUPPORTED (understates ~9.3%)
"tCO2e/kt"                   UNIT_UNSUPPORTED <- caught only because it lacks the letters TONNE
"kgCO2e/t"                   UNIT_UNSUPPORTED <- the P13 numerator fix, still working

MWh-basis line (quantity_mwh='100'):
"tCO2e/MWh"                  COMPUTED 300     <- correct
"tCO2e/kMWh"                 COMPUTED 300     <- should be UNIT_UNSUPPORTED
"tCO2/MMWh"                  COMPUTED 300     <- should be UNIT_UNSUPPORTED
"tCO2e/MWH/t"                COMPUTED 300     <- a mass-per-energy hybrid, accepted for an energy line
"tCO2e/GWh"                  UNIT_UNSUPPORTED

Reachability, live in p14_review_sandbox:
