  -- no constraint on emission_unit exists (direct/indirect numeric, methodology, status, verification_status, version, reporting period only)
insert into public.emission_data (... emission_unit ...) values (..., 'tCO2e/kilotonne', ...);
  DB ACCEPTED emission_unit = | tCO2e/kilotonne
-- then, as a plain MEMBER of the importer org:
set role authenticated; set request.jwt.claims='{"sub":"be92879e-...","role":"authenticated"}';
update public.shipment_lines set emission_determination = <ACTUAL snapshot carrying 'tCO2e/kilotonne'> where id='cccccccc-0000-4000-8000-000000000002';
UPDATE 1
 DETERMINATION VALIDATOR ACCEPTED unit = | tCO2e/kilotonne
-- and the trusted channel persists the resulting figure:
set role service_role; select * from public.record_calculation_result(..., '10', null);
 OK | 2eec61ef-c616-4e21-829a-ca4c2f24fdf7
 PERSISTED | 10 | tCO2e/kilotonne
findings.why_controls_fail: unitMatchesQuantityBasis IS the control — its own doc comment says it exists so the engine never 'silently accepted them as mass-basis and computed a fabricated number instead of UNIT_UNSUPPORTED'. The P13 audit hardened the numerator with an anchored regex and the '/T' denominator with a negative lookahead, and the comment claims the result was 'Verified against both the original false-negative and this new false-positive class'. It was not verified against the OTHER denominator branch, which is still the bare substring test it always was. Downstream: app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record only asserts `v_ed.emission_unit is not distinct from (v_snapshot->>'emission_unit')` — it validates that the snapshot copied the unit faithfully, never that the unit is meaningful. record_calculation_result has no unit parameter beyond p_quantity_unit (TONNES/MWH) and never inspects the determination's emission_unit. record_declaration_filed sums embedded_emissions_tco2e as ::numeric with no unit awareness. reproduceCalculationResult recomputes with the same wrong rule and returns REPRODUCIBLE. Nothing anywhere else validates emission_unit — the engine comment itself concedes 'The real fix is an allow-list on EmissionData.emission_unit at entry ... this function remains a stop-gap', and that allow-list still does not exist.
findings.impact: A wrong embedded-emissions figure by a factor of 1000 or 1,000,000, produced by the trusted engine from unforged inputs, marked REPRODUCIBLE, and filable. Both directions are reachable: 'tCO2e/kilotonne' over-states 1000x, 'tCO2e/short tonne' under-states ~9.3% (a plausible US-operator entry). Because it is triggered by a free-text field on the counterparty's record, it does not require a malicious actor at all — a producer typing a legitimate unit the guard mishandles is enough, and the importer has no signal that anything is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Two changes, both already named in the codebase's own comments. (1) Replace the substring tests with an anchored denominator match on the whole remaining string: after the numerator, require the denominator to be exactly one of the accepted spellings (T | TONNE | TONNES | MWH), rejecting any prefix or suffix, rather than asking whether those letters appear anywhere. Bump ENGINE_VERSION, since units that previously COMPUTED will now correctly return UNIT_UNSUPPORTED. (2) Add the DB-level allow-list on emission_data.emission_unit that this function's own doc comment says is the real fix, mirroring default_emission_values_emission_unit_check, so the engine stops sniffing free text. Add golden tests covering kilotonne/megatonne/ktonne/short tonne/kMWh/MMWh — the existing engine test suite has no case in this class.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: Annex II sector proxy excludes indirect emissions for CN 2601 12 00, under-reporting by up to 50% — and the same good yields double the figure on the DEFAULT path
findings.boundary: Regulatory correctness: the filed embedded-emissions figure vs. the ACTIVE dataset's own published values. Crosses the ACTUAL/DEFAULT determination boundary — the two paths disagree on identical inputs.
findings.precondition: An importer with IMPORTER_DECLARANT declares a shipment line for CN 2601 12 00 (agglomerated iron ores and concentrates) and determines it from a verified ACTUAL emission_data record whose indirect_specific is non-zero. This is the ordinary, intended workflow — no forgery, no elevated role, no direct API access.
findings.affected_actor: The regulator and the filing. The declarant files, and surrenders certificates against, a materially understated figure.
findings.exploit:
1. The proxy is sector-level: `const ANNEX_II_SECTORS = new Set(["IRON_STEEL", "ALUMINIUM"])` (src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts:46-52), consulted at :298-300 as `goodSector !== null && ANNEX_II_SECTORS.has(goodSector)`.
2. CN 2601 12 00 carries sector IRON_STEEL, so the gate fires and indirect is dropped.
3. But the ACTIVE dataset itself publishes indirect values for this good and sums them into total — it is the ONLY gated good that does.
4. Run the real engine on a line of 1000 t with Kazakhstan's own published intensities (direct 0.170, indirect 0.170):
   - ACTUAL path, good_sector 'IRON_STEEL': 170 tCO2e
   - ACTUAL path, good_sector null (gate off): 340 tCO2e
   - DEFAULT path, same good, same country, dataset total 0.340: 340 tCO2e
5. The importer files 170 where the platform's own dataset says 340.
findings.evidence:
Counting the gated goods myself rather than trusting the audit:
$ psql "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/p14_review_sandbox" -tAc "select sector, count(*) from cbam_goods where record_level='TRADE_GOOD' and sector in ('IRON_STEEL','ALUMINIUM') group by 1;"
ALUMINIUM|15
IRON_STEEL|119
(134 TRADE_GOOD codes gated.)

Which of those the dataset contradicts:
$ psql ... -tAc "select g.trade_code, g.sector, g.description, count(*) filter (where d.indirect_status='AVAILABLE') as rows_with_indirect from cbam_goods g join default_emission_values d on d.good_id=g.id where g.record_level='TRADE_GOOD' and g.sector in ('IRON_STEEL','ALUMINIUM') group by 1,2,3 having count(*) filter (where d.indirect_status='AVAILABLE')>0;"
26011200|IRON_STEEL|Agglomerated iron ores and concentrates (excl. roasted iron pyrites)|28

The published values, and the share dropped:
$ psql ... -tAc "select c.name, d.direct_value, d.indirect_value, d.total_value, round(100*d.indirect_value/d.total_value,1) from default_emission_values d join cbam_goods g on g.id=d.good_id join countries c on c.id=d.country_id where g.trade_code='26011200' and d.indirect_status='AVAILABLE' order by 5 desc limit 6;"
Serbia|0.120|0.110|0.220|50.0
Kazakhstan|0.170|0.170|0.340|50.0
Bosnia and Herzegovina|0.090|0.090|0.190|47.4
Uzbekistan|0.390|0.350|0.740|47.3
Ukraine|0.080|0.050|0.120|41.7
Azerbaijan|0.070|0.050|0.120|41.7

The real, unmodified engine (imported from src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts), 1000 t:
26011200 agglomerated iron ore, Kazakhstan values (0.170/0.170), sector IRON_STEEL
   -> COMPUTED 170 ANNEX_II_DIRECT_ONLY+LINE_EMBEDDED_EMISSIONS
26011200 same values, sector forced null (no gate)
   -> COMPUTED 340 LINE_EMBEDDED_EMISSIONS
DEFAULT path, 26011200 Kazakhstan, 1000 t -> COMPUTED 340 LINE_EMBEDDED_EMISSIONS

And the sector really is IRON_STEEL, so the gate really does fire:
$ psql ... -tAc "select id, trade_code, trade_code_type, record_level, sector, functional_unit, active_from from cbam_goods where trade_code in ('26011200','28041000');"
34a3d83e-...|26011200|CN|TRADE_GOOD|IRON_STEEL|TONNES|2026-01-01
findings.why_controls_fail: Three controls look like they cover this and none does. (a) The ANNEX_II_SECTORS comment (:54-101) states the under-reporting risk in the abstract — 'such a good WOULD have its indirect emissions excluded' — and treats it as a hypothetical accepted cost. It is not hypothetical: the ACTIVE dataset contains exactly one such good and the divergence is up to 50%. Nobody appears to have run the query. (b) The unit tests assert the SECTOR behaviour, not good-level correctness — calculate-line-emissions.test.ts:629-673 uses a bare `good_sector: "IRON_STEEL"` with no CN code, so it passes while the behaviour is wrong for the one real code that matters. A passing test here is not evidence of a meaningful assertion. (c) The DB determination validator does not look at emissions treatment at all; it validates provenance and dataset identity, so it cannot notice that DEFAULT and ACTUAL now disagree by 2x on the same good. Nothing anywhere compares the two paths.
findings.impact: Systematic understatement of embedded emissions, up to 50% per line, on every ACTUAL-determined shipment line for agglomerated iron ores from any of 28 origin countries. Under-reporting a CBAM figure means too few certificates surrendered and an incorrect regulatory submission — the exact failure the codebase's own rules are built to prevent. The 2x DEFAULT/ACTUAL divergence also means the number a declarant sees depends on which determination method they happened to choose, which is indefensible if questioned.
findings.recommendation: Do not ship the ACTUAL-path Annex II gate in its current form. Shortest correct fix consistent with the facts-as-datasets rule: ingest a real Annex II CN-code list as a versioned regulatory_datasets row (dataset_type already has room for it) and gate on membership, not sector. If that cannot land before release, the defensible interim is to gate on the DATASET'S OWN signature rather than on sector — a good is direct-only when every default_emission_values row for it has indirect_status='UNAVAILABLE' — which is a regulatory fact already in the dataset, gets 2601 12 00 and hydrogen both right, and requires no new source. Whatever is chosen, the DEFAULT and ACTUAL paths must be reconciled.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: Any magnitude-prefixed tonne denominator is accepted at 1:1 — 'tCO2e/kilotonne' computes a 1000x over-report, 'tCO2e/megatonne' 1,000,000x
findings.boundary: Producer-supplied free text -> the regulated embedded-emissions figure. emission_data.emission_unit is an unconstrained text column crossing directly into the calculation engine.
findings.precondition: A producer (or an importer transcribing for an off-platform operator) types a magnitude-prefixed unit into the emission-data form's free-text unit field. The form's own placeholder is 'e.g. tCO2e/t', so this is a plausible typing error, not only an attack. The record then follows the ordinary verify -> share -> determine -> calculate path.
findings.affected_actor: The declarant and the regulator: a filed figure wrong by three or six orders of magnitude. Under a sharing grant this is cross-org — a producer's entry drives a different organisation's filing.
findings.exploit:
unitMatchesQuantityBasis (src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts:162-187) validates the numerator strictly and the denominator loosely:
  if (!/^TCO2E?(?:\/|_PER_|$)/.test(normalized)) return false;      // numerator: rejects KG/KT/G/LB prefixes
  return netMassTonnes !== null
    ? normalized.includes("TONNE") || /\/T(?![A-Z0-9])/.test(normalized)   // denominator: bare substring
    : normalized.includes("MWH");
'TCO2E/KILOTONNE'.includes('TONNE') is true. So is 'TCO2E/MEGATONNE', 'TCO2E/DECITONNE', 'TCO2E_PER_KILOTONNE'. Each is then multiplied against a quantity expressed in TONNES with no conversion.
1. Producer records direct 1.5 / indirect 0.5 with emission_unit 'tCO2e/kilotonne' (true intensity: 2 tCO2e per 1000 t = 0.002 tCO2e/t).
2. Importer determines a 1000 t line from it.
3. Engine returns 2000 tCO2e. The correct figure is 2. Factor 1000.
findings.evidence:
Exercising the guard's exact source (extracted verbatim):
"tCO2e/t"              massBasisAccepted= true
"tCO2e/kilotonne"      massBasisAccepted= true      <-- 1000x
"tCO2e/megatonne"      massBasisAccepted= true      <-- 1,000,000x
"tCO2e/decitonne"      massBasisAccepted= true      <-- 10x low
"tCO2e/hundredtonne"   massBasisAccepted= true
"tCO2e / kilotonne"    massBasisAccepted= true      (whitespace normalisation carries it through)
"TCO2E_PER_KILOTONNE"  massBasisAccepted= true
"kgCO2e/t"             massBasisAccepted= false     (numerator: correctly rejected)
"tCO2/TJ"              massBasisAccepted= false     (correctly rejected)

Real engine, 1000 t, direct 1.5 / indirect 0.5:
kilotonne denominator, 1.5/0.5 tCO2e/kilotonne, sector CEMENT -> COMPUTED 2000
tonne denominator control, 1.5/0.5 tCO2e/t, sector CEMENT     -> COMPUTED 2000
megatonne denominator                                          -> COMPUTED 2000
decitonne denominator                                          -> COMPUTED 2000
Identical output for four units spanning seven orders of magnitude.

Nothing constrains the column:
$ psql "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/p14_review_sandbox" -tAc "select conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where conrelid='public.emission_data'::regclass and contype='c';"
-> nine CHECK constraints returned, covering direct_specific/indirect_specific format and sign, methodology, reporting_period_kind, reporting_period_quarter, status, verification_status, verified_has_verifier, version. There is NO constraint on emission_unit.

Contrast the regulatory table, which does constrain it:
$ psql ... -tAc "select conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where conrelid='public.default_emission_values'::regclass and contype='c';"
default_emission_values_emission_unit_check|CHECK ((emission_unit = ANY (ARRAY['TCO2E_PER_TONNE'::text, 'TCO2_PER_MWH'::text])))

And the DB determination validator only checks the string ROUND-TRIPS, never that it is a sane unit:
  v_ed.emission_unit is not distinct from (v_snapshot->>'emission_unit')
findings.why_controls_fail: This is the exact symmetric twin of a defect the P13 audit already found and fixed, and the fix stopped halfway. The comment at :171-180 describes hardening the NUMERATOR against magnitude prefixes ('kgCO2e/t ... overstating embedded emissions 1000x ... so KGCO2E/T / KTCO2E/T / GCO2E/T / LBCO2E/T are rejected outright') and the test at calculate-line-emissions.test.ts:523-548 pins exactly those numerator cases. Nobody applied the same reasoning to the denominator, and no test covers it: grep for kilotonne|megatonne|/kt across the engine's test file returns nothing. The function's own doc comment even names the real fix ('an allow-list on EmissionData.emission_unit at entry (a DB CHECK or a small enum, mirroring default_emission_values' own constraint)') and describes itself as 'a stop-gap until that lands' — the candidate ships the stop-gap.
findings.impact: A filed CBAM figure wrong by 1000x or 1,000,000x from a single free-text field, with no constraint, no validation and no test standing in the way. At 1000x the declarant is billed for certificates against emissions three orders of magnitude larger than reality; the decitonne case runs the same mechanism 10x in the under-reporting direction. Because the field is producer-entered and crosses a sharing grant, one organisation's typo silently corrupts another organisation's regulatory submission.
findings.recommendation: Land the allow-list the code itself prescribes: a CHECK constraint on emission_data.emission_unit mirroring default_emission_values_emission_unit_check, plus a closed enum in recordEmissionData, so the engine stops sniffing free text. If a constraint cannot be added before release, at minimum anchor the denominator the way the numerator already is — require the denominator to be exactly T or TONNE(S) with no leading magnitude character — and add the missing test cases. Do not ship a guard that treats seven orders of magnitude as equivalent.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: An ACTUAL determination's reporting period is never checked against the shipment's, is not frozen in the snapshot, and the staleness monitor then reports the mismatch as CURRENT
findings.boundary: Reporting-period boundary between emission_data (installation, period) and the shipment/declaration being filed for a period. Crosses organisations whenever the data arrives through a sharing grant.
findings.precondition: An installation has verified ACTIVE emission_data for more than one reporting period — which the schema explicitly anticipates (emission_data_one_active_per_installation_period_uq is keyed on installation + period). An importer picks the wrong one. No elevated role, no forgery: the picker offers them all.
findings.affected_actor: The regulator and the filing — a period's declaration carries another period's emissions intensity — and the producer, whose figures are attributed to a year they do not describe.
findings.exploit:
There is no period check at any of the four places one could exist, and the fourth actively misreports:
1. PICKER — src/application/emissions/list-available-actual-data.ts:256-262 filters only `.eq("status","ACTIVE").eq("verification_status","VERIFIED")`. No period predicate. The record's period is attached at :504 purely as a display string (`reporting_period: record.period`) and rendered as a label (emissions-cell.tsx:121).
2. WRITE PATH — src/application/emissions/determine-from-actual-data.ts checks capability, org, status, verification, evidence completeness, verifier presence, cn_scope coverage (:494), installation provenance and no-op equality. `grep -n -i "period" determine-from-actual-data.ts` returns three hits, all of them a type import or an unrelated word in a comment. Zero period logic.
3. FROZEN SNAPSHOT — ActualEmissionSnapshot (src/domain/emissions/types.ts:107-158) has emission_data_id, version, installation_id, resolved_at, values, unit, methodology, verification, evidence, sharing_grant_id, record_provenance. It has NO period field, although the source EmissionData does (`period: ReportingPeriod`, :191). The mismatch is therefore not merely unblocked, it is unrecoverable after the fact from the snapshot alone.
4. DB VALIDATOR — app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record takes (p_determination, p_org_id, p_cn_code, p_origin_country, p_production_route_indicator). No period parameter exists, so the database cannot check it even in principle.
5. STALENESS MONITOR — this is the part that turns a gap into an affirmative false statement. check-actual-determination-staleness.ts:169-176 looks up the current ACTIVE record by the SHIPMENT'S period; checkActualSnapshotStaleness (src/domain/emissions/check-actual-snapshot-staleness.ts:48-63) then returns CURRENT when that lookup is null, and otherwise compares only installation_id and version. An out-of-period determination therefore reports CURRENT — the UI affirms the number is up to date.
6. Worse, when the shipment's period DOES have its own ACTIVE row, the comparison `currentEmissionData.version > snapshot.emission_data_version` runs ACROSS TWO DIFFERENT LINEAGES. Versions are only monotonic within an (installation, period) lineage — the function's own doc comment says so — so comparing a 2026 row's version to a 2025 snapshot's version is meaningless. It will report STALE against an unrelated record, or CURRENT against a period-correct record it should have flagged. The function guards installation_id but not emission_data_id or period.
findings.evidence:
Live against the sandbox, using a real 2025 record present in the data:
$ psql "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/p14_review_sandbox" -f actual.sql
BEGIN
SET   (set local role authenticated)
SET   (set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"7329fb81-8a00-4db0-818a-183957fd728c","role":"authenticated"}')
         fact         |    value
----------------------+-------------
 emission_data period | ANNUAL 2025

                             fact                             | value
--------------------------------------------------------------+-------
 validator accepts ACTUAL determination from this 2025 record | true
ROLLBACK

(The call was app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record(<snapshot for emission_data aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000001>, 'c7b4fb24-e0dc-4e86-94f1-087d6705e5a2', '72061000', 'CN', null) -> true. The record's own row: cn_scope {72061000}, ANNUAL 2025, direct 0.10 / indirect 0.05, tCO2e/t, version 1, evidence present, provenance OPERATOR_PROVIDED.)

The picker's only filters, verbatim from src/application/emissions/list-available-actual-data.ts:256-262:
      .from("emission_data")
      .select(EMISSION_DATA_COLUMNS)
      .eq("status", "ACTIVE")
      .eq("verification_status", "VERIFIED")
      .order("created_at", { ascending: false });

The staleness comparison, verbatim from src/domain/emissions/check-actual-snapshot-staleness.ts:48-63:
  if (currentEmissionData === null) { return "CURRENT"; }
  if (currentEmissionData.installation_id !== snapshot.installation_id) { return "CURRENT"; }
  return currentEmissionData.version > snapshot.emission_data_version ? "STALE" : "CURRENT";
findings.why_controls_fail: The period concept is present and load-bearing everywhere ELSE in the system — shipments, declarations, emission_data all carry reporting_period_kind/year/quarter, the draft generator filters members by period, and the staleness query itself filters by period — which is precisely why its absence here reads as an oversight rather than a decision. The staleness module's own doc comment (:51-53) states 'All of a shipment's lines share the SAME shipment-level period', and describes currentEmissionData as 'the current ACTIVE row for the SNAPSHOT'S own (installation_id, reporting_period)' — but the snapshot has no period, so its only caller substitutes the shipment's. The domain function's stated contract is violated by its sole caller, and the result is a green 'current' badge on a wrong-period figure. The DB validator, which is otherwise the strongest control in this codebase, cannot help: period is not among its parameters.
findings.impact: A declaration for one reporting period can be built entirely from another period's emissions intensities, with no blocker, no warning, and an affirmative 'current' indication in the UI. Because the period is not frozen into the snapshot, an already-filed mismatch cannot be detected from the archived determination at all — the evidence needed to find or correct it is simply not recorded. Magnitude is unbounded: it is whatever the difference between two years' intensities happens to be, in either direction.
findings.recommendation: Three changes, all small: (a) add `period: ReportingPeriod` to ActualEmissionSnapshot and freeze it — without this, existing mismatches cannot be found, only future ones prevented; (b) filter the picker by the shipment's period and reject a cross-period determineFromActualData at commit time with its own named reason (not folded into EMISSION_DATA_NOT_FOUND — the user needs to know why); (c) fix checkActualSnapshotStaleness to compare the snapshot's own frozen period and emission_data lineage, not just installation_id, so the version comparison stops crossing lineages. Add the period to the DB validator's signature so the database is a second wall here as it is elsewhere. A backfill query over existing determinations is needed to find any already-filed mismatch.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: Rolling the application back to the recorded known-good SHA after this release permanently breaks every calculation write, and ROLLBACK.md's confirmation procedure reports success
findings.boundary: Release / rollback procedure: old application code (95c95bb) against the post-pending-set database schema.
findings.precondition: The 11 pending migrations are pushed to production (DEPLOYMENT.md step 4), then the application is rolled back to the recorded rollback target — ROLLBACK.md §1's entire subject. No attacker required.
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant of the deployed system. The core product action (computing and persisting embedded emissions for a shipment line) stops working for everyone, with no user-visible cause.
findings.exploit:
1. Push the pending set. 20260903190000 executes `drop policy if exists calculation_results_insert_own_org_as_self on public.calculation_results` and `revoke insert, update, delete on public.calculation_results from anon, authenticated`, moving writes to record_calculation_result(...) granted to service_role alone.
2. Follow ROLLBACK.md §1 and redeploy the recorded known-good build. The deploy branch head, and thus the rollback target, is 95c95bb (P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:451, 'the deploy branch head'); `git ls-tree 95c95bb supabase/migrations/ --name-only | wc -l` = 63, exactly the 63 migrations production has applied.
3. That build writes the table directly as the signed-in `authenticated` role: `git show 95c95bb:src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts | grep -n 'from("calculation_results")'` -> `240:      .from("calculation_results")`.
4. Every calculation save now fails. ROLLBACK.md §1's 'Confirm the rollback succeeded' is `GET /api/health` -> status ok plus a git_sha match; both still pass, so the rollback is declared good.
findings.evidence:
Live reproduction against p14rev_a10_leak (a template clone of the review sandbox, i.e. the candidate schema), replaying the 95c95bb insert as an ordinary OWNER of the line's own organisation:

psql "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/p14rev_a10_leak" -c "
begin;
set local role authenticated;
set local request.jwt.claims = '{\"sub\":\"d7ffd167-fa3d-41f4-aada-d8069d847b23\",\"role\":\"authenticated\"}';
insert into public.calculation_results
    (org_id, line_id, shipment_id, engine_version, parameter_datasets,
     quantity, quantity_unit, determination, steps, embedded_emissions_tco2e,
     calculated_by_user_id, correlation_id)
select sl.org_id, sl.id, sl.shipment_id, 'v1', '[]'::jsonb,
       '1', 'TONNE', sl.emission_determination, '[]'::jsonb, '1',
       auth.uid(), gen_random_uuid()
from public.shipment_lines sl where sl.id = '3e76b531-516e-46b2-a735-f73895e32c62';
rollback;"

Exact output:
  BEGIN
  SET
  SET
  ERROR:  permission denied for table calculation_results
  HINT:  Grant the required privileges to the current role with: GRANT INSERT ON public.calculation_results TO authenticated;

Grant state confirming the cause, on the candidate schema:
psql "...p14_review_sandbox" -tAc "select grantee||' | '||privilege_type from information_schema.role_table_grants where table_schema='public' and table_name='calculation_results' and grantee in ('anon','authenticated') order by 1"
  anon | REFERENCES
  anon | SELECT
  anon | TRIGGER
  authenticated | REFERENCES
  authenticated | SELECT
  authenticated | TRIGGER

psql "...p14_review_sandbox" -tAc "select policyname||' | '||cmd from pg_policies where tablename='calculation_results'"
  calculation_results_select_own_org | SELECT

Source: supabase/migrations/20260903190000_p141_calculation_results_trusted_write_only.sql:144 (drop policy), :147 (revoke insert, update, delete), :357 (grant execute ... to service_role). Rollback target code: src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts:240 at 95c95bb.
findings.why_controls_fail: ROLLBACK.md's §2 states the correct rule — an application rollback is safe 'only when every migration applied since then was additive' — and instructs the operator to 'explicitly confirm the target commit's code is still compatible with the current schema' before rolling back past a destructive migration. But nothing in this release identifies 20260903190000 as that migration. It is not listed as destructive anywhere; DEPLOYMENT.md's promotion procedure step 6 says only 'Record the previous SHA as the rollback target'; and §42 escalation was not triggered for it because a REVOKE plus a DROP POLICY does not look like a schema-destructive change. The rollback's own success test (health 200 + git_sha match, ROLLBACK.md §1 items 1-2) is blind to it by construction, and item 3 ('the original incident's symptom is gone') would also pass, because the broken thing is a different feature from whatever prompted the rollback.
findings.impact: The rollback path this release depends on is not available. After the push, redeploying 95c95bb produces a system that passes every health signal the runbook checks while silently refusing to persist any emissions calculation — and since calculation_results feeds the declaration filing snapshot, no declaration can be advanced either. Recovery from a bad deploy would require an unplanned forward migration written under incident pressure.
findings.recommendation: Before shipping, record 20260903190000 in the release report as a NON-ADDITIVE migration and state explicitly that 95c95bb is no longer a valid rollback target once it is applied. Either (a) keep a compatibility shim for one release — retain the INSERT grant and policy alongside the RPC, and revoke them in a follow-up release after the new code is proven — which restores a genuine rollback path, or (b) declare the rollback target roll-forward-only for calculation writes and add a post-rollback smoke step that actually saves a calculation, since /api/health cannot see this.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: CHAIN C1 (COMPOSITE, PROVEN END TO END): a plain MEMBER files a declaration reporting 0 tCO2e for 1,000 tonnes of Chinese steel — #11 + the unchecked evidence array on INSERT + #26's prefix scope + a filing gate that asks none of the right questions
findings.boundary: role boundary inside a tenant (MEMBER -> the organisation's own filed regulatory record), and the platform -> regulator boundary. The declarant's immutable filed_snapshot is the artifact the product exists to produce.
findings.precondition: One ordinary MEMBER account in an importer/declarant organisation, its own session JWT, and the ability to issue raw PostgREST calls. No ADMIN, no OWNER, no service-role key, no counterparty, no forged token, no elevated grant. The ADMIN who files is honest and unaware.
findings.affected_actor: The declarant organisation itself, and the CBAM regulator receiving the figure. Own-tenant actor, but the harm lands on the regulatory record.
findings.exploit: 1. The MEMBER creates an IMPORTER_ENTERED operator and installation for their own org (permitted; enforce_record_provenance_capability only checks the org holds IMPORTER_DECLARANT). 2. One INSERT into emission_data with status='ACTIVE', verification_status='VERIFIED', verifier_user_id=<themselves>, direct_specific='0', indirect_specific='0', cn_scope='{7}', evidence_file_ids='{99999999-9999-9999-9999-999999999999}' — a UUID naming no evidence_files row at all. Every gate that would have stopped the equivalent UPDATE is a BEFORE UPDATE trigger. 3. PATCH the shipment line's emission_determination with an ACTUAL snapshot naming that record; app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record accepts it, because its evidence test is `coalesce(array_length(v_ed.evidence_file_ids,1),0) = 0` plus a set-equality against the snapshot — it never asks whether the ids resolve. 4. The application's own trusted channel does the rest: calculateLineEmissions returns 1000 * (0+0) = 0 and record_calculation_result (service_role) persists it. 5. An ADMIN marks the declaration READY and calls record_declaration_filed. OK.
findings.evidence:
Single transaction against p14_review_sandbox, rolled back, leakage verified as 0 afterwards (scratchpad/chain3.sql).

STEP 1 (as role authenticated, jwt sub a5e70000-...-0001, whose memberships row reads MEMBER):
  insert into public.emission_data (... status, verification_status, verifier_user_id, evidence_file_ids ...) values (..., 'ACTIVE','VERIFIED','a5e70000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001','{99999999-9999-9999-9999-999999999999}');
  -> INSERT 0 1
  id | status | verification_status | verifier_user_id | evidence_file_ids | direct_specific | indirect_specific | emission_unit | cn_scope
  05e70000-...-0001 | ACTIVE | VERIFIED | a5e70000-...-0001 | {99999999-...-9999} | 0 | 0 | tCO2e/t | {7}
  select count(*) as real_evidence_rows_backing_it from public.evidence_files where id='99999999-9999-9999-9999-999999999999'; -> 0

STEP 2: the determination validator accepted the ACTUAL snapshot naming that record -> `method_on_line = ACTUAL`.

STEP 3 (service_role, exactly as src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts:283-299 does):
  select * from public.record_calculation_result(...,'1000','TONNES',<the line's determination>,...,'0',...);
  -> result_status OK
  embedded_emissions_tco2e | quantity | quantity_unit | engine_version
  0                        | 1000     | TONNES        | 1.3.0

STEP 5 (as the ADMIN):
  select * from public.record_declaration_filed('d0000000-...-00c1','EU-CBAM-REF-2026Q1-0001');
  -> OK | d0000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1
  filed_snapshot->'totals' = {"line_count": 1, "shipment_count": 1, "embedded_emissions_tco2e": "0"}
  status = FILED_RECORDED

GROUND TRUTH FROM THE PLATFORM'S OWN ACTIVE DATASET:
  select dev.source_trade_code, c.name, dev.total_value, dev.emission_unit from default_emission_values dev join regulatory_datasets rd on rd.id=dev.dataset_id and rd.status='ACTIVE' join countries c on c.id=dev.country_id where dev.source_trade_code like '7208%' and c.iso2='CN' and dev.total_status='AVAILABLE';
  -> 7208 | China | 3.187 | TCO2E_PER_TONNE

1,000 t x 3.187 = 3,187 tCO2e. Filed: 0.

POST-ROLLBACK: leaked_decls 0, leaked_emission_data 0, leaked_orgs 0.
findings.why_controls_fail: Four controls each hold on their own and none of them is in this path. (a) app.enforce_emission_data_activation_gate and app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate are `BEFORE UPDATE ON public.emission_data` — I read pg_get_triggerdef for all four triggers on the table and there is no BEFORE INSERT trigger of any kind. (b) emission_data_insert_own_org's WITH CHECK is only `entered_by_org_id in (select app.user_org_ids()) and exists (select 1 from installations i where i.id = ... and i.org_id = ...)`; the evidence-existence anti-join that emission_data_update_own_org carries is absent from the INSERT side. (c) the CHECK constraint emission_data_verified_has_verifier_ck requires only that verifier_user_id be NON-NULL when VERIFIED — the caller supplies the value, and app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate's overwrite `new.verifier_user_id := auth.uid()` is on the UPDATE path only. (d) record_declaration_filed compares determination, quantity and quantity_unit against the line and refuses empty members — all of which are TRUE here, because the forged inputs are internally consistent. The gate verifies that the number was computed from the stated inputs; nothing verifies that the inputs are real.
findings.impact: A materially false CBAM declaration, immutable, with a complete and internally consistent audit trail (declaration.filed, shipment.locked, provenance.calculation_result_ids naming a real calculation row), produced by the lowest-privileged role in the organisation and signed off by an honest administrator. The understatement in the reproduction is total — 0 against 3,187 tCO2e — and the same INSERT sets any figure the attacker likes in either direction. Nothing in the product surfaces the forgery: no trigger audits emission_data writes, reproduceCalculationResult recomputes from the row's own frozen inputs and returns REPRODUCIBLE, and the evidence id resolves to nothing only if someone thinks to check.
findings.recommendation: Add a BEFORE INSERT arm to both gates (or a single BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger) so a row can only be born DRAFT/UNVERIFIED, and move the verifier_user_id := auth.uid() overwrite there too. Add the evidence-existence anti-join from emission_data_update_own_org to emission_data_insert_own_org. Independently, make evidence_file_ids a uuid[] with an FK-equivalent constraint rather than text[], so a fabricated id cannot be stored at all. Then write the INSERT-driven twin of every case in tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts, whose ~12 cases all drive UPDATE.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: CHAIN C2 (COMPOSITE, PROVEN LIVE, CROSS-TENANT): a producer MEMBER displaces the ADMIN-verified emission record with a 98.6%-lower forgery stamped with the ADMIN's own user id, and the counterparty importer cannot tell — #11 + #17 + #26
findings.boundary: The cross-organisation trust boundary the whole product rests on: 'ACTIVE + VERIFIED means an ADMIN of the operating installation verified this against real evidence.' Grantor org -> grantee org, through sharing_grants.
findings.precondition: One MEMBER account in a producer/operator organisation that has at least one installation already shared with an importer under an ACTIVE sharing grant — the ordinary commercial relationship the product is built to support. No ADMIN, no OWNER, no cross-tenant credential.
findings.affected_actor: The counterparty importer, a DIFFERENT tenant, who consumes the figure and files it. Secondarily the producer's own ADMIN, whose identity is attached to a record they never saw.
findings.exploit: 1. UPDATE the genuine ACTIVE+VERIFIED record to status='DISCARDED'. Permitted: emission_data_update_own_org requires only org membership, and app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate's un-verify guard and DRAFT guard are both keyed on `old.status = 'ACTIVE'` with `new.status = 'DRAFT'` — DISCARD is explicitly unaffected, as that migration's own comment says. 2. INSERT a replacement with version=2 and predecessor_id naming the genuine record (needed only because emission_data_version_uq is real), status='ACTIVE', verification_status='VERIFIED', verifier_user_id = the ADMIN's uuid, evidence_file_ids reusing the genuine record's real evidence file, and cn_scope broadened to '{7}'. 3. The one-ACTIVE-per-installation-period unique index is now satisfied by the forgery instead of the genuine record, so the grantee's emission_data_select_own_org (`shared installation AND status='ACTIVE' AND verification_status='VERIFIED'`) returns exactly one row: the forgery.
findings.evidence:
Single transaction against p14_review_sandbox, rolled back, leakage verified 0 (scratchpad/chainB3.sql).

WHAT THE IMPORTER SAW BEFORE (as role authenticated, jwt sub a9000000-...-0003, ADMIN of the grantee org):
  id | direct_specific | indirect_specific | verification_status | status | evidence_count
  f9000000-...-000a | 3.100 | 0.500 | VERIFIED | ACTIVE | 1
(that record was verified by a9000000-...-0002, an ADMIN, and backed by evidence_files row f9000000-...-00e1, 'verifier-report.pdf', sha256 cccc...)

THE ATTACK (as role authenticated, jwt sub a9000000-...-0001):
  select role from public.memberships where user_id=auth.uid(); -> MEMBER
  update public.emission_data set status='DISCARDED' where id='f9000000-...-000a'; -> UPDATE 1
  insert into public.emission_data (..., verification_status, verifier_user_id, evidence_file_ids, status, version, predecessor_id) values (..., 'VERIFIED','a9000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002','{f9000000-...-00e1}','ACTIVE',2,'f9000000-...-000a'); -> INSERT 0 1

WHAT THE IMPORTER SEES AFTER:
  id | direct_specific | indirect_specific | verification_status | status | verifier_user_id | cn_scope
  f9000000-...-000b | 0.050 | 0.000 | VERIFIED | ACTIVE | a9000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002 | {7}

3.600 t/t of combined specific emissions replaced by 0.050 — a 98.6% reduction — attributed to the producer's ADMIN, on a scope entry that now covers every CN code beginning with 7. Verified separately: app.code_prefix_covers('7','72081000') -> t, ('7','76011000') -> t, and there are zero CHECK constraints on emission_data mentioning cn_scope.

A WALL THAT DID HOLD, worth stating: my first attempt without version=2 failed on `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "emission_data_version_uq"`.
findings.why_controls_fail: The verification gate's own comment states its purpose — 'an ACTIVE, VERIFIED record cannot be un-verified. Importers may already have frozen its evidence set into a determination.' It is keyed on `old.status = 'ACTIVE'`, so DISCARD walks out from under it, and the INSERT arm does not exist at all, so a fresh ACTIVE+VERIFIED row walks back in. The record_provenance check added by owner decision D2 verifies that the snapshot's provenance matches the INSTALLATION's provenance — it is OPERATOR_PROVIDED, truthfully, because the installation genuinely belongs to the producer. Every field the validator cross-checks (methodology, installation_id, version, evidence set, verifier_user_id, the numbers themselves) is checked against the forged row, which is self-consistent by construction. The grantee has no way to see the DISCARDED predecessor: emission_data_select_own_org admits shared rows only at ACTIVE+VERIFIED.
findings.impact: The single trust claim the sharing model exists to carry is manufacturable by the lowest-privileged member of the producer org, and lands in the counterparty's tenancy indistinguishable from the real thing. The importer then determines, calculates and files against it — chaining directly into C1's filing path. This is a producer under-reporting to its own customer's regulator, with the customer as the unwitting filer and the producer's own administrator named as verifier.
findings.recommendation: Same INSERT-side gates as C1. Additionally: forbid ACTIVE -> DISCARDED for a record referenced by any counterparty's frozen determination, or make DISCARD of an ACTIVE+VERIFIED record ADMIN-only, mirroring the verify path. Constrain cn_scope elements with a CHECK (minimum length, digits only) and reject the empty string outright.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The Annex II sector proxy drops up to 50.0% of the published emissions total for CN 2601 12 00, and the platform's own ACTIVE regulatory dataset is the proof — no attacker, ordinary supported workflow (prior #23, HIGH -> BLOCKER)
findings.boundary: Platform -> regulator. This is the regulated figure itself, produced by the trusted path from honest data.
findings.precondition: None adversarial. A producer records a verified emission_data row whose cn_scope covers 26011200; an importer with a sharing grant determines a line ACTUAL and calculates. Every actor behaves correctly.
findings.affected_actor: Every declarant filing an ACTUAL-method line on agglomerated iron ores and concentrates, and the regulator.
findings.exploit: No exploit. calculate-line.ts:215-223 resolves good_sector from cbam_goods for the line's cn_code; 26011200 is registered as sector IRON_STEEL; ANNEX_II_SECTORS in src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts:46-52 contains IRON_STEEL, so the direct-only branch fires at :298-300 and indirect_specific is excluded from the filed figure. For the identical good and origin, the DEFAULT path uses the dataset's `total`, which includes that indirect component. The two paths therefore disagree by the whole indirect share.
findings.evidence:
Measured against the ACTIVE dataset in p14_review_sandbox.

The good is declarable:
  select trade_code, sector, record_level, functional_unit, active_from, active_to from cbam_goods where trade_code='26011200';
  -> 26011200 | IRON_STEEL | TRADE_GOOD | TONNES | 2026-01-01 | (null)

The only IRON_STEEL code in the ACTIVE dataset carrying a published indirect value is this one:
  select distinct dev.source_trade_code from default_emission_values dev join regulatory_datasets rd on rd.id=dev.dataset_id and rd.status='ACTIVE' join cbam_goods g on regexp_replace(g.trade_code,'\s','','g')=regexp_replace(dev.source_trade_code,'\s','','g') where g.sector='IRON_STEEL' and dev.indirect_status='AVAILABLE';
  -> 2601 12 00

Sector-by-indirect_status census (my own run; note the prior finding's table omitted four rows — CEMENT|UNAVAILABLE|471, FERTILISERS|REFERENCE_REQUIRED|182, FERTILISERS|UNAVAILABLE|41 — but its load-bearing row, IRON_STEEL|AVAILABLE|28 with 28 non-zero, is exact):
  ALUMINIUM|UNAVAILABLE|1632|0 ; CEMENT|AVAILABLE|337|326 ; CEMENT|UNAVAILABLE|471|0 ; FERTILISERS|AVAILABLE|2416|2416 ; FERTILISERS|REFERENCE_REQUIRED|182|0 ; FERTILISERS|UNAVAILABLE|41|0 ; HYDROGEN|UNAVAILABLE|96|0 ; IRON_STEEL|AVAILABLE|28|28 ; IRON_STEEL|REFERENCE_REQUIRED|688|0 ; IRON_STEEL|UNAVAILABLE|6649|0

The share of the published total that the proxy discards, worst first:
  country | direct | indirect | total | pct of total dropped
  Kazakhstan            | 0.170 | 0.170 | 0.340 | 50.0
  Serbia                | 0.120 | 0.110 | 0.220 | 50.0
  Bosnia and Herzegovina| 0.090 | 0.090 | 0.190 | 47.4
  Uzbekistan            | 0.390 | 0.350 | 0.740 | 47.3
  Azerbaijan            | 0.070 | 0.050 | 0.120 | 41.7
(all TCO2E_PER_TONNE, dataset 2026-definitive-corrected, status ACTIVE)
findings.why_controls_fail: There is no control. The file's own comment (:74-86) states the risk in plain terms — 'while the proxy REFUSED, its imprecision was conservative ... Now that the proxy APPLIES an exclusion, the same imprecision points the other way: such a good would have its indirect emissions excluded and would be UNDER-reported' — and ships anyway. docs/regulatory/CALCULATION_RULE_REGISTER.md RULE-EE-004's stated applicability ('total_emissions should already equal direct-only, with no indirect component, at the source') is true for 8,129 of 8,157 AVAILABLE rows in those sectors and FALSE for exactly the 28 rows of this good. The engine records an ANNEX_II_DIRECT_ONLY trace step naming good_sector, so the exclusion is auditable after the fact — but nothing refuses, warns, or surfaces the ambiguity.
findings.impact: Systematic under-reporting of a regulated figure by up to half, for a good the platform ships as declarable from 2026-01-01, with a complete and internally consistent trace attesting to the omission. Under-reporting is the direction that matters for a compliance filing. I upgrade this from the prior HIGH because it needs no attacker, no raw API, and no unusual configuration: it is what the product does when used correctly.
findings.recommendation: Escalate to the owner (CLAUDE.md's 'material regulatory behavior change'). The correct fix is the versioned Annex II membership dataset the register already says was never transcribed. Until it exists, the platform must not resolve the ambiguity in the under-reporting direction: revert to refusing (PARAMETER_DATASET_UNAVAILABLE) for any sector-proxied good whose ACTIVE-dataset row carries a non-zero indirect component, which is a query the platform can already answer. Do not hardcode a code list here — CLAUDE.md's facts-as-datasets rule forbids it.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: NEW: emission_data's INSERT policy never checks that evidence_file_ids name real evidence_files rows — which is precisely what defeats the determination validator's 'evidence present' test
findings.boundary: Role boundary within a tenant, and the cross-tenant evidence-provenance boundary. This is a distinct hole from the status/verification bypass and survives fixing it if fixed in isolation.
findings.precondition: Any member who can insert an emission_data row for their own installation.
findings.affected_actor: The counterparty importer, the auditor reading a filed declaration's provenance chain, and the regulator.
findings.exploit: Set evidence_file_ids to any array of UUID-shaped strings. The column is text[] with no CHECK, no FK, and no policy-level existence test on the INSERT side. app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record's ACTUAL branch tests only `coalesce(array_length(v_ed.evidence_file_ids,1),0) = 0` (non-empty) and set-equality between the snapshot's array and the row's array. Both pass on fabricated ids, so the forged record satisfies the evidence requirement without a single byte of evidence existing.
findings.evidence:
Live, in the C1 reproduction (rolled back):
  evidence_file_ids on the accepted, ACTIVE+VERIFIED row: {99999999-9999-9999-9999-999999999999}
  select count(*) as real_evidence_rows_backing_it from public.evidence_files where id='99999999-9999-9999-9999-999999999999'; -> 0
  and the ACTUAL determination naming that record was accepted onto the shipment line (method_on_line = ACTUAL).

The asymmetry, from pg_policy on emission_data: the UPDATE policy's WITH CHECK carries the full anti-join against evidence_files (quoted in full in the preceding finding); the INSERT policy's WITH CHECK does not mention evidence_files at all.

Column type confirmed from information_schema.columns: `evidence_file_ids ARRAY '{}'::text[] null=NO` — text, not uuid, so any string is storable.
findings.why_controls_fail: The validator was written to defend against a forged SNAPSHOT diverging from a real RECORD, and it does that well — it binds emission_unit, both figures, methodology, installation, version, provenance, verifier and the evidence set. It never asks whether the record's own evidence set is real, because the INSERT policy was assumed to guarantee that; it does not, and only the UPDATE policy does. 20260829560000's evidence_files DELETE lock protects existing evidence rows from removal, which is a different question from whether they ever existed.
findings.impact: A filed CBAM declaration's provenance chain can point at evidence documents that were never uploaded and never existed. An auditor following the chain finds nothing, with no indication of when or how it was lost — indistinguishable from ordinary data loss.
findings.recommendation: Add the anti-join to emission_data_insert_own_org. Separately, change the column to uuid[] and enforce referential integrity properly (a trigger, since Postgres has no array FK) rather than relying on two policies to agree.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The frozen candidate cannot pass its own CI: the fast-gates secret scan exits 1 at cad99adb
findings.boundary: Release certification gate — the CI job that decides whether a commit is shippable
findings.precondition: None. Push cad99adb (or open a PR from it). This is the frozen candidate's own tree, unmodified.
findings.affected_actor: The release process and anyone relying on a green CI run as evidence the candidate was certified.
findings.exploit: 1. Check out cad99adb (clean tree, verified: `git status --porcelain` empty, `git rev-parse HEAD` = cad99adbc...). 2. Run the exact fast-gates step body from ci.yml:110-117. 3. It matches four lines of docs/plans/P14_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.json, prints ::error::, and exits 1. The offending substrings are the PRIOR REVIEW'S OWN fabricated demonstration strings, committed as documentation in cad99adb itself (`git log --oneline -1 -- docs/plans/P14_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.json` -> cad99ad).
findings.evidence:
Script (verbatim from ci.yml:111-117, with `cut -c1-160` added only to shorten the printed lines):
  set -euo pipefail
  PATTERN='eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|re_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|sb_(publishable|secret)_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}'
  if git grep -InE "$PATTERN" -- . ':!pnpm-lock.yaml' ':!.github/workflows/ci.yml' | grep -vF 'eyJpc3MiOiJzdXBhYmFzZS1kZW1vIiwicm9sZSI6' | cut -c1-160; then
    echo "::error::Possible committed secret found."; exit 1; fi
  echo "Secret scan clean."
Output:
  docs/plans/P14_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.json:1063: ...
  docs/plans/P14_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.json:1074: ...
  docs/plans/P14_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.json:1080: ...
  docs/plans/P14_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.json:1086: ...
  ::error::Possible committed secret found.
  FG_EXIT=1
The actual matched substrings, extracted with `git grep -hInE '<PATTERN>' -- docs/plans/P14_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.json | grep -oE '<PATTERN>' | sort -u`:
  eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9abcdefghijklmnop
  sb_secret_abcdefghijklmnop
File tracked at HEAD: `git ls-files --error-unmatch docs/plans/P14_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.json` -> TRACKED.
findings.why_controls_fail: There is no control here to fail — this IS the control, and it is red. The reason nobody noticed is the second half of the picture: the OTHER secret scan, in build-and-test (ci.yml:497-610), holds a superset pattern that also matches both strings, yet reports green because it is dead (see the next finding). So the workflow's two secret scans disagree about the same commit: one red, one green. Reading only the build-and-test log — which is what §22's certification table quotes ('No secret-shaped literals found in tracked files.') — gives exactly the wrong answer.
findings.impact: There is no green CI run for the frozen candidate, so any claim that this commit passed its gates is false. Worse, the failure is triggered by review documentation rather than by a secret, which creates direct pressure to weaken the scan a third time (the first two weakenings — the ':!*.md' exclusion and the KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT filter — are how the gate got into its current state). Fixing this by excluding docs/ would restore the exact hole the P13 audit removed.
findings.recommendation: Do not exclude docs/ or *.json. Either (a) rewrite the two demonstration strings in P14_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.json so they are not secret-shaped (e.g. 'eyJ<...redacted...>' ), or (b) add them as two exact, fixed KNOWN_SAFE_ literals the same way the demo JWT and local PG URL are allowlisted. Then re-run the step and confirm it prints 'Secret scan clean.' with exit 0 before certifying anything.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: build-and-test's secret scan is dead and FAILS OPEN: it reports clean and exits 0 while holding real matches
findings.boundary: Committed-credential gate on every branch push and PR
findings.precondition: None. The defect fires on every run of the build-and-test job, unconditionally, since commit 464d6d8 (2026-09-03).
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant and the regulator, if a service-role key or database password ever reaches a tracked file: this is the only step that would have caught it.
findings.exploit: Commit any file containing a service-role JWT, a `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=<real password>` line, or a `postgres://user:password@host` URL. ci.yml:583-592 captures it correctly into RAW_MATCHES and GIT_GREP_EXIT=0. Then ci.yml:599-602 expands `$KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT`, which is never assigned anywhere in the file — only KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_DEMO_JWT and KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_PG_URL are. Under `set -u` (ci.yml:499) the command substitution's subshell dies on a FATAL shell error, which `||` cannot intercept, so MATCHES becomes the empty string regardless of what RAW_MATCHES held. The `if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]` at 604 is false, and 610 prints success.
findings.evidence:
Reproduction script (structure copied verbatim from ci.yml:599-610), run with bash:
  set -euo pipefail
  RAW_MATCHES="secret-line-one\nsecret-line-two"
  KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_DEMO_JWT='zzz'; KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_PG_URL='yyy'
  MATCHES="$(printf '%s\n' "$RAW_MATCHES" | grep -vF "$KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_DEMO_JWT" | grep -vF "$KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_PG_URL" | grep -vE "$KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT" || true)"
  echo "REACHED-AFTER-ASSIGNMENT MATCHES=[$MATCHES]"
  if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then echo "$MATCHES"; echo '::error::Possible secret literal found'; exit 1; fi
  echo "No secret-shaped literals found in tracked files."
Exact output:
  <script>: line 10: KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT: unbound variable
  REACHED-AFTER-ASSIGNMENT MATCHES=[]
  No secret-shaped literals found in tracked files.
  EXIT=0
The two secret lines were present in RAW_MATCHES and were silently discarded. Variable never defined: `grep -n KNOWN_SAFE .github/workflows/ci.yml` yields definitions only at the DEMO_JWT and PG_URL lines; the sole occurrence of KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT is its USE at ci.yml:602. Introduced by `git log -S 'KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT' -- .github/workflows/ci.yml` -> 464d6d8 ("ci: stop the secret scan failing on two lines that contain no secret").
findings.why_controls_fail: The step's own 30-line comment at ci.yml:570-582 documents having ALREADY fixed a fail-open bug of exactly this shape ('this security gate quietly becoming a no-op on its own future edit') by splitting git grep out and checking GIT_GREP_EXIT explicitly. That fix is intact and works — and it is bypassed, because the reintroduced hole is downstream of it, in the filter pipeline the same `|| true` still guards. The unbound-variable diagnostic does print to the job log's stderr, but the step is green, so nothing surfaces it. Note also that naively defining the variable as an empty string would NOT fix it: `grep -vE ''` matches every line and inverts to zero output, leaving MATCHES empty just the same.
findings.impact: Since 464d6d8 no push has been scanned by the thorough pattern. Combined with the next finding, the shapes this scan uniquely covers — `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=`/`ANON_KEY=`/`SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=` assignments and raw `postgres://user:pass@host` strings — are covered by nothing at all. A leaked service-role key grants unrestricted, RLS-bypassing read/write across every tenant's emissions, shipments and declarations.
findings.recommendation: Define KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT explicitly (the intended value, per 464d6d8's message, anchors on the `process.env.` prefix and a trailing semicolon), and add a self-test to the step so it can never silently become a no-op again: pipe a known secret-shaped fixture through the same filter chain and assert it survives, failing the step if it does not. Do not rely on `set -u` catching this — as proved above, inside `$(...)` it does not fail the step.

findings.title: No INSERT gate on emission_data: a plain MEMBER manufactures an ACTIVE + VERIFIED operator-attested record and drives it end to end into a trusted calculation result
findings.boundary: Organisation membership role boundary (MEMBER vs ADMIN/OWNER) and the producer -> importer sharing boundary. Also the regulator-facing boundary: the resulting figure is what gets calculated and filed.
findings.precondition: One ordinary, non-admin MEMBER account in a PRODUCER_OPERATOR organisation that owns at least one installation, and an ACTIVE sharing grant to an importer — i.e. the entirely normal state of any producer using the product. No admin action, no stolen credential, no service_role key. The member needs only their own JWT against the public PostgREST endpoint.
findings.affected_actor: Cross-tenant. The grantee importer organisation consumes fabricated emissions as verified operator data and files on it; the regulator receives a false CBAM figure attributed to a named verifier and to evidence that does not exist. The producer's own ADMIN/OWNER are also bypassed — their verification authority is simply not consulted.
findings.evidence:
Step 3 -> `INSERT 0 1`, then `select id,status,verification_status,verifier_user_id,evidence_file_ids,direct_specific from emission_data where id='5555...e1'` -> `5555...e1 | ACTIVE | VERIFIED | 1111...0005 | {aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee} | 0.0000001`. Corroborating: `select count(*) from evidence_files where emission_data_id='5555...e1'` -> `0`; `select count(*) from memberships where user_id='1111...0005' and org_id='2222...0001'` -> `0`.
Step 4 -> as importer: `importer sees | 5555...e1 | 0.0000001 | VERIFIED | ACTIVE | 1111...0005`.
Step 6 -> `UPDATE 1`, `COMMIT`, then `DETERMINATION PERSISTED | ACTUAL | | OPERATOR_PROVIDED | {"direct_specific": "0.0000001", "indirect_specific": "0.0000001"} | {"status": "VERIFIED", "verifier_user_id": "1111...0005"}`.
Step 7 -> `result_status | result_calculation_id` = `OK | 176c83fc-0e1a-4490-b5db-63afa220a9ea`, and `select embedded_emissions_tco2e, quantity, determination->'snapshot'->>'record_provenance' from calculation_results where line_id='8888...0001'` -> `0.0001 | 1000 | OPERATOR_PROVIDED`.
Root cause, measured not assumed — trigger inventory with timing/event decoded from pg_trigger.tgtype:
  emission_data_activation_gate_trg     | BEFORE | UPDATE
  emission_data_prevent_fact_change_trg | BEFORE | UPDATE
  emission_data_touch_updated_at_trg    | BEFORE | UPDATE
  emission_data_verification_gate_trg   | BEFORE | UPDATE
Four triggers, zero on INSERT. And the INSERT policy, from pg_policy: `emission_data_insert_own_org | a | with check ((entered_by_org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids())) AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM installations i WHERE i.id = emission_data.installation_id AND i.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id)))` — no clause mentions status, verification_status, verifier_user_id or evidence_file_ids. Policy source: supabase/migrations/20260829230000_p7b_emission_data_schema.sql:399, never narrowed since.
findings.why_controls_fail:
Every control that would have stopped this is an UPDATE-path control, and this write is an INSERT.
(1) `app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate` — the ADMIN/OWNER check, the verifier_user_id := auth.uid() overwrite, the un-verify block, the evidence-shrink block — is attached BEFORE UPDATE only, and its body dereferences OLD throughout, so it could not have been attached to INSERT without rewriting. It never runs here.
(2) `app.enforce_emission_data_activation_gate` ('a record may only transition to ACTIVE from DRAFT while verification_status = VERIFIED and evidence_file_ids is non-empty') is BEFORE UPDATE and keyed on `new.status is distinct from old.status`. A row born ACTIVE never transitions to ACTIVE.
(3) The CHECK constraints are the only INSERT-time controls, and the only relevant one is `emission_data_verified_has_verifier_ck` — `verification_status <> 'VERIFIED' OR verifier_user_id IS NOT NULL`. It requires that a verifier be *named*, not that they have any authority: verifier_user_id's only other constraint is an FK to auth.users, so any user in the system, in any organisation, satisfies it (confirmed: 1111...0005 has zero memberships in the entering org).
(4) The application layer is correct and irrelevant. `recordEmissionData` (src/application/emissions/manage-emission-data.ts:307-327) never sends status or verification_status, so the columns rest at their DRAFT/UNVERIFIED defaults on the honest path — which is exactly why nobody noticed the defaults are the *only* thing holding the line. The attacker does not call the application.
(5) `app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record` — the wall that should have caught the forged record downstream — checks status='ACTIVE', verification_status='VERIFIED', `array_length(evidence_file_ids,1) <> 0`, and an ACTIVE sharing grant. All four are true of the forged row. It never checks that the evidence ids resolve to `evidence_files` rows (it compares the snapshot array to the emission_data array, i.e. one unverified claim against another), and it never checks that verifier_user_id is a member of the entering org, let alone an ADMIN.
(6) P14.1's `record_calculation_result` binds `p_determination` to the line's current `emission_determination` byte-for-byte — which is the forged determination. Its stated invariant ('a user cannot cause a persisted calculation result containing an emissions value the trusted path did not produce') holds literally and is worthless here: the trusted path produced the number faithfully from forged inputs.
(7) `checkEmissionDataEvidenceCompleteness` (src/domain/emissions/snapshot-completeness.ts:180-202) defines 'complete evidence' as `record.evidence_file_ids.length !== 0`. A single fabricated string satisfies every evidence gate in the system, in the application and in the database.
findings.impact: Any member of any producer organisation can publish arbitrary emissions figures as verified, operator-attested actual data to every importer they share with, with a verifier attribution naming someone who never verified anything and an evidence trail that does not exist. The importer cannot tell: I confirmed the forged row appears in the importer's shared-actual-data query alongside genuine records with nothing to distinguish them (`visible shared actual rows | 5555...b1 | 2.5 | 1.5` and `5555...e1 | 0.0000001 | 0.0000001`). The figure flows into a calculation result the system will attest was engine-produced and reproducible, and from there into a CBAM declaration. This is the exact failure mode the entire protected-regulatory posture, the D2 provenance decision and the P14.1 trusted-write migration exist to prevent, and it is reachable by the lowest-privileged authenticated actor in the product.
findings.recommendation: Add a BEFORE INSERT trigger on public.emission_data (a new trigger, or widen the existing gates to `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` with TG_OP branches — note the existing bodies dereference OLD and cannot be reused unmodified) that forces a new row to be born in the initial state the domain defines: status='DRAFT', verification_status='UNVERIFIED', verifier_user_id IS NULL, rejection_reason IS NULL, evidence_file_ids='{}'. Overwrite rather than reject, so the honest application path is unaffected — it already sends none of these columns. Equivalently, and better as defence in depth, narrow `emission_data_insert_own_org`'s WITH CHECK to pin those five columns; a policy cannot be turned off by `session_replication_role` the way a trigger can. Independently, and regardless of how the INSERT hole is closed: (a) make `app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record` require every entry of the record's evidence_file_ids to resolve, via app.try_cast_uuid, to an `evidence_files` row with matching emission_data_id and org_id — the same EXISTS the UPDATE policy already performs; and (b) make it require verifier_user_id to be a non-deactivated ADMIN/OWNER membership of entered_by_org_id at the time of the check. Each of these is independently sufficient to stop the chain reaching a declaration, and all three should land — this pass has now found the same class of hole in the INSERT path, the UPDATE path and the validator, which argues for the invariant being asserted in more than one place.

findings.title: The P14 v2 evidence and un-verify invariants are bypassed by ACTIVE -> DISCARDED (or SUPERSEDED) -> DRAFT, and every gate keyed on old.status = 'ACTIVE' switches off
findings.boundary: The producer -> importer data-integrity boundary: the guarantee an importer relies on when freezing a counterparty's evidence set into a determination. Also the MEMBER/ADMIN boundary, since the walk needs no admin.
findings.precondition: One ordinary MEMBER of the organisation that owns a genuine, admin-verified, ACTIVE emission_data record. No admin action at any point. Purely own-org writes, which is why every scope-based control passes.
findings.affected_actor: The counterparty importer organisation, which has frozen the record's evidence set into a determination and has no visibility into the change. The producer's own ADMIN/OWNER, whose verification is silently re-pointed at evidence they never saw. Downstream, the regulator, who sees a VERIFIED record attributed to a named verifier against an evidence set that verifier never approved.
findings.why_controls_fail:
The v2 migration reasoned about which *statements* could carry a record out of its protected state and closed the single-statement and two-statement forms it found (its header explicitly enumerates `set status='DRAFT', verification_status='...'` in one statement, and the same in two). It did not consider a route that leaves ACTIVE via a transition it deliberately permits. Its three gates all open with `if old.status = 'ACTIVE'`, so a record sitting at DISCARDED or SUPERSEDED for the duration of one statement is outside all of them.
The migration's own justification for the ACTIVE -> DRAFT block states the risk exactly and then under-scopes the fix: 'park the record at DRAFT, and every gate keyed on old.status = ACTIVE stops applying to it.' That is precisely right — and DISCARDED and SUPERSEDED are two more parking spots it did not block. The block it wrote (`old.status='ACTIVE' and new.status='DRAFT'`) is the one-hop form of a two-hop problem.
The other walls: `emission_data_update_own_org`'s WITH CHECK does require each claimed evidence id to resolve to a real evidence_files row for this record — but that is satisfied trivially, because `evidence_files_insert_own_org` lets the same MEMBER create such rows at will on a VERIFIED record (only DELETE is gated on `verification_status <> 'VERIFIED'`). So the check catches typos, not adversaries. `app.enforce_emission_data_activation_gate` is satisfied honestly at the final hop: old.status really is DRAFT, verification_status really is VERIFIED (nobody changed it, so the ADMIN-only gate was never triggered), and evidence really is non-empty. `app.prevent_emission_data_fact_change` permits status and evidence_file_ids by design. `verifier_user_id` is immutable — which here works *against* the defender: the swapped record keeps the original admin's name on it and there is no way to correct that attribution through the API.
The application layer is not in the path: `discardEmissionData` and `activateEmissionData` exist, but a raw PostgREST caller does not use them, and `transitionEmissionData`'s in-memory state machine (which has no DISCARDED -> DRAFT edge) is never consulted.
findings.impact: A producer-side MEMBER can silently substitute the entire evidence set behind an ACTIVE, VERIFIED emission record while the record continues to name the admin who verified the original evidence, and can equally walk it to DRAFT/UNVERIFIED. The importer's frozen determination becomes unrewritable and is nulled on the next ordinary edit to their own line, with an error message ('failed validation', or 'locked or void' at the application boundary) that names neither the cause nor the counterparty. This is a cross-organisation integrity and availability failure with no audit signal at the harmed party, and it defeats an invariant this very release candidate added a migration to establish, the day before the freeze.
findings.recommendation: Constrain `status` transitions positively rather than by blacklisting individual bad edges. Add to `app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate` (or a dedicated status-transition gate) an allowlist matching src/domain/emissions/emission-data-lifecycle.ts exactly: DRAFT -> {ACTIVE, DISCARDED}, ACTIVE -> {SUPERSEDED, DISCARDED}, and SUPERSEDED/DISCARDED -> {} (terminal). That single change closes DISCARDED -> DRAFT, SUPERSEDED -> DRAFT, and every other undiscovered edge in the same class, and it is the shape the domain already asserts. Additionally, key the evidence-shrink and un-verify gates on the record's history rather than its instantaneous status — the cheapest form is `if old.verification_status = 'VERIFIED'` (independent of status) for the un-verify rule, and a check that evidence may never shrink once the record has ever been ACTIVE. Both are worth having even after the transition allowlist lands, for the same reason the transition allowlist is worth having: this is now the third distinct route found into the same invariant, and it should be defended more than once.
