findings.title: emission_data has no INSERT-time gate at all: a plain MEMBER can create an ACTIVE + VERIFIED emissions record with a forged verifier and phantom evidence, and file it
findings.boundary: Intra-tenant authorization (MEMBER vs ADMIN/OWNER verification authority) and the regulatory integrity of the emissions record. Reachable by any authenticated member of any importer/declarant organization through the same PostgREST endpoint the application itself writes.
findings.precondition: A normal user session with MEMBER role in any organization holding IMPORTER_DECLARANT. No admin rights, no cross-tenant access, no stolen credentials. The organization's own installation is created by the same member (operators_insert_own_org and installations_insert_own_org both require only org membership).
findings.affected_actor: The regulator and the filing. A declarant organization — or any single junior employee within it — can file a CBAM declaration whose embedded-emissions total has no verified basis. Secondarily, the named verifier: verifier_user_id can be set to a real user in an unrelated organization, so a third party is recorded as having attested to a figure they never saw.
findings.exploit:
Four statements, all as a plain MEMBER over the ordinary data API.
1. Create an operator and an installation in your own org (permitted to MEMBER).
2. INSERT an emission_data row already at status='ACTIVE', verification_status='VERIFIED', verifier_user_id=<any auth.users id>, evidence_file_ids=<any string>, direct_specific=<any figure>. All four BEFORE UPDATE gates (enforce_emission_data_activation_gate, enforce_emission_data_verification_gate, prevent_emission_data_fact_change, touch_updated_at) are skipped because none of them fires on INSERT.
3. INSERT a shipment_line whose emission_determination is an ACTUAL snapshot citing that row. app.validate_emission_determination_write -> app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record accepts it: its ACTUAL branch only asks whether the cited record is ACTIVE + VERIFIED with a non-empty evidence array, which the forgery satisfies by construction, and skips the sharing-grant check entirely because entered_by_org_id = p_org_id.
4. Have the engine record the calculation (service_role, via record_calculation_result — it binds the frozen determination and quantity to the line, both of which are the attacker's own), mark the shipment READY, create a declaration and call record_declaration_filed.
findings.evidence:
Fixture: org rev-atk (IMPORTER_DECLARANT) with OWNER aaaa…0001 / ADMIN aaaa…0002 / MEMBER aaaa…0003; org rev-vic (PRODUCER_OPERATOR) with OWNER bbbb…0001.

Step 2, run as the MEMBER:
  begin; set local role authenticated;
  set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"aaaa0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","role":"authenticated","email":"am@atk.test"}';
  insert into emission_data(id,installation_id,entered_by_org_id,cn_scope,reporting_period_kind,reporting_period_year,
    direct_specific,indirect_specific,emission_unit,methodology,verification_status,verifier_user_id,evidence_file_ids,status)
   values ('a3000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000a','a2000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000a','a0000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000a',
    array['7206'],'ANNUAL',2026,'0.001','0.000','TCO2E_PER_TONNE','EU_METHOD','VERIFIED',
    'bbbb0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001',array['deadbeef-0000-4000-8000-000000000000'],'ACTIVE');
Output:
  acting as aaaa0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003 role=authenticated
  INSERT 0 1
  INSERTED: id=a3000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000a status=ACTIVE vs=VERIFIED verifier=bbbb0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 evidence=deadbeef-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 direct=0.001
  COMMIT

Re-read of the committed row afterwards:
  FORGED ROW STILL COMMITTED: id=a3000000-… status=ACTIVE verification_status=VERIFIED verifier_user_id=bbbb0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 (that user belongs to org rev-vic) entered_by=rev-atk evidence_file_ids=deadbeef-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 evidence_files rows actually present=0 direct_specific=0.001

Step 3, same MEMBER, snapshot carrying record_provenance='IMPORTER_ENTERED':
  INSERT 0 1
  LINE PERSISTED method_col=ACTUAL direct=0.001 verifier=bbbb0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001

Step 4:
  record_calculation_result(...)  -> result_status=OK, id f5842d74-ecd3-404c-8932-0fc11bcb9f88
  record_declaration_filed('ad000000-…','EU-REF-FORGED-001') -> result_status=OK
  FILED TOTAL tCO2e = 1.000
  filed_reference=EU-REF-FORGED-001 status=FILED_RECORDED

The real regulatory default for this line (IN / 7206 90 00, ACTIVE dataset):
  select c.iso2, dev.source_trade_code, pr.source_route_indicator, dev.total_status, dev.total_value ...
  IN | 7206 90 00 | route=(C) | total_status=AVAILABLE | total=2.640
So 1000 t should carry ~2640 tCO2e. The filed figure is 1.000.

Catalog proof of the missing gate — every emission_data trigger is UPDATE-only:
  emission_data_activation_gate_trg      BEFORE UPDATE
  emission_data_prevent_fact_change_trg  BEFORE UPDATE
  emission_data_touch_updated_at_trg     BEFORE UPDATE
  emission_data_verification_gate_trg    BEFORE UPDATE
and the INSERT policy's entire WITH CHECK is:
  ((entered_by_org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids())) AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM installations i WHERE i.id = emission_data.installation_id AND i.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id)))
findings.why_controls_fail:
Four separate controls should each have stopped this and none of them applies on INSERT.
(a) app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate contains the explicit ADMIN/OWNER check `new.verification_status in ('VERIFIED','REJECTED') and not app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of(...)`, and the P14 verifier-pinning logic `new.verifier_user_id := auth.uid()`. It is declared BEFORE UPDATE only, so a row born VERIFIED never meets it.
(b) app.enforce_emission_data_activation_gate enforces DRAFT -> ACTIVE with VERIFIED + non-empty evidence. Also BEFORE UPDATE only; a row born ACTIVE never meets it.
(c) The application layer does gate this — verifyEmissionData() in src/application/emissions/manage-emission-data.ts:618-626 rejects PERMISSION_DENIED without hasAdminAccess. But emission_data is written through the user's own session client (same file, lines 307-320), so the table is a live authenticated endpoint and the application gate is simply not in the path of a direct write.
(d) app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record is the designated anti-forgery control for determinations, and its ACTUAL branch is where this should have been caught. It tests the cited record's *state* (ACTIVE, VERIFIED, evidence non-empty) but never tests whether that state was legitimately reached, never resolves evidence_file_ids against the evidence_files table, and never checks that verifier_user_id belongs to the owning org. It also short-circuits the sharing-grant check whenever entered_by_org_id = p_org_id, which is precisely the self-dealing case. `emission_data_verified_has_verifier_ck` only requires verifier_user_id to be non-null; the FK only requires it to be some real auth.users row.
findings.impact: A single junior user can cause their organization to file a materially false CBAM declaration. In the reproduction the filed total is 1.000 tCO2e where the regulatory default basis gives 2640 — a 99.96% under-report — recorded as FILED_RECORDED with a filing reference and an immutable filed_snapshot, and attributed to a verifier in another company. Because record_declaration_filed's completeness pass only checks that each line has a current calculation matching the line's own determination and quantity, and nothing downstream ever revalidates the cited emission_data, the falsehood is invisible at every later surface: the panel, the exports and the archived snapshot all repeat it. This is regulatory misreporting with a forged attestation trail, produced without any privilege the product intends to require.
findings.recommendation: Add a BEFORE INSERT trigger on emission_data that enforces the same invariants the UPDATE gates do — reuse the existing functions by re-declaring them BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE with TG_OP branches rather than writing new logic. At minimum, on INSERT: force status='DRAFT' and verification_status='UNVERIFIED' (a record cannot be born verified or active); reject any non-null verifier_user_id; and reject any evidence_file_ids entry that does not resolve to an evidence_files row whose emission_data_id is this row and whose org_id is entered_by_org_id — the same containment the UPDATE policy's WITH CHECK already expresses, which is conspicuously absent from the INSERT policy. Separately, harden app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record's ACTUAL branch to resolve evidence_file_ids against evidence_files and to require verifier_user_id to hold an active ADMIN/OWNER membership of entered_by_org_id, so the determination layer stops trusting the emission_data row's self-declared state. Write the failing tests first (TDD, per CLAUDE.md) and re-run pnpm regulatory:verify afterwards.

findings.title: The ACTIVE+VERIFIED evidence-immutability gate is bypassed by ACTIVE -> DISCARDED -> DRAFT; a plain MEMBER can swap or destroy the evidence behind a verified record
findings.boundary: Intra-tenant integrity of a verified emissions record, and the cross-tenant contract with any importer that has frozen that record's evidence set into a determination. Reachable by any authenticated MEMBER of the producer organization.
findings.precondition: MEMBER role in the organization that owns the emission_data row (entered_by_org_id). No ADMIN, no OWNER. The emission_data UPDATE policy's USING clause is bare `entered_by_org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids())` — no role predicate and no status predicate whatsoever.
findings.affected_actor: Any importer/declarant that consumed this record under a sharing grant and froze its evidence set into a determination — their frozen determination now cites evidence that no longer exists or was never seen by the verifier. Also the regulator, who is shown a record marked VERIFIED whose evidence is not the evidence that was verified.
findings.exploit:
Three or four UPDATEs, all as a plain MEMBER.
Evidence SWAP: (1) `update emission_data set status='DISCARDED'` — permitted, and the verification gate's ACTIVE-keyed branches do not fire because verification_status is unchanged. (2) `update ... set status='DRAFT'` — old.status is now 'DISCARDED', so the P14.1 `old.status='ACTIVE' and new.status='DRAFT'` guard does not match, and every gate keyed on old.status='ACTIVE' has stopped applying. (3) Upload a different evidence file and `update ... set evidence_file_ids=array[<new id>]` — the shrink check is keyed on old.status='ACTIVE' and is skipped. (4) `update ... set status='ACTIVE'` — the activation gate is satisfied because verification_status never left 'VERIFIED' and the array is non-empty.
Evidence DESTRUCTION: same first two hops, then `update ... set verification_status='UNVERIFIED'` (permitted — the ADMIN check only covers transitions INTO 'VERIFIED'/'REJECTED', and the 'cannot leave VERIFIED' branch is keyed on old.status='ACTIVE'), then `delete from evidence_files where emission_data_id=…` — now permitted because evidence_files_delete_own_org requires only `ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED'`.
findings.evidence:
SWAP, as plain MEMBER bbbb…0002 of rev-vic:
  begin; set local role authenticated;
  set local request.jwt.claims='{"sub":"bbbb0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","role":"authenticated"}';
  BEFORE ACTIVE/VERIFIED verifier=bbbb0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 ev=b4000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000b
  update emission_data set status='DISCARDED' where id='b3000000-…';   -> UPDATE 1
  update emission_data set status='DRAFT'     where id='b3000000-…';   -> UPDATE 1
  insert into evidence_files(... 'swap.pdf' ...);                        -> INSERT 0 1
  update emission_data set evidence_file_ids=array['b6000000-…'];        -> UPDATE 1
  update emission_data set status='ACTIVE'    where id='b3000000-…';   -> UPDATE 1
  FINAL ACTIVE/VERIFIED verifier=bbbb0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 ev=b6000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000b
The record returns to ACTIVE + VERIFIED, still stamped with the original OWNER as verifier, with an evidence set that OWNER never saw.

Intermediate step confirming the hop is what unlocks it (same session):
  S1 DISCARDED/VERIFIED
  S2 DRAFT/VERIFIED
  S3 DRAFT/VERIFIED ev=[]        <- the entire evidence array stripped
and re-activation with an EMPTY array is correctly refused:
  ERROR: emission_data: a record may only transition to ACTIVE from DRAFT while verification_status = VERIFIED and evidence_file_ids is non-empty

DESTRUCTION, same MEMBER:
  start: ACTIVE/VERIFIED evidence rows=1
  update emission_data set status='DISCARDED' ...              -> UPDATE 1
  update emission_data set status='DRAFT' ...                  -> UPDATE 1
  update emission_data set verification_status='UNVERIFIED' ... -> UPDATE 1
  now: DRAFT/UNVERIFIED
  delete from evidence_files where emission_data_id='b3000000-…'; -> DELETE 1
  evidence rows remaining=0
  emission_data still claims evidence_file_ids=b4000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000b
The row is left with a dangling evidence reference — the exact state the invariant exists to prevent.
findings.why_controls_fail: app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate is the control, and its own in-body comment states the reasoning that fails here: 'Keyed on old.status only. Deliberately NOT on new.status: that is exactly the conjunct that let set status=DRAFT, verification_status=VERIFICATION_PENDING through.' The P14.1 fix correctly closed the direct ACTIVE -> DRAFT edge, but every one of the four protective branches — cannot-leave-VERIFIED, cannot-return-to-DRAFT, evidence-cannot-shrink, verifier-immutability — is guarded by `old.status = 'ACTIVE'`. DISCARDED is an accepted status under emission_data_status_check and there is no transition table constraining status moves, so ACTIVE -> DISCARDED (which changes no verification_status and therefore trips nothing) launders old.status out of 'ACTIVE' in one statement and every gate switches off. The evidence-shrink check's comment explicitly claims 'DISCARD and SUPERSEDE are unaffected because they do not change verification_status, so this branch is never reached for them' — true, and that is precisely the hole: DISCARD is not merely unaffected, it is the escape hatch. The RLS UPDATE policy provides no backstop: emission_data_update_own_org's USING is org-membership only, with no role and no status predicate, and its WITH CHECK validates evidence containment but places no constraint on status transitions at all.
findings.impact: The single strongest integrity guarantee this schema advertises — that a verified emissions record's evidence cannot be removed once an importer may have frozen it — does not hold against a plain member of the producer organization, and the version-chain escape hatch it was written to close is still open. An importer's frozen ActualEmissionSnapshot can be left citing evidence_file_ids that resolve to nothing, inside a filed, immutable declaration. A record can be presented to a regulator as VERIFIED, naming a real verifier, over evidence that verifier never examined. Nothing in the schema records that the swap happened: emission_data has no history table, and the audit trail for it is written by the application layer, which this path bypasses.
findings.recommendation: Stop keying the gates on old.status and enforce the lifecycle itself. Add an explicit transition whitelist for emission_data.status as a BEFORE UPDATE trigger (DRAFT->ACTIVE, DRAFT->DISCARDED, ACTIVE->SUPERSEDED, ACTIVE->DISCARDED; nothing else — DISCARDED and SUPERSEDED terminal), mirroring src/domain/emissions/emission-data-lifecycle.ts, which per the verification gate's own comment already has only DRAFT->ACTIVE and DRAFT->DISCARDED. Independently, make verification_status non-reversible once VERIFIED for any row that has ever been ACTIVE (a `verified_at`/`ever_active` column, or key the guard on the existence of the verifier stamp rather than on current status), and gate every verification_status change behind ADMIN/OWNER rather than only transitions into VERIFIED/REJECTED. Tighten evidence_files_delete_own_org the same way: a file that has ever backed a verified record should not be deletable by re-driving the parent's status. Add a foreign-key-shaped integrity check so evidence_file_ids can never dangle.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: The build-and-test secret scan is a guaranteed no-op on every run, and the surviving fast-gates scan does not cover the credential shapes it was built for
findings.boundary: CI quality gate -> repository secret hygiene (source control boundary)
findings.precondition: None. The defect is unconditional: the step is dead on every push and every PR, for every input, on the frozen candidate cad99ad.
findings.affected_actor: The regulator/filing and every tenant: the only automated control preventing a Supabase service-role key, DB password or a password-bearing postgres:// URL from being committed to this repository.
findings.exploit: 1) Commit any tracked file containing `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=<real password>`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: "<value>"`, or `postgresql://postgres:<realpassword>@db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432/postgres`. 2) Push. 3) build-and-test's "Scan for committed secrets" step (.github/workflows/ci.yml:497-610) prints "No secret-shaped literals found in tracked files." and exits 0. 4) fast-gates' "Scan for committed secrets" step (ci.yml:109-117) prints "Secret scan clean." and exits 0, because its PATTERN (ci.yml:112) contains no SUPABASE_*/postgres:// alternatives at all. Both jobs green.
findings.evidence:
MECHANISM, isolated (bash 5.2.37):
$ cat repro602c.sh
set -euo pipefail
A="$(printf 'x\n' | grep -vE "$UNDEFINED_VAR" || true)"
echo "REACHED-WITH-ORTRUE A=[$A]"
$ bash repro602c.sh; echo "EXIT_WITH_ORTRUE=$?"
repro602c.sh: line 2: UNDEFINED_VAR: unbound variable
REACHED-WITH-ORTRUE A=[]
EXIT_WITH_ORTRUE=0

Same construct WITHOUT the trailing `|| true` fails loudly, proving `|| true` is the masking element:
$ bash repro602b.sh; echo "EXIT_NO_ORTRUE=$?"
repro602b.sh: line 3: UNDEFINED_VAR: unbound variable
EXIT_NO_ORTRUE=1

END-TO-END, the real step run verbatim (lines 499-610 of ci.yml extracted with sed, comments stripped, run in a throwaway git repo containing three planted credentials):
$ sed -n '499,610p' .github/workflows/ci.yml | sed 's/^          //' | grep -v '^ *#' > /tmp/p14rev/bt.sh
$ bash /tmp/p14rev/bt.sh; echo "BUILD_AND_TEST_STEP_EXIT=$?"
/tmp/p14rev/bt.sh: line 25: KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT: unbound variable
No secret-shaped literals found in tracked files.
BUILD_AND_TEST_STEP_EXIT=0

The planted file (leak.env.ts) was:
  SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=Hunter2ProdPassword
  postgresql://postgres:RealProdPassword9@db.abcdefgh.supabase.co:5432/postgres
  SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: "not-a-jwt-but-real-secret-value"

THE DEAD PATTERN WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL THREE (so this is not redundant coverage):
$ PATTERN='<ci.yml:538 verbatim>'; git grep -InE "$PATTERN" -- . ':!pnpm-lock.yaml' ':!.github/workflows/ci.yml'; echo "exit=$?"
leak.env.ts:1:export const a = "SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=Hunter2ProdPassword";
leak.env.ts:2:export const b = "postgresql://postgres:RealProdPassword9@db.abcdefgh.supabase.co:5432/postgres";
leak.env.ts:3:export const c = 'SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: "not-a-jwt-but-real-secret-value"';
exit=0

THE SURVIVING fast-gates SCAN CATCHES NONE OF THEM:
$ bash /tmp/p14rev/fg.sh; echo "FASTGATES_STEP_EXIT=$?"
Secret scan clean.
FASTGATES_STEP_EXIT=0
(its raw git grep with ci.yml:112's PATTERN returned exit 1, no matches)

file:line — .github/workflows/ci.yml:602 (`grep -vE "$KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT"`, variable never assigned anywhere in the file), masked by the `|| true` at the end of the same line-continued command at ci.yml:602, under `set -euo pipefail` declared at ci.yml:499.
findings.why_controls_fail: Three controls should have stopped this and none do. (1) `set -u` is present and does fire — it just fires inside a `$(...)` subshell whose non-zero status the trailing `|| true` discards, so errexit never sees it; I proved both halves separately. (2) The step's own guard for a broken scan (ci.yml:586-597, GIT_GREP_EXIT > 1) is correct and I verified it fires on exit 128 — but it guards only `git grep`, and the death happens in the filter pipeline three lines later. (3) The fast-gates duplicate is not a compensating control: its PATTERN at ci.yml:112 was never updated with the P11 hardening described at ci.yml:509-537, so it lacks the SUPABASE_(SERVICE_ROLE_KEY|DB_PASSWORD|ANON_KEY) and postgres(ql)://user:pass@ alternatives entirely. I confirmed by running the exact patterns side by side against the same planted file.
findings.impact: The credential-hygiene gate this release is certified on does not exist. Scope is bounded honestly: I re-ran the dead scan's own pattern against the real repo at cad99ad and it surfaces no live secret today (only the intended `process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY = ...` false positives in tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts:274,462 that the missing variable was meant to allowlist, plus the audit documents describing this very bug). So this is a proven-dead future-facing control, not evidence of a current leak. It is a BLOCKER because the release certification claims this gate executed, and because the repo's own .env holds production credentials of exactly the two shapes only the dead scan checks.
findings.recommendation: Define KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT (intended value: an ERE matching `process\.env\.SUPABASE_(SERVICE_ROLE_KEY|DB_PASSWORD|ANON_KEY)\s*=`), or delete the third filter. Independently, remove the `|| true` and handle grep's no-match exit 1 explicitly, so a future unbound variable fails the step instead of greening it. Then bring ci.yml:112's PATTERN to parity with ci.yml:538 so the two jobs are genuinely redundant. Add a self-test to the step: plant a known secret-shaped string in a temp tracked file, assert the scanner exits 1 on it, then remove it — a scanner that has never been observed failing is not known to work.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: emission_data's entire evidence-integrity check lives in an UPDATE policy; INSERT is completely ungated, so a MEMBER creates an ACTIVE+VERIFIED record citing evidence ids that never existed -- and the record then cannot be retired by anyone
findings.boundary: Intra-tenant privilege boundary (MEMBER vs verifier), escalating across the sharing boundary: the resulting row is selectable and consumable by any grantee importer org via emission_data_select_own_org's shared-installation branch.
findings.precondition: An ordinary MEMBER of a PRODUCER_OPERATOR org that owns at least one installation. Nothing else.
findings.affected_actor: The grantee importer/declarant org that consumes the figure as independently verified and evidenced, the regulator receiving the resulting declaration, and the producer org itself -- whose OWNER cannot subsequently withdraw the row.
findings.exploit: A single INSERT. The member supplies status='ACTIVE', verification_status='VERIFIED', verifier_user_id = their own uuid, and evidence_file_ids = an array of uuids corresponding to no evidence_files row -- the array may even contain a non-UUID string, because the try_cast_uuid hardening added by 20260829490000 lives in the UPDATE policy's WITH CHECK and is never evaluated on INSERT. The record satisfies app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record (status ACTIVE, verification_status VERIFIED, array length > 0) and is therefore freezable into an importer's determination. It is then PERMANENTLY IMMUTABLE: any UPDATE preserving the array fails the WITH CHECK anti-join, any UPDATE removing it fails the P14 shrink trigger, and emission_data has no DELETE policy -- so no authenticated user, including the org OWNER, can discard, supersede or correct it.
findings.why_controls_fail: 20260829480000's own header names 'evidence_file_ids forgery' as the defect it closes, and closes it by adding the anti-join to `emission_data_update_own_org`'s WITH CHECK -- an UPDATE policy. 20260829490000 then hardens that same anti-join with try_cast_uuid and its header explicitly notes a non-uuid entry is 'only possible at INSERT time ... nothing at INSERT time validates evidence_file_ids' contents' -- the gap is written down in the repository and was never closed. The activation gate (app.enforce_emission_data_activation_gate) is the control that would require VERIFIED + non-empty evidence, but it fires only BEFORE UPDATE on a status transition, so a row born ACTIVE never meets it. emission_data_verified_has_verifier_ck only tests verifier_user_id IS NOT NULL, not that the verifier is an ADMIN or even a different person. The un-verify and shrink triggers then close the trap: designed to protect a legitimately-verified record, they make the forged one unretirable.
findings.impact: A member can manufacture, in one statement, an emissions figure presented to a counterparty importer as independently verified and evidenced, with the evidence citations entirely invented and no bytes behind them. Because the grantee importer cannot read evidence_files at all (evidence_files_select_own_org is own-org only), they have no way to check. The figure flows into the importer's determination, calculation and declaration. And because the row can never be updated or deleted by any authenticated role, the forgery cannot be withdrawn without direct database administrator access.
findings.recommendation: Move evidence integrity to where it cannot be bypassed by choosing the verb. Add the same anti-join (with try_cast_uuid) to `emission_data_insert_own_org`'s WITH CHECK, and add a BEFORE INSERT trigger asserting what the activation gate asserts on UPDATE: a row may not be born with status <> 'DRAFT', may not be born verification_status='VERIFIED', and verifier_user_id must be NULL at insert. Separately reconcile the deadlock between the 20260829480000 anti-join and the 20260903150000 shrink rule -- the shrink rule should exempt removal of an id that no longer resolves to an evidence_files row, otherwise any dangling id (including one produced by the concurrent-removal race documented at src/application/evidence/upload-evidence.ts:474-480) bricks the row permanently.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: emission_data's activation and verification gates are BEFORE UPDATE only — a plain MEMBER INSERTs a fully forged ACTIVE + VERIFIED record (prior #11, BLOCKER confirmed)
findings.boundary: Role boundary within a tenant (MEMBER -> ADMIN-only verification), and from there the cross-tenant sharing boundary.
findings.precondition: One MEMBER account in an organisation holding at least one installation. Raw PostgREST access with that member's own session token.
findings.affected_actor: Every grantee organisation reading the record as operator-attested verified data, and every regulator receiving a figure derived from it.
findings.exploit: A single POST /rest/v1/emission_data with status='ACTIVE', verification_status='VERIFIED', verifier_user_id set to any uuid the attacker chooses, and evidence_file_ids set to any uuid at all. The three walls that stop the equivalent UPDATE — ADMIN-only verify, DRAFT->ACTIVE-requires-VERIFIED-and-evidence, and the evidence-must-name-real-files anti-join — are all on the UPDATE side.
findings.evidence:
Trigger census on the live sandbox — all four are UPDATE-only, there is no INSERT trigger:
  emission_data_activation_gate_trg      BEFORE UPDATE ON public.emission_data ... app.enforce_emission_data_activation_gate()
  emission_data_prevent_fact_change_trg  BEFORE UPDATE ...
  emission_data_touch_updated_at_trg     BEFORE UPDATE ...
  emission_data_verification_gate_trg    BEFORE UPDATE ... app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate()

Policy asymmetry, read from pg_policy:
  INSERT (polcmd 'a') WITH CHECK: ((entered_by_org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids())) AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM installations i WHERE i.id = emission_data.installation_id AND i.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id)))
  UPDATE (polcmd 'w') WITH CHECK: the same, PLUS `AND (NOT (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM unnest(emission_data.evidence_file_ids) claimed(evidence_file_id) WHERE (NOT (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM evidence_files ef WHERE ef.id = app.try_cast_uuid(claimed.evidence_file_id) AND ef.emission_data_id = emission_data.id AND ef.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id))))))`

Live, begin/rollback, before 0 rows and after 0 rows both verified:
  set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"11111111-0000-0000-0000-000000000001","role":"authenticated"}';
  (that user's memberships row reads MEMBER)
  insert into public.emission_data (...) values (..., 'VERIFIED','11111111-0000-0000-0000-000000000001','{}','ACTIVE') returning ...;
  -> INSERT 0 1
  id | status | verification_status | verifier_user_id | evidence_file_ids | direct_specific
  55555555-...-f011 | ACTIVE | VERIFIED | 11111111-...-0001 | {} | 0.0000001
  ROLLBACK -> post_rows 0
findings.why_controls_fail: Every gate the P13 and P14 remediation passes added was expressed as a BEFORE UPDATE trigger, because every finding those passes reproduced was an UPDATE. The CHECK constraint emission_data_verified_has_verifier_ck is the only INSERT-time control touching verification, and it only requires the field be non-null — the caller supplies it. The repository's own regression suite mirrors the blind spot: tests/integration/emission-data-write-hardening.test.ts's case titled 'a plain MEMBER cannot set status=ACTIVE directly on a DRAFT+UNVERIFIED+no-evidence row' drives `.update({status:'ACTIVE'})`, and none of its cases drives an INSERT.
findings.impact: The ADMIN-only verification gate, the evidence requirement, and the DRAFT->ACTIVE lifecycle are all optional for anyone willing to create the row in its final state. This is the ignition for chains C1 and C2.
findings.recommendation: Convert both gate triggers to BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE with a TG_OP='INSERT' arm that admits only DRAFT + UNVERIFIED + null verifier_user_id, and add the UPDATE policy's evidence anti-join to the INSERT policy. Write the INSERT twin of every existing case in the hardening suite before touching the trigger.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: The 'evidence may grow but never shrink' invariant is fully bypassed by an ACTIVE -> DISCARDED -> DRAFT -> ACTIVE detour — and the no-ADMIN variant I found is strictly stronger than the one previously reported (prior #17, BLOCKER confirmed and widened)
findings.boundary: Role boundary within a tenant, with cross-tenant harm: the party damaged is the importer whose frozen determination cites the evidence.
findings.precondition: Any MEMBER of the producer organisation, over PostgREST with their own session. No ADMIN at any step in the variant I reproduced.
findings.affected_actor: The counterparty importer, whose frozen ActualEmissionSnapshot compares its evidence set byte-for-byte against the live array; and the regulator, for whom the cited evidence no longer exists.
findings.exploit:
VARIANT A (evidence swap, keeps VERIFIED, no ADMIN, 3 statements): PATCH {status:'DISCARDED'}; PATCH {status:'DRAFT', evidence_file_ids:[<a different file>]}; PATCH {status:'ACTIVE'}. The evidence-shrink gate and the un-verify gate are both keyed on `old.status='ACTIVE'`, so neither applies once the row is DISCARDED; verification_status is never touched, so the ADMIN-only verify gate never fires; and DRAFT->ACTIVE passes because the row is still VERIFIED and the evidence array is still non-empty.
VARIANT B (physical destruction, no ADMIN): PATCH {status:'DISCARDED'}; PATCH {verification_status:'UNVERIFIED'} (the ADMIN gate fires only for VERIFIED/REJECTED, and the un-verify gate is keyed on old.status='ACTIVE'); then DELETE the evidence_files row, whose delete policy requires only `ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED'`.
findings.evidence:
All in one rolled-back transaction against p14_review_sandbox, acting as role authenticated with the JWT of a user whose memberships row reads MEMBER.

CONTROL (the gate is genuinely in force on the direct path):
  update public.emission_data set evidence_file_ids='{77777777-...-00e2}' where id='66666666-...-00e1';
  -> ERROR: emission_data: evidence cannot be removed from an ACTIVE, VERIFIED record ... CONTEXT: PL/pgSQL function app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate() line 70 at RAISE

VARIANT A:
  update ... set status='DISCARDED' ...                                             -> UPDATE 1
  update ... set status='DRAFT', evidence_file_ids='{77777777-...-00e2}' ...        -> UPDATE 1
  update ... set status='ACTIVE' ...                                                -> UPDATE 1
  final state: status | verification_status | verifier_user_id | evidence_file_ids
               ACTIVE | VERIFIED            | 11111111-...-0002 | {77777777-...-00e2}
The row is back at ACTIVE+VERIFIED, STILL STAMPED WITH THE ADMIN'S verifier_user_id, carrying evidence the ADMIN never saw. The prior finding's own reproduction required an ADMIN for its last two steps; this variant requires none, because it never changes verification_status.

VARIANT B, same session:
  (control) delete from public.evidence_files where id='77777777-...-00e1'; -> DELETE 0, row still present (count 1)
  update ... set status='DISCARDED';                                       -> UPDATE 1
  update ... set verification_status='UNVERIFIED';                          -> UPDATE 1
  delete from public.evidence_files where id='77777777-...-00e1';          -> DELETE 1
  evidence_rows_remaining -> 0, while emission_data.evidence_file_ids still reads {77777777-...-00e1} — a dangling reference.
ROLLBACK; post_rollback count 0.
findings.why_controls_fail: 20260903150000's own comment explains that the un-verify gate is 'Keyed on old.status only. Deliberately NOT on new.status: that is exactly the conjunct that let `set status=DRAFT, verification_status=VERIFICATION_PENDING` through' — the fix moved the conjunct rather than removing the state machine's freedom. DISCARDED is an unguarded waypoint: nothing forbids ACTIVE -> DISCARDED, nothing forbids DISCARDED -> DRAFT, and every gate that protects an ACTIVE+VERIFIED record tests `old.status = 'ACTIVE'`. 20260829560000's evidence_files delete lock keys on `ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED'` alone, so step 2 of variant B unlocks it. The domain lifecycle (emission-data-lifecycle.ts) has no DISCARDED -> DRAFT transition, so no application code would ever do this — which is exactly why the database never learned to refuse it.
findings.impact: The evidence set behind a verified figure — the thing a CBAM auditor would ask for — can be swapped or destroyed by the lowest-privileged member, with the verifying ADMIN's identity left attached. The importer's frozen determination silently stops validating and the error surfaced says only 'locked or void'.
findings.recommendation: Express the lifecycle as an explicit transition whitelist in a single BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger (DRAFT->ACTIVE, DRAFT->DISCARDED, ACTIVE->SUPERSEDED, ACTIVE->DISCARDED and nothing else), rather than adding another gate keyed on a status pair. Key the evidence-shrink and un-verify gates on 'has this record EVER been ACTIVE+VERIFIED' — a persisted flag or the audit trail — not on old.status. Gate the evidence_files delete lock the same way.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: The certification run's secret scan is inert: an undefined shell variable under `set -euo pipefail` is swallowed by `|| true`, and the audit cites the resulting empty output as a passing gate (prior #33, BLOCKER confirmed)
findings.boundary: Release-certification integrity, and the credential boundary: the repository's .env holds production credentials and this is the only automated guard against a similar file being committed.
findings.precondition: None. The step is dead on every run.
findings.affected_actor: Everyone relying on the release certification, and ultimately the production Supabase project whose credentials this gate exists to keep out of git.
findings.exploit: Commit any file containing a dotenv-style `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=<real password>` or a `postgres://` DSN and push. The build-and-test 'Scan for committed secrets' step reports clean and exits 0. The fast-gates job's separate scan cannot catch it either: its PATTERN (.github/workflows/ci.yml:112) is `eyJ...|sk-...|re_...|sb_(publishable|secret)_...` and contains no SUPABASE_*= or postgres:// shape at all.
findings.evidence:
The variable is used and never assigned. `grep -n KNOWN_SAFE .github/workflows/ci.yml`:
  562: KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_DEMO_JWT='eyJpc3MiOiJzdXBhYmFzZS1kZW1vIiwicm9sZSI6'
  570: KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_PG_URL='postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1'
  600:   | grep -vF "$KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_DEMO_JWT" \
  601:   | grep -vF "$KNOWN_SAFE_LOCAL_PG_URL" \
  602:   | grep -vE "$KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT" || true)"
No assignment to KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT exists anywhere in the file. The step opens `set -euo pipefail` at :499, and :604 is `if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]`.

I reproduced the mechanism with a planted secret in the input:
  bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; RAW="leak.env:1:SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=hunter2secretvalue"; M="$(printf "%s\n" "$RAW" | grep -vF "$K1" | grep -vF "$K2" | grep -vE "$KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT" || true)"; echo "exit=$?"; echo "MATCHES=[$M]"; if [ -n "$M" ]; then echo "WOULD FAIL"; else echo "No secret-shaped literals found in tracked files."; fi'
  ->  bash: line 1: KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT: unbound variable
      exit=0
      MATCHES=[]
      No secret-shaped literals found in tracked files.

The unbound-variable error kills the command substitution; `|| true` restores exit 0; MATCHES is empty unconditionally; the success string always prints.
findings.why_controls_fail: `set -euo pipefail` and `|| true` are individually correct and jointly fatal here: `-u` makes the expansion an error, and `|| true` converts that error into a successful empty result rather than a failure. The step's neighbour at :594 gets this right — it checks `if [ "$GIT_GREP_EXIT" -gt 1 ]` and treats an unexpected status as 'a broken scan, not "no secrets found"'. That reasoning was applied to git grep's exit status and not to the filter pipeline below it.
findings.impact: Two of the release's gates report clean on a repository containing a committed database password. The audit document then cites this output as evidence that the gate passed, which converts a dead check into an affirmative claim. I keep this at BLOCKER not because of what it currently lets through — nothing is committed today — but because the release certification's own evidence is manufactured by a step that cannot fail.
findings.recommendation: Assign KNOWN_SAFE_PROCESS_ENV_ASSIGNMENT (or delete the filter). Then, in every scan step, drop `|| true` and handle grep's exit status explicitly the way :594 already does. Add a negative test: a fixture file with a planted secret that the workflow must reject, so a dead scan fails loudly. Note that the documented filter regex would itself match three lines of docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md, so re-enabling the scan will need that prose handled.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: Nothing in CI asserts that a self-skipping suite actually ran; ~201 tests hang off a 1500 ms timing probe
findings.boundary: Regression gate for cross-org tenancy isolation (master plan §13's 'standing test, not an assumption')
findings.precondition: Any transient condition that makes a 1500 ms fetch to http://127.0.0.1:54321/auth/v1/health miss its deadline while vitest is collecting — runner CPU contention, Docker networking hiccup, a slow Kong warm-up.
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant. These suites are the standing regression coverage for every cross-org bug found in P3, P4, P7, P9, P10 and P11.
findings.exploit: 1. The probe: `AbortSignal.timeout(1500)` in tests/integration/organizations-isolation.test.ts:134-151, evaluated at module scope (`const localSupabaseReachable = await isLocalSupabaseReachable();` at :153-154) and consumed by `describe.skipIf(!localSupabaseReachable)` at :156. Sixteen integration files use this identical shape. 2. If it misses, every test in that file is marked skipped. 3. vitest run exits 0. 4. The CI Test step (ci.yml:359-365) is `pnpm test` with no post-processing of the result, and no step anywhere inspects a skip count. The job goes green having executed none of the isolation coverage.
findings.why_controls_fail: The workflow does prove Supabase is reachable — twice with `curl -sf .../auth/v1/health` (ci.yml:~303 and ~318) and via the ACTIVE=12540 assertion. But those probes run in the PREVIOUS step, in a different process, minutes earlier. The suites' own probe re-runs inside vitest with a 1.5 s budget, and its result is the one that decides. The gap between 'the workflow proved Supabase was up' and 'the suites actually executed' is exactly where a false green lives. The workflow's own comments (ci.yml:165-172, 456-459) explicitly identify silent skipping as the enemy and then never assert against it.
findings.impact: A run that exercises zero cross-org isolation tests is indistinguishable in the UI from one that exercises all 201. The release-certification claim 'the isolation suites run for real' rests on comments, not on any assertion the job makes.
findings.recommendation: Make skipping fatal in CI: have the integration suites throw when `process.env.CI` is set and the probe fails (the same discipline tests/e2e/actual-data-determination.spec.ts:165-172 already applies for Storage), and/or add a CI step that parses vitest JSON output and fails the job if the skipped count is non-zero or the passed count is below a pinned floor. Also raise the 1500 ms probe timeout, which is far too tight for a cold Kong on a shared runner.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: No CI job builds the Dockerfile, and Railway deploys from it independently of CI, so no gate in this workflow can block a deploy
findings.boundary: CI-to-deployment boundary
findings.precondition: None. This is the standing structure of the pipeline.
findings.affected_actor: Production and every tenant in it.
findings.exploit: 1. railway.json specifies `"builder": "DOCKERFILE"`, `"dockerfilePath": "Dockerfile"` and deploys on push to the configured branch. 2. ci.yml contains no `docker build` step anywhere — the full step inventory (`grep -nE '^\s+- name:|^\s+run:' .github/workflows/ci.yml`) is: checkout, pnpm, node, install, typecheck, test, build, secret scan (fast-gates); checkout, pnpm, node, install, typecheck, python setup, pip install, start supabase, test, playwright install, write .env.local, playwright test, supabase stop, upload report, pnpm audit, secret scan (build-and-test). 3. Nothing makes the Railway build wait on, or consult, either job's conclusion. A push with both jobs red deploys exactly as fast as a push with both green.
findings.why_controls_fail: ci.yml was changed on 2026-09-02 from `push: branches: [main]` to `branches: ['**']` precisely so CI would RUN against the deployed commit — which it now does. But running against a commit and gating that commit are different things, and only the first was fixed. The strict artifact assertion (`--require-artifact`, which is what refuses an image built from a bypass-carrying build) exists only inside the Docker build, which CI never performs; so the invariant is enforced only at deploy time, after the decision to deploy has already been made. The `pnpm build` that CI does run (ci.yml:103-107) uses placeholder Supabase env and does not pass --require-artifact.
findings.impact: Every finding in this report about a dead or weak gate is compounded: even a correctly-failing gate would not stop a release. And the image build path itself — ARG-injected NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY, the standalone copy, the strict bypass assertion — is validated by nothing before it reaches production.
findings.recommendation: Add a `docker build` step to CI (it exercises `--require-artifact` for free), and configure Railway to require the CI check, or move deployment behind a workflow that depends on both jobs. Until one of those exists, no statement of the form 'the gates passed, therefore it is safe to ship' is supportable.

findings.title: A forged emission_data row is permanently un-retractable through the API — not even the organisation's OWNER can discard it
findings.boundary: Remediation boundary. Nothing that an organisation's highest-privileged role can reach undoes the forgery; recovery requires service_role or direct DBA access.
findings.precondition: Any successful exploitation of finding 1 with an evidence_file_ids entry that does not resolve to a real evidence_files row — which is the natural form of the attack, since fabricating the array is the whole point. Worst form: a non-UUID token, which no evidence_files row can ever satisfy (evidence_files.id is uuid).
findings.affected_actor: The victim organisation's own OWNER/ADMIN, and the grantee importers, who continue to be served the forged record as verified operator data for as long as it exists — which, through the product, is forever.
findings.evidence:
R1: `before | ACTIVE | {aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee}` then the DISCARD -> `ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy for table "emission_data"`.
R2: -> `ERROR: emission_data: evidence cannot be removed from an ACTIVE, VERIFIED record...` (verification gate line 70).
L1: `INSERT 0 1`; `L1 inserted | 5555...c1 | {not-a-uuid}`; then as OWNER, `update emission_data set status='DISCARDED'` -> `ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy for table "emission_data"`.
The mechanism is in the UPDATE policy's WITH CHECK, from pg_policy: `NOT (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM unnest(emission_data.evidence_file_ids) claimed(evidence_file_id) WHERE NOT (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM evidence_files ef WHERE ef.id = app.try_cast_uuid(claimed.evidence_file_id) AND ef.emission_data_id = emission_data.id AND ef.org_id = emission_data.entered_by_org_id))))`. It is evaluated against the NEW row on *every* UPDATE, including ones that do not touch evidence_file_ids at all. `app.try_cast_uuid('not-a-uuid')` returns NULL, `ef.id = NULL` matches nothing, so the condition is unsatisfiable for any NEW row that still carries the token — and the evidence-shrink gate blocks removing it. DELETE is unavailable (`DELETE 0`, no DELETE policy). The row is wedged.
findings.why_controls_fail:
The WITH CHECK was added (20260829490000, 'evidence uuid cast hardening') to stop a member *claiming* evidence they do not have. It does that on the UPDATE path. But because it is a WITH CHECK on the whole new row rather than a condition on the columns being changed, it converts a row that entered the table in a state the check would have rejected into a row that can never be updated again. The INSERT policy does not carry the same clause (finding 1's root cause), so the table can be seeded with rows the UPDATE policy will permanently refuse. Combined with the absence of a DELETE policy — a deliberate append-only posture that is correct in isolation — there is no statement any `authenticated` role can issue against such a row.
The evidence-shrink gate then closes the one obvious escape: an OWNER cannot strip the bad id, because stripping it is a shrink on an ACTIVE+VERIFIED record. (Ironically the finding-2 walk *would* let them out — DISCARDED, DRAFT, fix, ACTIVE — but the first hop is itself an UPDATE and fails the same WITH CHECK. The two defects do not cancel.)
The only remaining route is to fabricate an evidence_files row whose id equals the attacker's chosen UUID, i.e. to make the forgery look genuine — and that route does not exist at all when the token is not a UUID.
findings.impact: The forgery is not merely possible, it is irreversible in-product. An organisation that discovers a member has published false operator-attested emissions to its counterparties cannot withdraw the record, cannot discard it, cannot correct its evidence, and cannot delete it. It stays ACTIVE and VERIFIED, and stays visible and consumable to every grantee importer, until someone with the service_role key or database credentials intervenes manually. For a compliance product this is a serious incident-response failure independent of how the bad row got there — and note it also applies to a bad row created by ordinary application bugs or bad data migrations, not only by attack.
findings.recommendation: Two changes, both small. First, scope the evidence WITH CHECK so it constrains the change rather than the whole row — e.g. only require resolution for ids in `new.evidence_file_ids` that are not already in `old.evidence_file_ids` (this is a trigger's job, not a policy's, since a policy cannot see OLD; move the clause into `app.enforce_emission_data_verification_gate` alongside the shrink rule, which already has both tuples). That restores the intended 'you may not claim new evidence you do not have' meaning while leaving an unrelated status change permitted. Second, provide a retraction path that works on a wedged row: either permit DISCARD explicitly regardless of the evidence array's validity (a discard is precisely the operation you want available when the array is bad), or add a narrow SECURITY DEFINER RPC restricted to OWNER of the entering org. Closing finding 1 reduces how often this arises but does not fix it — a bad row from any other cause has the same non-exit.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The ACTUAL determination validator treats the emission_data row as its own witness: evidence ids are never resolved and the verifier is never checked for authority
findings.boundary: The determination-validation boundary — the last database-side wall between a shared emission record and a persisted, calculable, filable ACTUAL determination.
findings.precondition: An emission_data row that is ACTIVE + VERIFIED with a non-empty evidence_file_ids array, plus an ACTIVE sharing grant (or own-org ownership). Finding 1 supplies exactly such a row to any MEMBER; but this defect is independent of how the row is created and would still be exploitable if finding 1 were closed and some other route to a bad row existed.
findings.affected_actor: The importer and the regulator. Both are told, by a control specifically built to make the determination trustworthy, that the numbers rest on verified evidence and a named verifier — neither of which the control actually checks.
findings.exploit: L2, in one transaction. Producer MEMBER inserts an ACTIVE+VERIFIED row whose evidence array is `array['not-a-uuid']` — a value that cannot possibly denote an evidence file, since evidence_files.id is uuid. Importer MEMBER then inserts a shipment line carrying an ACTUAL determination whose snapshot repeats `evidence_file_ids: ['not-a-uuid']` and names verifier 1111...0001 (a plain MEMBER of the producer org, not an admin, who performed no verification).
findings.evidence:
`INSERT 0 1` for the emission_data row, `INSERT 0 1` for the shipment line, then:
`L2 determination accepted | 8888...c2 | ["not-a-uuid"]`.
The validator, `app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record`, accepted an ACTUAL determination whose entire evidentiary basis is the four-letter string 'not-a-uuid'. Reading its ACTUAL branch, the evidence check in full is: `if coalesce(array_length(v_ed.evidence_file_ids,1),0) = 0 then return false; end if;` and later a sorted array comparison of `v_snapshot->'evidence_file_ids'` against `v_ed.evidence_file_ids`. There is no join to evidence_files anywhere in the function. The verifier check in full is: `v_ed.verifier_user_id is not distinct from app.try_cast_uuid(v_snapshot->'verification'->>'verifier_user_id')` — an equality against the row's own column, with no membership or role lookup. Corroborating from finding 1: `select count(*) from evidence_files where emission_data_id='5555...e1'` -> `0`, and that determination was accepted too.
findings.why_controls_fail:
The function is a *consistency* checker that has been relied on as an *authenticity* checker. Every one of its ACTUAL-branch tests compares the snapshot against the emission_data row — installation_id, methodology, version, emission_unit, values, verifier_user_id, evidence_file_ids, record_provenance. That correctly stops an importer from fabricating a snapshot around a real record (which is what it was built for, per the forgery-fix v2..v10 series). It cannot stop anything when the record itself is false, because the record is the only oracle it consults.
The two facts it could have checked against independent tables, it does not. `evidence_files` exists, carries `emission_data_id` and `org_id`, and is already joined this way in `emission_data_update_own_org`'s WITH CHECK — the validator simply never does it. `memberships` exists and `app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of` is already written and used by the verification trigger — the validator never asks whether verifier_user_id has any relationship to entered_by_org_id at all.
By contrast the DEFAULT branch of the same function is rigorous to the point of pedantry: it re-derives the resolver's uniqueness rule, checks the OTHER_COUNTRIES_FALLBACK precondition against `default_emission_values`, validates the dataset is ACTIVE, and matches the source row exactly. The asymmetry is the finding. Regulatory defaults are validated against the authoritative dataset; operator-attested actuals are validated against the claim itself.
Downstream, `record_calculation_result` explicitly delegates: it binds the number to whatever determination the line carries and states in its own header that the database cannot verify the number, only make it unforgeable. That reasoning is sound and it makes this validator the load-bearing wall — which is why its two blind spots are HIGH and not MEDIUM.
findings.impact: The phrase 'verified operator data' means, at the database boundary, only 'a row that says so'. An ACTUAL determination can be persisted, calculated and filed against evidence that does not exist and a verifier with no authority, and every artefact downstream — the determination panel, the exports, the audit payloads, the filed declaration — will repeat both claims as fact. This also removes the natural second line of defence against finding 1: even if the INSERT hole is closed, any future route to a bad emission_data row (a migration error, a service_role bug, a different policy gap) passes straight through to a filed figure.
findings.recommendation: In the ACTUAL branch of `app.emission_determination_matches_regulatory_record`, add two checks. (1) Every entry of `v_ed.evidence_file_ids` must resolve: `not exists (select 1 from unnest(v_ed.evidence_file_ids) as claimed where not exists (select 1 from public.evidence_files ef where ef.id = app.try_cast_uuid(claimed) and ef.emission_data_id = v_ed.id and ef.org_id = v_ed.entered_by_org_id))` — the same predicate the UPDATE policy already uses, so no new semantics are introduced. (2) `v_ed.verifier_user_id` must be a non-deactivated OWNER/ADMIN membership of `v_ed.entered_by_org_id`; the function is already SECURITY DEFINER with search_path=public, so it can read memberships directly. Both are cheap, both are checkable in SQL without duplicating any regulatory semantics (the objection that correctly rules out recomputing the engine does not apply here), and either alone would have broken the finding-1 chain before it reached a calculation. Also worth stating plainly in the function's comment which claims it does and does not authenticate, since the current comment block's confidence about record_provenance ('checked here rather than trusted from the writer') reads as covering more than it does.
