findings.title: Trigger enabled state is never compared: three disabled integrity triggers, including the v10 determination validator, and the tool says POSTURE MATCHES — with the forgery then landing
findings.boundary: Recovery verification boundary, and the write-integrity boundary that this schema implements as triggers.
findings.precondition: A restore or bulk load in which triggers are left disabled — `pg_restore --disable-triggers`, `session_replication_role = replica`, or an operator running `ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER` to load data during recovery and not re-enabling. No attacker access is needed to create the state; an ordinary member exploits it.
findings.affected_actor: The regulator and every organisation whose filed declaration is built from a shipment line. A member of the line's own organisation writes an emission determination the resolver never produced, and it flows into the frozen filed snapshot.
findings.exploit:
1. Recovery leaves shipment_lines_validate_emission_determination_trg disabled (and, in my test, emission_data_verification_gate_trg and audit_events_pin_occurred_at_trg with it).
2. Run the documented acceptance test -> POSTURE MATCHES, restore accepted.
3. An ordinary authenticated OWNER/member of the line's organisation issues a plain UPDATE setting emission_determination to a fabricated value. It is accepted.
findings.evidence:
Live, on p14rev_a10_leak, user d7ffd167-fa3d-41f4-aada-d8069d847b23, line 3e76b531-516e-46b2-a735-f73895e32c62, forging emission_factor_tco2_per_t = 0.000001 with resolution.reason = FORGED:

  BEGIN / SET / SET
  ERROR:  shipment_lines: emission_determination failed validation for line 3e76b531-516e-46b2-a735-f73895e32c62
  CONTEXT:  PL/pgSQL function app.validate_emission_determination_write() line 34 at RAISE

=== 2. TRIGGER DISABLED ===
psql -c "alter table public.shipment_lines disable trigger shipment_lines_validate_emission_determination_trg"
  trigger enabled=D
  UPDATE 1
                    id                  | determination_method | resolution_reason |    ef
  --------------------------------------+----------------------+-------------------+----------
   3e76b531-516e-46b2-a735-f73895e32c62 | DEFAULT              | FORGED            | 0.000001

=== 3. THE TOOL'S VERDICT ON A DATABASE IN THAT STATE ===
On p14rev_a10_mut with three triggers disabled:
psql -tAc "select c.relname||'.'||t.tgname||' enabled='||t.tgenabled::text from pg_trigger t join pg_class c on c.oid=t.tgrelid where not t.tgisinternal and t.tgenabled<>'O'"

  emission_data.emission_data_verification_gate_trg enabled=D
  audit_events.audit_events_pin_occurred_at_trg enabled=D
psql -tAc "select pg_get_triggerdef(oid) from pg_trigger where tgname='emission_data_verification_gate_trg'"

node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs <sandbox> <p14rev_a10_mut>
  [MATCH] triggers (22 rows both sides)
  ... all other checks [MATCH]/[OK] ...
  RESULT: POSTURE MATCHES

file:line — scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:183-196, the `triggers` check, selects `t.tgname` and `pg_get_triggerdef(t.oid)`. pg_get_triggerdef does not render the enabled state, and pg_trigger.tgenabled is never read anywhere in the file.
findings.why_controls_fail: The check's own stated rationale at :185 is 'the fact-immutability and append-only walls in this schema are triggers'. It compares the walls' blueprints and never asks whether they are switched on. This is the exact shape of failure the script was written to prevent — the 2026-09-03 lesson was that a control can be present-and-inert — reproduced one layer over. Nothing else compensates: RLS still passes the UPDATE (the member owns the row), the CHECK constraints do not concern the determination JSON, and calculation_results is downstream of a value that is now wrong at source.
findings.impact: After a restore that leaves triggers disabled — a routine recovery mistake, and the tool reports the database as matching — the ten-migration determination-forgery defence, the emission-data verification gate and the audit-event timestamp pin are all inert simultaneously. I landed a fabricated emission factor of 0.000001 on a real line as an ordinary member, which is the exact class this project has already treated as a release blocker three times.
findings.recommendation: Add `|| ' | enabled=' || t.tgenabled::text` to the `triggers` check at :188, and add a self-check that hard-fails on any non-internal trigger in public/app with tgenabled <> 'O'. Both are one-line changes and both are needed — the self-check because a production push has no source database to compare against.

findings.title: Grants to PUBLIC are invisible to both grant checks: TRUNCATE on every public table reaches anon and authenticated while truncate_granted_to_api_roles reports [OK] and the run reports POSTURE MATCHES
findings.boundary: Recovery verification boundary, on the one privilege class (TRUNCATE) that row-level security does not constrain at all.
findings.precondition: Any restore, repair or operator action that grants table privileges to PUBLIC rather than naming the API roles — including a hand-written recovery grant, a third-party tool's bootstrap, or an ACL restored from a source where PUBLIC held them.
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant, and the regulator. `authenticated` and `anon` gain TRUNCATE on audit_events, emission_data, calculation_results, declarations and every other public table — total, unrecoverable destruction of the append-only audit log and of filed evidence, from an ordinary session.
findings.exploit:
1. `grant truncate, insert, update, delete on all tables in schema public to public;` reaches the database by any of the routes above.
2. Run the documented acceptance test. RESULT: POSTURE MATCHES, and truncate_granted_to_api_roles specifically reports [OK].
3. Any authenticated user issues `truncate table public.audit_events cascade;`. RLS does not apply to TRUNCATE.
findings.evidence:
Effective privilege, on p14rev_a10_pub2 (clone of the fresh rebuild + the one PUBLIC grant):
psql -tAc "select 'authenticated TRUNCATE on emission_data: '||has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.emission_data','TRUNCATE')::text"
  authenticated TRUNCATE on emission_data: true
psql -tAc "select 'anon TRUNCATE on audit_events: '||has_table_privilege('anon','public.audit_events','TRUNCATE')::text"
  anon TRUNCATE on audit_events: true
psql -tAc "select 'authenticated INSERT on calculation_results: '||has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.calculation_results','INSERT')::text"
  authenticated INSERT on calculation_results: true

What the check that exists to catch exactly this sees:
psql -tAc "select coalesce(string_agg(table_name||'|'||grantee,', '),'<no rows -- check reports OK>') from information_schema.role_table_grants where table_schema='public' and grantee in ('anon','authenticated') and privilege_type='TRUNCATE'"
  <no rows -- check reports OK>

node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs <sandbox> <p14rev_a10_pub2>
  [MATCH] effective_grants (566 rows both sides)
  ... all 14 [MATCH] ...
  [OK] api_roles_hold_their_grants
  [OK] truncate_granted_to_api_roles
  RESULT: POSTURE MATCHES

And it is executable, not theoretical. On p14rev_a10_trunc (clone of the data-bearing sandbox clone + the PUBLIC grant):
  audit_events rows before: 1738
  begin; set local role authenticated;
  set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"d7ffd167-fa3d-41f4-aada-d8069d847b23","role":"authenticated"}';
  truncate table public.audit_events cascade;
    audit_events rows after truncate, as authenticated: 0
  rollback;
  audit_events rows after rollback: 1738   (verified restored)

file:line — scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:132 (`and grantee in ('anon', 'authenticated', 'service_role', 'postgres')`) and :408 (`and grantee in ('anon', 'authenticated')`). information_schema.role_table_grants materialises grants to PUBLIC under the grantee name 'PUBLIC', which neither IN-list contains, so both checks step straight over them.
findings.why_controls_fail: truncate_granted_to_api_roles exists solely to prove that migration 20260903170000's revoke survived a restore — its `why` at :403 says 'a restore is exactly where a grant silently comes back'. It looks only for the grant coming back under the two role names, and a grant to PUBLIC is precisely a grant coming back under a different name. api_roles_hold_their_grants, the guard that is supposed to stop the TRUNCATE check passing vacuously, also counts only named-role rows, so it is satisfied and adds no protection here. Separately, pg_default_acl is never compared at all, so a rebuild whose ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES include TRUNCATE would hand it to every future table with the same silence.
findings.impact: The P14 TRUNCATE revoke — shipped as a security fix precisely because RLS does not constrain TRUNCATE — can be fully undone while the check written to prove it survived reports OK and the overall run reports POSTURE MATCHES. I destroyed a 1,738-row audit log as an ordinary authenticated user in that state.
findings.recommendation: Change both grant checks to test effective privilege rather than ACL bookkeeping: replace the information_schema enumeration with `has_table_privilege('authenticated', c.oid, 'TRUNCATE')` (and the same for anon, and for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on calculation_results) over every table in public. That is immune to whether the privilege arrives via a role name, PUBLIC, or role membership. Add a comparison check over pg_default_acl at the same time.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.boundary: Recovery/rebuild verification boundary. DEPLOYMENT.md's 'Rebuilding on a fresh database' step 6 names `compare-database-posture.mjs --check` as the way to 'Verify the security posture survived, rather than assuming it'.
findings.precondition: A fresh rebuild or restore in which authenticated regains INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on calculation_results and EXECUTE on record_calculation_result, without also regaining TRUNCATE — e.g. an older seed.sql, a targeted operator grant, or a restored ACL. findings.affected_actor: The regulator and every importer organisation. The trusted-write channel that 20260903190000 restricted to service_role becomes directly callable by any authenticated member.
findings.exploit:

2. Run DEPLOYMENT.md step 6's verification. RESULT: POSTURE MATCHES.
3. The single control the P14.1 blocker fix added is gone, and the verification step designed to notice cannot.

psql -tAc "select 'truncate to api roles: '||count(*)::text from information_schema.role_table_grants where table_schema='public' and grantee in ('anon','authenticated') and privilege_type='TRUNCATE'"
  truncate to api roles: 0

node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs --check "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/p14rev_a10_narrow"
  === Self-consistency checks on the database ===
  [OK] auth_schema_and_helpers_present
  [OK] auth_user_foreign_keys_present
  [OK] policy_functions_resolve
  [OK] tables_without_rls
  [OK] rls_without_policies
  [OK] tables_without_insert_policy
  [OK] api_roles_hold_their_grants
  [OK] truncate_granted_to_api_roles

file:line — the nine SELF_CHECKS are at scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:254, 277, 301, 314, 327, 344, 383, 402, 414. None reads pg_proc.proacl; the only function-grant check is `function_grants` at :169, which exists in comparison mode only and needs a source database that a restore or a production push does not have.
findings.why_controls_fail: seed.sql's own header (supabase/seed.sql:50-60) states the risk precisely — 'a member could simply call the trusted channel directly and pass it any number' — and the coupling comment at :68-77 says the safeguard is a test (tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts). That test runs in CI against a CI-built database; it does not run against a restored production database, which is exactly where the documented verification is --check. So the only control covering the restored case is the one that cannot see it. In partial mitigation, I confirmed the direct table INSERT is still refused by RLS (`ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy for table "calculation_results"`, because the INSERT policy was dropped), and my attempt to drive a forged figure through the re-granted RPC was refused with DETERMINATION_MISMATCH — so this is a proven verification blind spot, not a completed forgery.
findings.impact: The verification step the deployment runbook prescribes for a fresh rebuild cannot detect the reintroduction of the exact defect that shipped as a release blocker fix hours earlier. A rebuilt or restored production database with the trusted-write channel wide open would be signed off as posture-verified.
findings.recommendation: Add two self-checks that need no source database: one asserting `has_table_privilege` is false for anon and authenticated on calculation_results for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and one asserting `has_function_privilege` is false for anon, authenticated and PUBLIC on record_calculation_result. These are the two facts the P14.1 blocker fix rests on and they belong beside the TRUNCATE check they sit next to.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: CHAIN C3 (COMPOSITE, PROVEN LIVE): a plain MEMBER's period edit plus two missing clauses in the filing gate produce two immutable FILED declarations that double-count the same tonnes across two reporting periods — #22 + #20 + #21
findings.boundary: Role boundary (MEMBER changes what an ADMIN's frozen declaration will file) and platform -> regulator (the filed artifact misstates which period the goods belong to, twice).
findings.precondition: A plain MEMBER in the importer org for the period edit; an ADMIN or OWNER to press file, who need not be complicit. No raw member-set editing is required in the version driven by the MEMBER.
findings.affected_actor: The declarant organisation and the regulator. Own-tenant scope, no cross-tenant reach.
findings.exploit: 1. Shipment S sits in period P1 and is READY; declaration D(P1) is drafted and marked READY by the normal service, freezing member_shipment_ids=[S]. 2. A MEMBER PATCHes S's reporting_period_* columns to P2 — shipments_update_own_org_not_terminal role-gates only the LOCKED transition, and the sole trigger on shipments is prevent_org_id_change. 3. generateOrRefreshDeclarationDraft picks S up for D(P2), because it queries shipments by their CURRENT period columns. 4. File D(P1) -> OK; S becomes LOCKED. 5. File D(P2) -> OK, because record_declaration_filed accepts `s.status in ('READY','LOCKED')` unconditionally and never consults supersedes_declaration_id, and never asks whether another FILED_RECORDED declaration already lists S.
findings.evidence:
All live in p14_review_sandbox, one transaction, rolled back (scratchpad/f2021b.sql).

The two filings (as an ADMIN):
  select * from public.record_declaration_filed('f2000000-...-000029','REF-CROSS-PERIOD-2029'); -> OK
  select * from public.record_declaration_filed('f2000000-...-000030','REF-CROSS-PERIOD-2030'); -> OK

The result — two immutable snapshots, same calculation_result_id, two different periods, over a shipment that belongs to neither:
  filed_reference       | period_claimed                                    | total | calc_ids
  REF-CROSS-PERIOD-2029 | {"kind": "ANNUAL", "year": 2029, "quarter": null} | 999   | ["e2000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"]
  REF-CROSS-PERIOD-2030 | {"kind": "ANNUAL", "year": 2030, "quarter": null} | 999   | ["e2000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"]
  shipment: ADV-D-2035 | ANNUAL | 2035 | LOCKED

The MEMBER's period edit, same session:
  set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"a2000000-...-0001","role":"authenticated"}';
  select role as acting_membership_role from memberships where user_id=auth.uid(); -> MEMBER
  update public.shipments set reporting_period_kind='QUARTERLY', reporting_period_year=2033, reporting_period_quarter=2 where id='c2000000-...-0001'; -> UPDATE 1
  ADV-D-2035 | QUARTERLY | 2033 | 2 | READY
ROLLBACK; leaked 0.
findings.why_controls_fail: I read the full prosrc of record_declaration_filed. reporting_period_kind/_year/_quarter appear in the body ONLY inside jsonb_build_object — they are stamped onto filed_snapshot and never compared against the member shipments' own columns. The lockability test is `s.id = any(v_member_ids) and s.org_id = v_decl.org_id and s.status in ('READY','LOCKED')`; the header comment justifies accepting LOCKED only for amendments ('an amendment (supersedes_declaration_id) covers shipments the superseded version already locked'), but the SQL never consults supersedes_declaration_id and there is no uniqueness constraint or lookup preventing a shipment appearing in two FILED declarations. On the shipments side, the RLS policy role-gates the LOCKED transition and nothing else; no trigger pins the period columns. The gate is thorough about whether the NUMBER matches its inputs and silent about what the number is a number OF.
findings.impact: The same goods, the same tonnes and the same calculation are declared twice, in two periods, in immutable artifacts that each cite the same provenance id — and neither period is the one the goods were actually released in. The duplication is discoverable only by cross-reading calculation_result_ids across periods, which nothing in the product does. The period-summary report filters on the shipment's CURRENT period columns, so the report and the filed artifact silently disagree about the same period.
findings.recommendation: In record_declaration_filed, refuse any member shipment whose reporting_period_* does not equal the declaration's, and refuse any member shipment already present in another FILED_RECORDED declaration unless this declaration's supersedes_declaration_id names the one that filed it. Pin shipments.reporting_period_* against UPDATE once the shipment is READY (a BEFORE UPDATE trigger, matching prevent_declaration_fact_change's shape), or restrict that column set to ADMIN/OWNER.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: CHAIN C5 (COMPOSITE): the release's entire verification apparatus is unable to detect its own headline regression — the acceptance gate prints POSTURE MATCHES on a database with the whole P14.1 fix reverted, two of its nine checks fire only at exactly zero, it is run by nothing automated and covered by no test, and no test in the repository asserts a database privilege at all (prior #1 + #37 + #42 + #43 + #39 + #46)
findings.boundary: Operational/recovery boundary. Everything downstream of 'we verified the restore' and 'we verified the deploy'.
findings.precondition: A restore, a rebuild, or a promotion — i.e. the normal operations the runbooks describe. No attacker.
findings.affected_actor: Whoever runs a disaster recovery or a cutover, and every declarant whose declarations are frozen from calculation_results afterwards.
findings.exploit: Restore or provision by any route that re-applies a broad grant after the narrow revokes (a pg_dump/pg_restore round trip records the grants that exist, never their absence; a fresh Supabase project's bootstrap re-runs `grant all on all tables/functions in schema public`; a `psql -f` restore without ON_ERROR_STOP continues past a failed GRANT block). Then run the verification BACKUP_RESTORE.md:530 and DEPLOYMENT.md:574 prescribe — `node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs --check <dsn>` — which is the only available form after a PITR restore because the source is gone. It prints RESULT: POSTURE MATCHES and exits 0, the identical verdict string the full two-DSN comparison prints.
findings.evidence:
I reverted the entire P14.1 output-forgery fix on the sandbox and ran the gate.

BEFORE (candidate posture):
  anon: REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER ; authenticated: REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER
  rcr acl: {postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}

REVERT (all three halves of 20260903190000):
  grant insert, update, delete on public.calculation_results to anon, authenticated;
  grant execute on function public.record_calculation_result(uuid,uuid,uuid,text,jsonb,text,text,jsonb,jsonb,text,uuid) to anon, authenticated;
  create policy calculation_results_insert_own_org_as_self on public.calculation_results for insert to authenticated with check (org_id in (select app.user_org_ids()));
  -> anon: DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,UPDATE ; authenticated: same
  -> rcr acl: {postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres,anon=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres}

THE GATE:
  node scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs --check postgresql://...@127.0.0.1:54322/p14_review_sandbox
  [OK] auth_schema_and_helpers_present
  [OK] auth_user_foreign_keys_present
  [OK] policy_functions_resolve
  [OK] tables_without_rls
  [OK] rls_without_policies
  [OK] tables_without_insert_policy
  [OK] api_roles_hold_their_grants
  [OK] truncate_granted_to_api_roles
  [OK] security_definer_without_search_path
  RESULT: POSTURE MATCHES
(I then restored the candidate posture and re-verified: SELECT/REFERENCES/TRIGGER only, rcr acl postgres+service_role, 1 policy on calculation_results, and the gate still prints POSTURE MATCHES.)

The two exact-zero checks, read from source:
  :277 auth_user_foreign_keys_present — message 'NO product foreign key references auth.users -- expected 10', predicate `... ) = 0`. Nine of ten missing is a pass.
  :383 api_roles_hold_their_grants — `where ... (select count(*) ...) = 0`. One grant out of ~250 surviving is a pass.

Wiring: `grep -rn compare-database-posture .github/ tests/ package.json scripts/` returns hits only in docs and in the script itself. `grep -rn "has_table_privilege|information_schema|role_table_grants|has_function_privilege" --include=*.test.ts` across the repository returns zero matches.
findings.why_controls_fail: calculation_results is explicitly EXEMPTED from tables_without_insert_policy (:344-380 names it in the not-in list, with a comment explaining why). truncate_granted_to_api_roles covers 20260903170000 only. effective_grants and function_grants — the two checks that WOULD have caught this — are comparison checks, skipped entirely in --check mode (:510 `const selfOnly = args[0] === "--check"`). So the one migration whose revoke IS covered is the TRUNCATE one, and the one whose revoke is not is the one that closed a live-reproduced forgery into a filed declaration. Nothing else backstops it: no CI job runs the script, no npm script invokes it, no test covers its 24 queries, and the suite contains no privilege assertion of any kind — the test titled '(4) grants no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on calculation_results to anon or authenticated at all' asserts a behavioural refusal, never a privilege, and constructs no anon client.
findings.impact: The single automated acceptance test standing behind the release's headline security remediation cannot see that remediation, and the operator running it during a recovery — when nobody has time to audit the tool — is told the restore is sound. Two further checks certify POSTURE MATCHES on a database where nine of ten auth.users referential-integrity rules are gone, or where the application is completely unusable because 249 of 250 grants did not survive.
findings.recommendation: Add self-checks for both halves of 20260903190000 (calculation_results holds no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for anon/authenticated; record_calculation_result's ACL names service_role only). Change both exact-zero predicates to compare against expected counts, or better, to name the specific missing objects. Wire `--check` into CI against the freshly built database so the tool is exercised on every run, and give it a negative fixture: a database with a deliberately broken posture that the tool must reject.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: This release's migrations are not additive, so the documented deploy order guarantees a Calculate outage and an application rollback to the recorded known-good SHA leaves it permanently broken — a category ROLLBACK.md does not name (prior #45)
findings.boundary: Operational. Deployed application build <-> promoted schema.
findings.precondition: Following DEPLOYMENT.md exactly, on the release this candidate is.
findings.affected_actor: Every importer member trying to calculate a line during the promotion window, and every user afterwards if the rollback procedure is followed.
findings.exploit: 1. DEPLOYMENT.md:517 step 4 runs `supabase db push`, promoting all pending migrations including 20260903190000. 2. Before :528 step 6 completes, the still-deployed build issues `insert into calculation_results` as the signed-in member; both the policy and the grant are gone, so it fails. 3. If anything goes wrong and ROLLBACK.md §1 is followed to the recorded known-good SHA, the failure becomes permanent: migrations are forward-only (ROLLBACK.md:151) and the old code has no service-role path to record_calculation_result.

  240:      .from("calculation_results")
  241:      .insert(

The migration removes both the policy and the grant. `grep -n 'drop policy|revoke|grant' supabase/migrations/20260903190000_p141_calculation_results_trusted_write_only.sql`:
  144: drop policy if exists calculation_results_insert_own_org_as_self
  147: revoke insert, update, delete on public.calculation_results
  353: revoke all on function public.record_calculation_result(
  357: grant execute on function public.record_calculation_result(

The order. docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md:517 '4. **Dry run, then push.**'; :528 '6. **Only then deploy the application.**'

The taxonomy gap. ROLLBACK.md:159-170 defines the safe case as 'a new nullable column, a new table, a new index, a new RLS policy that doesn't remove a capability the old code relies on'; :171 defines destructive as '(dropped or renamed a column/table the old code reads or writes, tightened a constraint the old code's writes would now violate)'. A DROPPED RLS policy and a REVOKED table grant appear in neither list.
findings.why_controls_fail: ROLLBACK.md's classification is the control, and it is expressed as two enumerations rather than a principle. A reader classifying 20260903190000 against those lists finds no dropped column, no renamed table and no tightened constraint, and reasonably concludes 'additive' — the exact misclassification the section exists to prevent. Master plan §42's escalation requirement for destructive database changes did not fire either, presumably for the same reason.
findings.impact: A guaranteed outage of the platform's core workflow during every promotion of this release, and a rollback procedure that, followed exactly as written including its own 'record the known-good SHA' step, leaves Calculate permanently broken with no documented recovery.
findings.recommendation: Extend ROLLBACK.md's destructive enumeration to name dropped policies and revoked grants explicitly, and better, restate it as the principle: 'any migration that removes a capability the currently-deployed code exercises.' For this release specifically, either deploy the application before pushing 20260903190000, or land a compatibility step (retain the grant for one release, revoke it in the next) so the two halves can move independently.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: Engine unit guard validates magnitude prefixes in the numerator only: 'tCO2e/kilotonne' is accepted as tonne-basis and overstates emissions 1000x, on a field with no CHECK constraint anywhere in the chain (prior #6)
findings.boundary: Data-entry -> calculation engine -> filed figure. Fully UI-reachable; no forgery, no elevated privilege.
findings.precondition: A producer (or an importer entering an IMPORTER_ENTERED record) types a magnitude-prefixed denominator into the free-text emission-unit box.
findings.affected_actor: The declarant, who over-reports and over-surrenders certificates; and the regulator, who receives a figure three orders of magnitude wrong.
findings.exploit: Enter 'tCO2e/kilotonne', 'tCO2e/megatonne', 'tCO2e/short tonne' or (on an energy line) 'tCO2e/kMWh'. Nothing rejects it. An importer determines a line ACTUAL from that record and calculates; the engine returns COMPUTED with a figure 1000x, 1,000,000x or ~10x too large, and it is persisted, reported REPRODUCIBLE by reproduceCalculationResult, and filed.
findings.evidence:
src/domain/calculations/calculate-line-emissions.ts:163-186. The numerator is anchored — `if (!/^TCO2E?(?:\/|_PER_|$)/.test(normalized)) return false;` — but the denominator is a bare substring test: `return netMassTonnes !== null ? normalized.includes("TONNE") || /\/T(?![A-Z0-9])/.test(normalized) : normalized.includes("MWH");`

Evaluating that predicate, transcribed verbatim, in node:
  mass   "tCO2e/t"            -> true
  mass   "tCO2e/tonne"        -> true
  mass   "tCO2e/kilotonne"    -> true    (true value 1/1000 of what is computed)
  mass   "tCO2e/megatonne"    -> true
  mass   "tCO2e/gigatonne"    -> true
  mass   "tCO2e/short tonne"  -> true
  mass   "kgCO2e/t"           -> false   (the P13 numerator fix works)
  energy "tCO2e/MWh"          -> true
  energy "tCO2e/kMWh"         -> true
  energy "tCO2e/GMWh"         -> true

The field is unvalidated end to end. `select con.conname, pg_get_constraintdef(con.oid) from pg_constraint con join pg_class c on c.oid=con.conrelid where c.relname='emission_data'` returns ten constraints and NONE of them mentions emission_unit.
findings.why_controls_fail: The P13 fix closed the numerator half of exactly this class and the file's comment claims the pattern was 'Verified against both the original false-negative and this new false-positive class' — but only numerator cases were tested. The file itself names the real fix and its own status: 'The real fix is an allow-list on EmissionData.emission_unit at entry (a DB CHECK or a small enum) so the engine stops string-sniffing free text at all -- this function remains a stop-gap until that lands, not a permanent design.' It did not land.
findings.impact: A materially wrong regulated figure produced by the trusted path from data that passed every wall, with no error state anywhere. The exploitable direction here is overstatement (understatement via sub-tonne denominators like '/kg' is blocked by the numerator anchor) — but it composes with the emission_data INSERT bypass, where an attacker selects the unit deliberately and can reach understatement by other means. Honest data-entry ambiguity is as likely a trigger as malice: 'tCO2e/kt' is rejected while 'tCO2e/kilotonne' silently computes.
findings.recommendation: Land the allow-list the file names: a CHECK constraint on emission_data.emission_unit (or a small enum), mirroring default_emission_values' own constraint, and delete the string-sniffing. If that must wait, anchor the denominator the way the numerator is anchored — an exact match against a closed set of accepted spellings — and add cases for every prefix above.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: Global emission_data_predecessor_id_uq lets a member of an unrelated organisation permanently and invisibly block a producer from ever recording a corrected emissions figure (prior #12)
findings.boundary: Cross-tenant. Attacker org -> victim org, with no shared object between them.
findings.precondition: The attacker knows the victim's emission_data UUID — which every grantee importer is handed by design through emission_data_select_own_org — and holds any account in any organisation with an installation of its own.
findings.affected_actor: The victim producer organisation, and downstream every importer relying on a corrected figure that can never be published.
findings.exploit: POST one emission_data row entirely inside the attacker's own org, on the attacker's own installation, with predecessor_id set to the victim's record id. It passes emission_data_insert_own_org because every column the policy inspects is the attacker's own; nothing scopes predecessor_id to the same org or installation. From that moment the victim's recordEmissionData for that (installation, period) fails permanently on a unique violation against a row they cannot see, cannot query, and cannot delete.
findings.evidence:
The index is global. `select indexdef from pg_indexes where tablename='emission_data'`:
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX emission_data_predecessor_id_uq ON public.emission_data USING btree (predecessor_id) WHERE (predecessor_id IS NOT NULL)

Live, one transaction, rolled back (scratchpad/f12.sql). Victim org b1200000-...-0001 (its OWNER a1200000-...-0001) holds ACTIVE record e1200000-...-0001. Attacker org b1200000-...-0002, its user a1200000-...-0002 is a MEMBER, with its own operator and installation:

  -- as the attacker
  set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"a1200000-...-0002",...}';
  insert into emission_data (... entered_by_org_id 'b1200000-...-0002', installation_id 'd1200000-...-0002', ..., predecessor_id 'e1200000-...-0001');
  -> INSERT 0 1
  id | entered_by_org_id | predecessor_id
  e1200000-...-00a1 | b1200000-...-0002 | e1200000-...-0001

  -- as the VICTIM OWNER, doing the ordinary product operation
  set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"a1200000-...-0001",...}';
  insert into emission_data (... entered_by_org_id 'b1200000-...-0001', ..., predecessor_id 'e1200000-...-0001', version 2);
  -> ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "emission_data_predecessor_id_uq"
ROLLBACK; leaked 0.

There is no remedy in-product: pg_policy on emission_data lists exactly three policies — insert, select, update. There is NO DELETE policy, so nobody can remove the squatting row through the API, and it lives in a tenancy the victim cannot read.
findings.why_controls_fail: The unique index enforces 'a record has at most one successor', which is a per-lineage invariant expressed as a global one. predecessor_id is the one column on the table that legitimately names a row outside the writer's control, and no policy clause, CHECK or trigger constrains it to the writer's own org or installation. The FK is an ordinary FK, checked with RLS bypassed, so it also functions as a cross-tenant row-existence oracle: a nonexistent uuid returns 'Key is not present in table "emission_data"' while a real one succeeds. Facts are immutable by app.prevent_emission_data_fact_change, so superseding is the ONLY correction path.
findings.impact: A cross-tenant, permanent, invisible denial of the most compliance-critical write in the producer half of the product: correcting a declared emissions figure. The victim sees only an opaque persist failure and has no attribution. Importer/producer counterparties have genuinely adversarial commercial interests, and every grantee is handed the UUID by design.
findings.recommendation: Scope the uniqueness to the lineage's own tenancy: make the index (entered_by_org_id, predecessor_id), and add a policy clause or trigger requiring predecessor_id to name a row with the same installation_id and entered_by_org_id as the new row. Consider translating the FK violation into a non-oracular error at the application boundary.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: cn_scope is unvalidated free text and the coverage test is a bare prefix match — one character scopes an entire HS chapter, and the EMPTY STRING covers every CN code in the catalogue (prior #26, MEDIUM -> HIGH)
findings.boundary: Cross-tenant, producer -> importer, through the sharing grant and the determination validator.
findings.precondition: A producer records one verified emission_data row with a coarse (or empty) cn_scope entry; the importer holds an ACTIVE sharing grant. Or, combined with the INSERT bypass, a single member does both halves.
findings.affected_actor: The importer whose line is matched to an emission value never measured for that good, and the regulator receiving the resulting figure.
findings.exploit: Enter '7' (or, via raw PostgREST, '') in the free-text comma-separated cn_scope field. Any importer holding an ACTIVE grant for that installation can then set that single record as the ACTUAL determination for any shipment line whose cn_code starts with 7 — attaching, for example, a low-intensity aluminium record to a high-intensity steel line. The validator's cn-scope test is `bool_or(app.code_prefix_covers(scope_entry, p_cn_code))` over unnest(cn_scope), which passes; every other gate (ACTIVE, VERIFIED, evidence present, grant present, snapshot fields match) is satisfied by the genuine record.
findings.evidence:
Live on p14_review_sandbox:
  select app.code_prefix_covers('7','72081000'), app.code_prefix_covers('7','76011000'), app.code_prefix_covers('2','28041000'), app.code_prefix_covers('','72081000');
  -> t | t | t | t

The empty-string case is the one the prior pass did not report, and it is the strongest: an empty scope entry covers EVERY code in the catalogue. The function's own SQL makes it inevitable — `length('') < length(code) and left(code, 0) = ''` is unconditionally true.

No constraint anywhere:
  select count(*) from pg_constraint where conrelid='public.emission_data'::regclass and pg_get_constraintdef(oid) ilike '%cn_scope%'; -> 0

And I used cn_scope='{7}' in both proven interaction chains (C1 and C2) — in C1 it let one forged record back an ACTUAL determination on CN 72081000; in C2 the forger broadened the genuine record's scope from {7208} to {7} in the same statement that halved its numbers.
findings.why_controls_fail: The application layer rejects only an EMPTY ARRAY (manage-emission-data.ts, EMPTY_CN_SCOPE) and the server action filters entries with `code.length > 0` — which stops the empty string through the form but not through PostgREST, and stops nothing about '7'. The database has no CHECK on the array's elements. app.code_prefix_covers is doing exactly what it says; the defect is that nothing constrains what it is asked to cover.
findings.impact: A good is matched to an emission value that was never measured for it, producing a filed figure carrying real verification provenance attached to the wrong product. As an amplifier it is severe: it turns one forged or one coarse record into a determination source for the entire catalogue.
findings.recommendation: CHECK constraint on emission_data.cn_scope: every element must be non-empty, digits only, and at least four characters (an HS heading). Mirror it in the zod schema and in cn-scope-covers-code.ts. Reject the empty string explicitly rather than relying on a length filter in one server action.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: good_sector is a calculation input that is neither frozen on the row nor re-checked at filing (prior #5)
findings.boundary: Role boundary within a tenant, into the filed regulatory record.
findings.precondition: An ordinary member of the importer org with raw PostgREST access and an emission_data record whose cn_scope covers both an Annex II code and a non-Annex-II one — trivially satisfied given the cn_scope finding above.
findings.affected_actor: The declarant's own filed declaration and the regulator.
findings.exploit: Calculate the line under one sector (the engine applies or omits the Annex II direct-only rule accordingly), then PATCH the line's cn_code to a good in the other sector — the trigger nulls the determination — then PATCH the byte-identical determination back. The filing gate's uncalculated_count is 0 because determination, quantity and quantity_unit all still match, and the figure the engine would now produce is different from the one frozen.
findings.evidence:
The input is derived live and dropped on the floor. src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts:215-223 computes `const goodSector = line.emission_determination?.method === "ACTUAL" ? await resolveGoodSectorForActualLine(...) : null;` and passes it into calculateLineEmissions at :224-233 — and then the writer call at :283-299 passes org_id, line_id, calculated_by_user_id, engine_version, parameter_datasets, quantity, quantity_unit, determination, steps, embedded_emissions_tco2e and correlation_id. No sector. No cn_code.

The row cannot hold it. `select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name='calculation_results'` -> id, org_id, line_id, shipment_id, engine_version, parameter_datasets, quantity, quantity_unit, determination, steps, embedded_emissions_tco2e, certificates_due, liability_amount, liability_currency, calculated_at, calculated_by_user_id, correlation_id.

The RPC cannot accept it. `pg_get_function_arguments` for record_calculation_result -> (p_org_id uuid, p_line_id uuid, p_calculated_by_user_id uuid, p_engine_version text, p_parameter_datasets jsonb, p_quantity text, p_quantity_unit text, p_determination jsonb, p_steps jsonb, p_embedded_emissions_tco2e text, p_correlation_id uuid).

The filing gate cannot check it. I read record_declaration_filed's full prosrc: member_line_counts compares `c.determination is distinct from ml.emission_determination`, `c.quantity is distinct from coalesce(ml.net_mass_tonnes, ml.quantity_mwh)` and `c.quantity_unit is distinct from (case ...)`. cn_code and sector appear nowhere in the function.
findings.why_controls_fail: 20260903110000 was written to close exactly this shape for QUANTITY — its own comment says a calculation row 'carrying the line's exact current determination with a smaller quantity passes both the determination comparison above and reproduceCalculationResult'. The same reasoning applies verbatim to the third engine input and was not extended to it. reproduceCalculationResult WOULD catch it (it re-derives sector from the current cn_code), but it is on-demand and per-row and is not consulted at filing.
findings.impact: A filed declaration carries an embedded-emissions figure the running engine would not produce from the line as it now stands, frozen into an immutable snapshot. Not reachable through the UI (a UI re-determination stamps a fresh resolved_at and correctly shows LINE_CALCULATION_STALE), but reachable with nothing more than an ordinary member's own credentials over raw PostgREST.
findings.recommendation: Add cn_code (or the resolved good_sector, or both) to calculation_results and to record_calculation_result's parameter list, and extend the filing gate's uncalculated_count predicate to compare the frozen value against the line's current cn_code the way it already compares quantity. Freezing the input is the fix; re-deriving it at filing time is a weaker second-best.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The evidence storage.objects DELETE policy carries no verification gate, so the evidence document itself can be deleted from behind an intact, VERIFIED record with every database check still passing (prior #18)
findings.boundary: Cross-tenant harm from an own-tenant action: the producer deletes, the importer and the regulator lose the document.
findings.precondition: Any member of the producing organisation, using the ordinary Storage client.
findings.affected_actor: The importer relying on the evidence, and the regulator auditing the filed declaration.
findings.exploit: supabase.storage.from('evidence').remove(['<own-org-id>/<emission-data-id>/<file>.pdf']) against a VERIFIED, ACTIVE record. The evidence_files metadata row survives (locked by 20260829560000), emission_data.evidence_file_ids is unchanged, and the determination validator therefore still returns true — the importer's determination keeps validating while the document it attests to no longer exists.
findings.evidence:
PARTIAL — policy source only; see 'could_not_test'. The current definition, from supabase/migrations/20260829410000_p11_review_evidence_storage_path_and_uuid_cast_hardening.sql:136-143 (which drops and replaces the 20260829240000 original):
  create policy evidence_storage_delete_own_org
      on storage.objects
      for delete
      to authenticated
      using (
          bucket_id = 'evidence'
          and app.try_cast_uuid((storage.foldername(name))[1]) in (select app.user_org_ids())
      );
Org membership and nothing else.

Contrast the metadata-row policy, read live from pg_policy on evidence_files:
  evidence_files_delete_own_org | d | ((org_id IN (SELECT app.user_org_ids())) AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM emission_data ed WHERE ed.id = evidence_files.emission_data_id AND ed.verification_status <> 'VERIFIED')))
The verification gate is on the metadata row and was never added to the object.

I could not exercise it: `select p.polname ... join pg_namespace n ... where n.nspname='storage'` on the sandbox returns zero policies, and supabase/config.toml:170 has `[storage] enabled = false`.
findings.why_controls_fail: 20260829560000 added the verification condition to the metadata delete policy with an explicit rationale — 'Deleting evidence out from under a VERIFIED record silently invalidates the verifier's own basis for approving it, for a record that may already be consumed cross-org via an active sharing grant.' The three storage.objects policies were last touched in 20260829410000 and were never revisited after that reasoning was established. The two halves of the same object are governed by policies written five migrations apart.
findings.impact: The one control the whole evidence model rests on — that a verified figure has a retrievable supporting document — is bypassable without touching Postgres, and unlike the metadata path it leaves NO trace in the database: every DB-level check still passes, the validator still returns true, and the cited evidence simply 404s under audit.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the metadata policy: add `and not exists (select 1 from evidence_files ef join emission_data ed on ed.id = ef.emission_data_id where ef.storage_path = storage.objects.name and ed.verification_status = 'VERIFIED')` (or the equivalent via the path's emission_data_id segment). Then get storage enabled locally or, failing that, add a CI case that exercises this exact delete — CI does enable storage.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: Offboarding or demoting an administrator does not revoke the invitations they issued, and (chained) an admin can mint one that never expires — a permanent re-entry path that survives every action the product offers for removal (prior #29 + #32, reported as the chain)
findings.boundary: Role/identity boundary within a tenant. Offboarding is the control; it is incomplete.
findings.precondition: A departing or compromised ADMIN, acting before they lose access. For the unbounded variant, raw PostgREST rather than the product's invite form.
findings.affected_actor: The organisation that believes it has revoked the administrator's access, and every producer whose shared verified data that org can read.
findings.exploit: Before losing access, the ADMIN invites an address they control at role ADMIN, and sets expires_at far in the future (the INSERT policy constrains org, inviter and status but not expires_at, whose 7-day value is only a column DEFAULT). The organisation then removes, deactivates or demotes them — none of those touches organization_invitations. At any later time the invitation is accepted and mints a fresh ADMIN membership.
findings.evidence:
The accept path never re-checks the inviter. I read the full prosrc of public.accept_organization_invitation: it tests `v_invite.status = 'ACCEPTED'`, `v_invite.status <> 'PENDING'`, `v_invite.expires_at < now()`, and the caller's confirmed email — `invited_by` appears nowhere in the body.

Nothing else covers it:
  select count(*) from pg_trigger t join pg_class c on c.oid=t.tgrelid where c.relname='organization_invitations' and not t.tgisinternal; -> 0
  grep -c "organization_invitations" src/application/organizations/manage-membership.ts -> 0

The expiry is client-controllable. From pg_policy:
  organization_invitations_insert_admin_or_owner | a | WITH CHECK: (app.user_is_admin_or_owner_of(org_id) AND (invited_by = auth.uid()) AND (status = 'PENDING'))
No expires_at clause. The read-side guard that DOES depend on it — organization_invitations_select_own_email's `(status='PENDING') AND (expires_at > now()) AND lower(email)=lower(coalesce(app.user_confirmed_email(),''))` — therefore never fires for such a row.
findings.why_controls_fail: Membership management and invitation management are separate subsystems with no referential relationship between them at either layer: no trigger, no application call, no audit event linking a removal to the orphaned invitations that removal should have killed. 20260829380000's own header treats the 7-day expiry as a security control ('an invitation that lapsed months ago still discloses the target org's name/id/role indefinitely to anyone who later controls that mailbox'), and the policy that would enforce it does not constrain the column.
findings.impact: Offboarding is not complete. The re-entered account is ADMIN: full read of the organisation's shipments, emissions and producers' shared verified data, and the ability to file declarations. The chain converts a 7-day window into an unbounded one. The Team screen does list pending invitations, so an attentive admin can spot the planted row — but nothing forces that and nothing warns.
findings.recommendation: In accept_organization_invitation, re-check that invited_by still holds an active ADMIN/OWNER membership of v_invite.org_id at acceptance time and return a distinct status if not. Independently, revoke an org's pending invitations issued by a member being removed, deactivated or demoted, from manage-membership.ts, with an audit event. Add `expires_at <= now() + interval '7 days'` to the INSERT policy's WITH CHECK.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: /auth/callback silently establishes an attacker-supplied session from the URL fragment with no identity-switch confirmation — while /auth/confirm, in the same codebase, requires an explicit Continue press for the same operation (prior #31, MEDIUM -> HIGH)
findings.boundary: Session/identity boundary. Login CSRF into a compliance product.
findings.precondition: The victim opens an attacker-supplied link on the real product origin. No credential theft, no XSS, no same-origin compromise.
findings.affected_actor: Any user of the platform, and the organisation whose data they then enter.
findings.exploit: The attacker signs in as themselves, captures their own access_token/refresh_token, and sends the victim `https://<app>/auth/callback#access_token=<attacker>&refresh_token=<attacker>`. On mount the page calls establishSessionAction with those values; the SERVER client's setSession writes real Set-Cookie headers the browser cannot refuse; router.replace sends the victim onward. The victim now browses the product as the attacker with no visible transition.
findings.why_controls_fail: The session-fixation guard was added to /auth/confirm and never applied to /auth/callback, which is still the live redirect target for both sign-up and password reset. Doing setSession server-side is deliberate and correct for the legitimate flow, and it is exactly what makes the illegitimate one irrefusable by the browser. isSafeRedirectPath does hold, so the redirect cannot leave the origin — which confines the attack to the real product and makes it credible rather than obvious.
findings.impact: Whatever the victim does next — creating shipments, entering emissions figures, uploading evidence PDFs — lands in the attacker's organisation, where the attacker reads it. In a product whose entire value is the confidentiality and integrity of commercially sensitive emissions data, that is a serious loss. I upgrade from the prior MEDIUM because the code is unconditional, present in every build, and the correct pattern is already implemented twenty files away.
findings.recommendation: Apply /auth/confirm's guard to /auth/callback: read the current session first, and if one exists for a different identity, render the identity-switch warning and require an explicit press before calling establishSessionAction. Better, do not accept session material from the fragment at all on this route — use the PKCE code exchange path exclusively.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: A pending invitee's account can be taken over by anyone who knows the invited address, because local email confirmation is stamped at signup (prior #28)
findings.boundary: Identity boundary: 'this person controls that mailbox' is the only thing standing between an invitation and a membership.
findings.precondition: Knowledge of an invited email address and the public anon key.
findings.affected_actor: The invited person, and the organisation whose membership is minted.
findings.exploit: POST /auth/v1/signup with the invited address. If the account is created already-confirmed, app.user_confirmed_email() returns that address, organization_invitations_select_own_email makes the invitation visible, and accept_organization_invitation mints the membership at the invited role.
findings.evidence:
NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED IN THIS PASS — there is no Auth service bound to p14_review_sandbox and I did not issue any HTTP request to a GoTrue endpoint. I confirmed the downstream half only, from the live catalog: organization_invitations_select_own_email's USING clause is `((status = 'PENDING') AND (expires_at > now()) AND (lower(email) = lower(COALESCE(app.user_confirmed_email(), ''))))`, and accept_organization_invitation's body validates existence, PENDING status, expiry and the caller's confirmed email — nothing more. So the entire acceptance path turns on app.user_confirmed_email(), i.e. on auth.users.email_confirmed_at.

I am reporting this at HIGH on the prior pass's measured evidence (email_confirmed_at set 426 ms after created_at, confirmation_sent_at NULL, on users the Playwright suite created through the app's own sign-up form) while stating plainly that I did not re-derive it.
findings.why_controls_fail: The invitation model correctly refuses to trust a client-supplied identity and instead trusts email confirmation. That is the right design and it inherits whatever the Auth configuration actually enforces. If confirmation is auto-stamped, the single control the whole invitation flow rests on is absent, and 20260829460000's onboarding email-confirmation hardening does not help because the flag it reads is already true.
findings.impact: An invited ADMIN membership can be claimed by whoever guesses or learns the address, from the public anon key alone.
findings.recommendation: Verify the hosted project's own confirmation setting directly (I deliberately did not probe production) and make it an asserted, tested invariant rather than a configuration assumption — e.g. a CI check that a freshly signed-up local user has email_confirmed_at NULL, and an application-side refusal to accept an invitation for an account whose confirmation_sent_at is NULL.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: Two of the posture comparator's nine self-checks fire only at EXACTLY zero, so nine of ten lost auth.users foreign keys, or 249 of 250 lost grants, certify as POSTURE MATCHES (prior #42 + #43)
findings.boundary: Operational/recovery.
findings.precondition: A partial restore — the case both checks exist to catch.
findings.affected_actor: The operator running the pre-cutover gate, and everyone downstream of a database certified sound.
findings.exploit: BACKUP_RESTORE.md's own D.2 case: auth.users restored incompletely from the provider backup so only some FKs can be created; or a `psql -f` restore without ON_ERROR_STOP that continues past a partially failed GRANT block, which is the documented restore command shape.
findings.evidence:
scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs, read at the candidate.

:277 auth_user_foreign_keys_present — the message and the predicate disagree:
      select 'NO product foreign key references auth.users -- expected 10'
      where ( select count(*) from pg_constraint con ... where con.contype='f' and cn.nspname='auth' and c.relname='users' and rn.nspname in ('public','app') ) = 0
  Ten expected; fires at zero. Nine missing is [OK].

:383 api_roles_hold_their_grants — same shape:
      from pg_roles r where r.rolname in ('anon','authenticated','service_role')
        and ( select count(*) from information_schema.role_table_grants g where g.table_schema='public' and g.grantee = r.rolname ) = 0
  Its own `why` at :384 claims it 'catches a --no-privileges restore' and that without it 'the TRUNCATE check below passes vacuously on a database that has no grants at all.' A near-total grant loss is not a no-grant loss, and the check it exists to keep honest is not kept honest.

I did not re-run the prior pass's throwaway-database demonstration (I created no additional databases), but the predicates are unambiguous and I read both in full. I did independently confirm the surrounding claim on the sandbox: with the entire P14.1 fix reverted, all nine checks print [OK] and the script prints RESULT: POSTURE MATCHES.
findings.why_controls_fail: The comment above the FK check (:280-285) explains that an earlier version 'passed on a project holding none of this application's schema at all. That is the same vacuous-pass this file exists to prevent.' The rewrite narrowed the SCOPE and left the exact-zero THRESHOLD in place — it fixed the wrong half of its own lesson. This makes three checks in the file whose `why` string promises more than its SQL delivers (the third is `sequences`, which compares names and not values while claiming to detect a wrong restored value).
findings.impact: An operator running the documented pre-cutover gate on a database that lost nine of ten referential-integrity rules on auth.users, or that no user can read a shipment from, is told the restore is sound. Those FKs are what stop a membership, an audit event or a calculation result naming a user that does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Compare against expected counts, or better, enumerate the missing objects by name so the message and the predicate cannot drift apart again. Add a negative fixture that deliberately drops one FK and one grant and asserts the tool rejects it.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: record_declaration_filed never checks that member shipments belong to the declaration's reporting period (prior #20)
findings.boundary: Platform -> regulator. The filed artifact misattributes goods to a period.
findings.precondition: An ADMIN/OWNER of the importer org over raw PostgREST, or — with no raw member-set edit at all — a plain MEMBER moving a READY shipment's period between markDeclarationReady and filing.
findings.affected_actor: The declarant and the regulator.
findings.exploit: PATCH /rest/v1/declarations?id=eq.<draft> with {"member_shipment_ids":[<any own-org shipment ids>],"completeness_report":{...},"status":"READY"} — declarations_update_own_org_pre_filing permits DRAFT->READY with arbitrary column values — then POST /rest/v1/rpc/record_declaration_filed.
findings.evidence:
I read record_declaration_filed's full prosrc from pg_proc. The only membership test on shipments is:
    select count(*) into v_lockable_count
    from public.shipments s
    where s.id = any(v_member_ids)
      and s.org_id = v_decl.org_id
      and s.status in ('READY', 'LOCKED');
reporting_period_kind / _year / _quarter appear in the body ONLY inside jsonb_build_object, i.e. only to STAMP the period onto filed_snapshot, never to verify it.

Live (see chain C3 for the full transcript): a shipment recorded as ANNUAL 2035 was filed into an ANNUAL 2029 declaration, returning OK, with the snapshot reading period_claimed {"kind": "ANNUAL", "year": 2029, "quarter": null} and total 999.

Both tables carry the columns, so the comparison is trivially available: shipments has reporting_period_kind/_year/_quarter, declarations has the same three.
findings.why_controls_fail: 20260903110000 was written to close 'a wall that checks the number but not what the number is a number OF' for quantity, and did so thoroughly. The same class for period was not considered. The completeness report computed at READY time is a snapshot the gate never re-derives against the period.
findings.impact: filed_snapshot — the archived, immutable, legally meaningful artifact the product exists to produce — can attribute a reporting period's emissions to goods released in an entirely different period, with a fully consistent audit trail and nothing in the payload a later reader could use to detect it.
findings.recommendation: Add `and s.reporting_period_kind = v_decl.reporting_period_kind and s.reporting_period_year = v_decl.reporting_period_year and s.reporting_period_quarter is not distinct from v_decl.reporting_period_quarter` to the lockability test, returning a distinct status so the operator learns why.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The same shipment and the same calculation_results row can be frozen into two different FILED declarations for two different reporting periods (prior #21)
findings.boundary: Platform -> regulator. Double counting across periods.
findings.precondition: An ADMIN/OWNER to press file twice; the member-set can be assembled without any raw edit if a MEMBER moves the shipment's period between the two READY marks.
findings.affected_actor: The declarant and the regulator.
findings.exploit: File D(P1) — the shipment becomes LOCKED. File D(P2), which lists the same shipment. `s.status in ('READY','LOCKED')` accepts LOCKED unconditionally, so the second filing succeeds and freezes the identical emissions into a second immutable snapshot.
findings.evidence:
Live, one transaction, rolled back (scratchpad/f2021b.sql):
  record_declaration_filed('f2000000-...-000029','REF-CROSS-PERIOD-2029') -> OK
  record_declaration_filed('f2000000-...-000030','REF-CROSS-PERIOD-2030') -> OK
  filed_reference       | period_claimed                                    | total | calc_ids
  REF-CROSS-PERIOD-2029 | {"kind": "ANNUAL", "year": 2029, "quarter": null} | 999   | ["e2000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"]
  REF-CROSS-PERIOD-2030 | {"kind": "ANNUAL", "year": 2030, "quarter": null} | 999   | ["e2000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"]
Two independent FILED_RECORDED declarations, different periods, citing the identical calculation_result_id as provenance for both.
findings.why_controls_fail: The function's own header justifies accepting LOCKED only for amendments — 'an amendment (supersedes_declaration_id) covers shipments the superseded version already locked' — but v_decl.supersedes_declaration_id is never consulted in the lockability test, and nothing anywhere asks whether another FILED_RECORDED declaration already lists this shipment. The comment states an invariant the SQL does not enforce.
findings.impact: The same goods, the same tonnes and the same calculation are declared twice. Both artifacts are immutable and both cite the same provenance id, so the duplication is discoverable only by cross-reading calculation_result_ids across periods — which nothing in the product does.
findings.recommendation: Accept a LOCKED member shipment only when this declaration's supersedes_declaration_id names the declaration that locked it, and refuse any member shipment already present in a FILED_RECORDED declaration's member_shipment_ids otherwise.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The only live secret scan cannot match SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD= or postgres://user:pass@ at all
findings.boundary: Committed-credential gate
findings.precondition: The build-and-test scan being dead (previous finding). Given that, fast-gates (ci.yml:109-117) is the only secret scan that executes to a meaningful verdict.
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant, and the hosted Supabase project, if a database password or connection string is ever committed.
findings.exploit: Commit a file containing `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD="Hunter2SuperSecretValue"` or `DB=postgresql://admin:RealProdPassword123@db.example.com:5432/app`. Push. The fast-gates PATTERN at ci.yml:112 contains only four alternations — eyJ..., sk-..., re_..., sb_(publishable|secret)_... — and none of them can match either shape. The step prints 'Secret scan clean.' and exits 0.
findings.evidence:
Built a throwaway git repo under the scratchpad containing exactly those two lines, then ran the fast-gates step body verbatim:
  $ bash run.sh
  Secret scan clean.
  FASTGATES_EXIT=0
Ran the build-and-test PATTERN (ci.yml:565) over the same repo to prove the coverage really is lost rather than redundant:
  GIT_GREP_EXIT=0
  RAW_MATCHES:
  leaked.env:1:SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD="Hunter2SuperSecretValue"
  leaked.env:2:DB=postgresql://admin:RealProdPassword123@db.example.com:5432/app
Both shapes are matched by the dead scan and by nothing else.
findings.why_controls_fail: The workflow appears to have defence in depth — two secret scans — but they are not equivalent. The P11 secrets-hygiene audit deliberately ADDED the quoted-assignment and raw-connection-string clauses to the build-and-test pattern (ci.yml:509-541 documents the reasoning at length, including 'exactly the shape a YAML/JSON config or a shell script would use'). fast-gates was never given them. The redundancy is therefore illusory: the strong scan is dead and the surviving scan is the pre-P11 shape.
findings.impact: The single highest-value credential in this system — SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD, which combined with supabase/.temp/pooler-url yields a direct superuser Postgres connection to the production regulatory project — can be committed and pushed with a fully green fast-gates job.
findings.recommendation: Make the two steps share one pattern and one allowlist (a single checked-in script both jobs invoke), rather than two hand-maintained copies that have already diverged. Add a fixture-based self-test as described in the previous finding.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: The live secret scan silently becomes a no-op if its regex is ever malformed — the exact defect the dead scan documents fixing
findings.boundary: Committed-credential gate
findings.precondition: Any future edit to PATTERN at ci.yml:112 that produces a regex git grep rejects (an unbalanced paren, a bad class). No attacker action needed — a maintainer typo suffices.
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant; the gate stops examining anything while continuing to report success.
findings.exploit: Append a broken alternation to the fast-gates PATTERN. git grep exits 128 and writes a fatal error to stderr; its stdout is empty, so the downstream `grep -vF` exits 1; under `set -o pipefail` the pipeline status is non-zero; the `if` at ci.yml:113 is therefore FALSE; control falls through to ci.yml:117 which prints 'Secret scan clean.' and the step exits 0.
findings.evidence:
Same throwaway repo (still containing the two leaked credential lines), fast-gates step body with `|(unclosed` appended to PATTERN:
  $ bash run3.sh
  fatal: command line, 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|re_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|sb_(publishable|secret)_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}|(unclosed': Unmatched ( or \(
  Secret scan clean.
  FASTGATES_MALFORMED_EXIT=0
findings.why_controls_fail: ci.yml:570-582 identifies this precise failure mode — 'that same `|| true` also silently absorbed git grep exiting 128 on a malformed PATTERN... the step would print "no secrets found" and exit 0 -- this security gate quietly becoming a no-op on its own future edit' — and fixes it by capturing GIT_GREP_EXIT and rejecting anything above 1. That fix was applied to the build-and-test copy ONLY. fast-gates, added later as the container-free job, was written in the original single-pipeline form and inherits the known bug. The remediation was never propagated, and because the fixed copy is dead, the unfixed copy is the one actually running.
findings.impact: The remaining secret gate is one typo away from a permanently green no-op, with the same fail-open direction and the same near-invisible symptom (a stderr line in a green step).
findings.recommendation: Port the GIT_GREP_EXIT check to fast-gates, or better, collapse both steps into one shared script so a fix can only be applied once.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: The surviving fast-gates secret scan silently passes when its own regex is malformed — the exact defect ci.yml:572-585 claims was fixed
findings.boundary: CI quality gate -> repository secret hygiene
findings.precondition: A future edit to the PATTERN literal at ci.yml:112 that makes it an invalid ERE (unbalanced bracket/paren). No attacker action required beyond an ordinary maintenance edit.
findings.affected_actor: Same as above — this is the only secret scan that still executes at all, given the BLOCKER above.
findings.exploit: Edit ci.yml:112's PATTERN so it is not a valid ERE (e.g. adding an alternative with an unmatched `[`). `git grep` then exits 128 and writes a fatal error to stderr; the `if` at ci.yml:113 sees a non-zero pipeline status, takes the else path, and the step prints "Secret scan clean." and exits 0. Every genuinely committed secret in the tree is now invisible to both jobs.
findings.evidence:
$ cat /tmp/p14rev/fg128.sh
set -euo pipefail
PATTERN='eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|sk-[(BROKEN'
if git grep -InE "$PATTERN" -- . ':!pnpm-lock.yaml' ':!.github/workflows/ci.yml' | grep -vF 'eyJpc3MiOiJzdXBhYmFzZS1kZW1vIiwicm9sZSI6'; then
  echo "::error::Possible committed secret found."
  exit 1
fi
echo "Secret scan clean."
$ bash /tmp/p14rev/fg128.sh; echo "FASTGATES_MALFORMED_EXIT=$?"
fatal: command line, 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|sk-[(BROKEN': Unmatched [ or [^
Secret scan clean.
FASTGATES_MALFORMED_EXIT=0

(raw `git grep` with that pattern independently returns exit 128, confirming the status exists and is discarded.)

Contrast — the build-and-test job's explicit guard, run on the same broken pattern, behaves correctly:
$ bash /tmp/p14rev/exitcap.sh; echo "EXIT=$?"
captured GIT_GREP_EXIT=128
BROKEN-SCAN GUARD FIRES (correct)
EXIT=1

file:line — .github/workflows/ci.yml:113 (single-pipeline `if git grep ... | grep -vF ...` form). The fix for precisely this failure mode is documented at ci.yml:572-585 and applied only in the other job.
findings.why_controls_fail: `set -o pipefail` is set at ci.yml:111 and does propagate a non-zero status — but the status is consumed by the `if` condition, where non-zero means "no secrets", not "the scan broke". The two meanings are conflated by construction. The repository already identified and fixed this exact conflation in the other job (ci.yml:586-597) and did not backport it to the job created later in the 2026-09-02 split.
findings.impact: The last remaining secret scan can be reduced to a no-op by a routine regex edit, with no signal in the job log other than one stderr line among thousands. Combined with the BLOCKER above, the project would then have zero working secret-hygiene coverage while both jobs report green.
findings.recommendation: Backport the explicit exit-code check from ci.yml:586-597 into the fast-gates step: capture `git grep`'s status, fail on >1, and only treat 0/1 as found/not-found. Alternatively delete the fast-gates copy and make the (repaired) build-and-test scan the single source of truth, so there is one scanner to keep correct rather than two that drift.
findings.reviewer_note: Reproduced directly by the reviewing session with its own psql/CLI probes, not taken from an agent report.

findings.title: The E2E gate cannot fail on a flaky test: retries:2 with no failOnFlakyTests means a genuinely broken assertion exits 0
findings.boundary: End-to-end journey gate (importer, producer, cross-org sharing, actual-data determination)
findings.precondition: A test that fails on its first attempt and passes on a retry — which playwright.config.ts's own comments say is a standing, observed condition in this suite.
findings.affected_actor: Every tenant relying on the cross-org sharing and determination journeys being verified before release.
findings.exploit: Any intermittent defect — a race in the sharing-grant acceptance path, a determination that occasionally resolves against stale data — fails attempt 1 and passes attempt 2. Playwright records it as 'flaky' and exits 0. `pnpm exec playwright test` (ci.yml:455) therefore succeeds and the job is green.
findings.why_controls_fail: The config's own comment argues retries absorb 'a genuine transient concurrency blip without masking a test that is actually, persistently broken -- that would still fail all three attempts.' That reasoning is sound only for a test that is broken 100% of the time. It is exactly wrong for an intermittent PRODUCT defect, which is the failure class that matters most in a multi-tenant compliance system, and which the same comment admits exists ('a residual single-spec flake under real concurrent load survived even at workers=3, cleared on retry every time it was observed'). Retries were tuned until that signal disappeared.
findings.impact: The E2E suite — the only gate that exercises real cross-org sharing and determination end to end — structurally converts intermittent correctness failures into passes. A race that leaks or mis-attributes data one run in three ships green.
findings.recommendation: Set `failOnFlakyTests: true` in playwright.config.ts so retries still stabilise the run but a flake is recorded as a job failure; or, at minimum, add a CI step that parses the Playwright JSON report and fails when the flaky count is non-zero. Keep retries for diagnosis, not for the verdict.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The Storage availability assertion produces "000000" on total unavailability and passes
findings.boundary: Precondition gate ensuring the evidence-storage RLS tests actually execute
findings.precondition: Kong/Storage unreachable or slower than the 5 s --max-time budget at the moment the step runs.
findings.affected_actor: Everyone relying on 20260829510000's bucket size/MIME limits and 20260829410000's storage.objects policies being genuinely exercised rather than shim-verified.
findings.exploit: When curl cannot complete the request it BOTH writes `000` via `-w '%{http_code}'` AND exits non-zero, which triggers the `|| echo "000"` fallback. The two concatenate. STORAGE_CODE becomes the string "000000", which equals neither "503" nor "000", so the guard at ci.yml:334-337 does not fire and the step reports Storage as up.
findings.evidence:
Ran the step's exact line against an unreachable port:
  set -euo pipefail
  STORAGE_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:1/storage/v1/bucket || echo "000")
  echo "STORAGE_CODE=[${STORAGE_CODE}]"
  if [ "${STORAGE_CODE}" = "503" ] || [ "${STORAGE_CODE}" = "000" ]; then echo '::error::...'; exit 1; fi
  echo "GATE PASSED -- storage considered up"
Output:
  STORAGE_CODE=[000000]
  GATE PASSED -- storage considered up
  EXIT=0
Source line: .github/workflows/ci.yml:332.
findings.why_controls_fail: The step's comment (ci.yml:~329-331) states '503 is what an unhealthy/absent Storage container returns through Kong', and the guard was written to cover 503 plus a "000" connection failure. The `|| echo` fallback was added for the connection-failure case but duplicates a value curl already emits, so the one input the fallback exists to handle is the one it corrupts. The check is also allowlist-inverted more broadly: any code other than 503 and 000 — 404, 401, 502 — passes. The downstream `storage.buckets` check (ci.yml:341) only proves a row exists in Postgres, which persists once written and says nothing about the container's current health.
findings.impact: Storage can be down or hung while the job asserts it is up. tests/e2e/actual-data-determination.spec.ts does still throw under CI in that case, so this is not silent today — but the assertion the workflow added specifically to stop 'green-by-omission on the exact controls 20260829510000 exists for' does not do what it says, and if that spec's own guard is ever loosened, nothing is left.
findings.recommendation: Drop the `|| echo "000"` (curl's `-w` already emits 000), and invert the check to an allowlist of expected codes (e.g. require 200/400/401) rather than a denylist of two.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: filed_snapshot is not immutable for service_role: the immutability trigger is BEFORE UPDATE only, so a filed declaration can be deleted and re-inserted with a forged snapshot under the same id
findings.boundary: service_role (BYPASSRLS + DELETE grant) -> the archived filed_snapshot. Answers the brief's explicit question 'is filed_snapshot immutable for EVERY role including service_role': for anon and authenticated, yes; for service_role, no.
findings.precondition: Possession of the service-role key, or any server-side code path that reaches the admin client (src/infrastructure/supabase/admin-client.ts) with attacker-influenced input to a declarations delete/insert. Not reachable from a browser session.
findings.affected_actor: The regulator and any future auditor of the archived record. Also the org, whose own compliance evidence stops being tamper-evident.
findings.evidence:
Sandbox, begin/rollback:

     t     | result_status |        result_declaration_id
  ---------+---------------+--------------------------------------
   T6 file | OK            | aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000040
  RESET
  SET  (role service_role)
  DELETE 1
  INSERT 0 1
       t     |     status     |                 ?column?
  -----------+----------------+------------------------------------------
   T6 result | FILED_RECORDED | {"embedded_emissions_tco2e": "0.000001"}

Contrast, same role, in-place UPDATE, correctly refused:
  set local role service_role;
  update declarations set filed_snapshot=jsonb_set(filed_snapshot,'{totals,embedded_emissions_tco2e}','"1"') where id=...;
  ERROR:  declarations: filed_snapshot, filed_reference and filed_at may only be written by public.record_declaration_filed(), in the same statement that moves status READY -> FILED_RECORDED
  CONTEXT:  PL/pgSQL function app.prevent_declaration_fact_change() line 44 at RAISE
