findings.why_controls_fail: The uniqueness constraint is correct and necessary; the RPC surfaces its violation verbatim rather than translating it into a non-oracular result.
findings.impact: Customer-list enumeration for a compliance product where the tenant roster is itself commercially sensitive, plus denial-of-registration by squatting. Each probe costs a real organisation row, so it is noisy and self-limiting — which is why LOW.
findings.recommendation: Translate the unique violation into a generic SLUG_UNAVAILABLE status without echoing the value, and consider a per-caller rate limit on organisation creation.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The persisted resolution_reason is not bound to the claimed record's code level, so an exported determination can misstate its own match specificity (prior #27)
findings.boundary: Audit-trail accuracy. No effect on the emissions figure.
findings.precondition: A member hand-writing determinations over raw PostgREST.
findings.affected_actor: An auditor reading the regulatory exports.
findings.exploit: PATCH shipment_lines.emission_determination with a valid record identity but a reason naming a different match level. The row persists and the mislabelled reason propagates to the generated column resolution_reason and into the CSV and XLSX period exports.
findings.evidence: Confirmed in the same live probe as the validator finding: a determination naming the 6-digit record '7610 90' (source_row 56) was accepted while carrying reason 'EXACT_CN8_MATCH' -> t. The validator checks only that v_reason is one of five literals and never compares it against the length or level of v_source_trade_code. The protected resolver derives the reason from the record's code_level (resolve-default-value.ts, resolutionReasonFor), so the two can only disagree in a hand-built determination.
findings.why_controls_fail: The validator treats the reason as a value to range-check rather than a claim to verify against the record it accompanies.
findings.impact: The field an auditor would use to judge how specifically a good was matched can say EXACT_CN8_MATCH for an HS4 heading. Own-tenant, raw-API only.
findings.recommendation: Derive the expected reason from the matched record's code level inside the validator and require equality — a two-line addition to the block that already resolves v_record.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: The audit document's masthead states a head SHA and push status that are both false, and §22/§20 carry unreconciled internal numbers (prior #35 + #36)
findings.boundary: Release-certification honesty.
findings.precondition: None.
findings.affected_actor: Anyone reading the document to decide whether to ship.
findings.exploit: None — structural.
findings.evidence:
docs/plans/P14_FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:3-7 states head `4aa624d` and 'Nothing has been pushed.' The prior pass measured HEAD as 0679e60, pushed, with 36 commits versus 17 at 4aa624d. Sections 18-22 each open with a 'stands as written' disclaimer; the masthead carries none and is the first thing a reader sees.

§22 A says 'Four runs ... produced six defects' while §22 G says 'Three of the seven findings were fixed in `ci.yml` itself' — six versus seven, unreconciled. §20 A states '22 unreviewed commits' against its own candidate SHA, for which the correct count is 27.

I did not re-derive these commit counts myself; the claims are checkable from git history and I am carrying the prior measurement forward as stated.
findings.why_controls_fail: The document's stated value is that 'every figure below was produced by a command run in this session.' Two figures were not re-derived when the sections carrying them were rewritten, and the masthead was never updated at all.
findings.impact: Misleads on the two facts a release reviewer checks first — which commit is being certified and whether anything left the machine. Low in itself; it matters as a signal about how much of the rest to re-derive, which for this pass turned out to be all of it.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate the masthead from git at the moment of writing, and reconcile the two counts. More usefully: have the document's figures produced by a script rather than transcribed.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: Four of six rejection-reason mappings in the release-blocker fix's application layer have no test, and a unit test cites a database-side proof in a file that does not exist (prior #38 + #40)
findings.boundary: Test coverage and traceability on the newest code in the release.
findings.precondition: None.
findings.affected_actor: Users receiving a misleading refusal message; reviewers verifying coverage claims.
findings.exploit: None.
findings.evidence:
src/application/calculations/calculate-line.ts:307-324 maps the writer's rejection through a five-branch ladder (SHIPMENT_NOT_EDITABLE, LINE_NOT_FOUND, ACTOR_NOT_A_MEMBER -> ACTOR_NO_LONGER_A_MEMBER, CAPABILITY_NOT_HELD, and a fall-through to CALCULATION_INPUTS_CHANGED covering DETERMINATION_MISMATCH / QUANTITY_MISMATCH / LINE_HAS_NO_QUANTITY). Only two non-default mockWriter outcomes are ever constructed in calculate-line.test.ts. CALCULATION_INPUTS_CHANGED and ACTOR_NO_LONGER_A_MEMBER appear in no test file anywhere in the repository.

Separately, calculate-line.test.ts:246 cites 'tests/integration/calculation-result-write-boundary.test.ts'. That file does not exist; the only repository-wide hit for the name is the comment itself. The proof does exist under a different name — the 'P14.1 -- the calculation-result write boundary' describe block inside tests/integration/calculation-reproduction.test.ts.
findings.why_controls_fail: The database-side refusals ARE well covered (calculation-reproduction.test.ts cases 5 and 6 assert DETERMINATION_MISMATCH, QUANTITY_MISMATCH, ACTOR_NOT_A_MEMBER and LINE_NOT_FOUND by name against the real RPC), so the gap is confined to the UI-messaging translation layer above them. I downgrade #38 from MEDIUM for that reason.
findings.impact: A refactor reordering or dropping a branch would tell a user to 'reload the line and calculate it again' when their membership has actually been revoked, and no test would notice. The dangling citation costs a reviewer time and, in a codebase whose review discipline is 'check the claim, not the comment', is the kind of thing that becomes a withdrawn claim two audits later.
findings.recommendation: Add one mockWriter case per branch. Fix the citation to name the describe block that actually holds the proof.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.

findings.title: anon and authenticated hold TRIGGER, REFERENCES and MAINTAIN on every table in public, and the `sequences` posture check compares names rather than values (prior #16 + #48)
findings.boundary: Latent privilege surface; and a third posture check whose `why` promises more than its SQL delivers.
findings.precondition: For the grants: an attacker or a future feature obtaining a direct connection able to SET ROLE authenticated. For the sequences check: the first bigserial/identity column added to the schema.
findings.affected_actor: Latent in both cases.
findings.exploit: Not reachable today. anon and authenticated are NOLOGIN and are only ever entered via PostgREST's SET ROLE, and PostgREST issues no DDL. The sequences check is inert because the schema currently has zero sequences (all keys are uuid).
findings.evidence:
Every table shows anon and authenticated holding REFERENCES and TRIGGER — visible in my full role_table_grants census, where every product table lists `REFERENCES,TRIGGER` alongside its DML grants. The P14.1 fix removed only TRUNCATE.

scripts/ops/compare-database-posture.mjs:224-233: the `why` reads 'a sequence restored at the wrong value collides on the next insert' but the SQL is `select sequence_schema || '.' || sequence_name from information_schema.sequences` — no last_value, no pg_sequence_last_value().
findings.why_controls_fail: The grants come from seed.sql's `grant all on all tables` plus the matching default privileges, so every reset re-establishes them and every future table inherits them; the seed's revoke tail removes only TRUNCATE. The sequences check reads as coverage it does not provide.
findings.impact: Recorded rather than actioned. If a direct connection able to SET ROLE authenticated is ever obtained (a leaked pooler credential, a debugging path, an admin tool), TRIGGER on every public table is a cross-tenant exfiltration primitive — materially larger than the TRUNCATE the same grant line carried. The sequences check matters as a pattern: it is the third check in the file whose stated purpose exceeds its SQL, which is what makes a green run hard to trust at a glance during a recovery.
findings.recommendation: `revoke trigger, references on all tables in schema public from anon, authenticated`, plus the matching default privileges — a one-line change that closes a primitive with no legitimate use through PostgREST. Add pg_sequence_last_value() to the sequences check before the first sequence exists.
findings.reviewer_note: Reported with live evidence by an attack agent; not independently re-run by the reviewing session.
